§ 2-500 QUALIFICATIONS.
   The City Solicitor shall be a member, in good standing, of the State Bar
Association. (Prior Code, § 2-500)
§ 2-501 GENERAL DUTIES.
   The City Solicitor shall be the legal advisor and attorney of this
municipality and its officers in matters relating to official duties. He or she
may prepare all ordinances of this municipality. He or she shall represent the
city in all matters and proceedings in any court in which the city is
interested. It will also be his or her duty to perform any incidental duties
the governing body or as the Mayor may require of him or her. (Prior Code, § 2-
501)
ARTICLE 6: RATE OF COMPENSATION FOR MUNICIPAL OFFICERS AND EMPLOYEES
Section
   
2-600   In general
   
2-601   Pay period
   
2-602   Overtime
§ 2-600 IN GENERAL.
   The rate of remuneration for city officials and employees shall be set, by
resolution, by City Council. Salaries of employees are confidential information
between the employee and management. (Prior Code, § 2-600)
§ 2-601 PAY PERIOD.
   All employees shall be paid bi-weekly. The two-week period ends on Sunday,
and checks received the following Wednesday. All hourly employees must sign
their time card listing hours worked, vacation, or sick, whichever applies.
(Prior Code, § 2-601)
§ 2-602 OVERTIME.
   No overtime will be allowed unless approved by the Mayor or the Council.
Hourly employees are entitled to daily overtime for pay for overtime hours at
the rate of one and one-half times their current hourly rate when actual work
hours exceed 40 hours within the designated work week of the employee. Sick
hours, holiday hours, and vacation hours shall not be counted as actual hours
worked and shall not be counted toward overtime. (Prior Code, § 2-602) (Ord.
passed 1- -2020)
ARTICLE 7: RESTRICTIONS ON MUNICIPAL OFFICERS AND EMPLOYEES
Section
   
2-700   Gifts and bribes
   
2-701   Outside employment
   
2-702   Political activity
   
2-703   Use of municipal time and property
   
2-704   Use of position or title
   
2-705   Strikes and union activity
   
2-706   Violations
§ 2-700 GIFTS AND BRIBES.
   It shall be unlawful for any municipal officer or employee to accept money,
favors, or any other form of gift from anyone, other than the municipality, for
the performance of an act or job. It shall also be unlawful for a municipal
officer or employee to accept money, favors, or any other form of gift which
could reasonably be construed as an attempt to influence the performance of his
or her municipal duties. (Prior Code, § 2-700)
§ 2-701 OUTSIDE EMPLOYMENT.
   Outside employment shall not interfere with the performance of the official
duties of the employee. (Prior Code, § 2-701)
§ 2-702 POLITICAL ACTIVITY.
   It shall be unlawful for any municipal employee to solicit campaign funds or
actively participate in any political campaign. This article shall not be
construed as to abridge a municipal officer or employee’s fundamental right to
vote or privately express his or her political views. This section shall not
apply to elected officers. (Prior Code, § 2-702)
§ 2-703 USE OF MUNICIPAL TIME AND PROPERTY.
   It shall be unlawful for any municipal officer or employee to use, or
authorize the use of, any municipal time or property for private benefit or for
the benefit of other private individuals or groups. This article shall not
apply whenever the governing body has given proper authorization for the use of
such time and property and is justly compensated for its use, at a rate
normally charged by private sources for comparable service. (Prior Code, § 2-
703)
§ 2-704 USE OF POSITION OR TITLE.
   It shall be unlawful for any municipal officer or employee to use his or her
position or title to secure unwarranted privileges or benefits for himself or
herself or others. No municipal officer or employee shall use his or her
position and title to make purchases in the name of the municipality when they
are intended for private use. (Prior Code, § 2-704)
§ 2-705 STRIKES AND UNION ACTIVITY.
   It shall be unlawful for any municipal officer or employee to participate in
any strike against the municipality. It shall also be unlawful for any
municipal officer or employee to join, be a member of, or solicit any other
municipal officer or employee to join a union which authorizes the use of
strikes against the municipality. (Prior Code, § 2-705)
§ 2-706 VIOLATIONS.
   Any municipal officer or employee who violates any section of this article
shall be subject to dismissal following a proper hearing and determination of
his or her wrong doing. He or she shall also be subject to a fine of not more
than $1,000 for each separate violation. (Prior Code, § 2-706)
Editor’s note:
   This section was revised November 16, 2015.

ARTICLE 9: COMMISSIONS
Section
   
2-900   In general
   
2-901   Commission limitations
§ 2-900 IN GENERAL.
   It will be necessary, from time to time, for municipalities to formulate
certain commissions to better oversee the development of specific areas under
the supervision of the municipality. Examples include: park commissions,
utility commission, or human relations commissions. In enacting enabling
ordinances creating such commissions, the governing body should include the
following provisions:
   (A)   Creation; composition; appointment; terms and compensation of members;
and filling vacancies.
      (1)   Appointed commissioners’ terms shall expire each June 30 at the end
of the appointed time period.
      (2)   Commissioners’ terms shall be five years unless otherwise stated.
   (B)   Purpose;
   (C)   Officers; rules; meetings; and records;
   (D)   Powers and authority generally; budget; and annual reports; and
   (E)   Duties. (Prior Code, § 2-900)
§ 2-901 COMMISSION LIMITATIONS.
   (A)   No commission or commissioners appointed by the City Council shall
have the authority to sell, trade, giveaway, transfer, or deed to another, or
in any way dispose of, any real property without first obtaining consent of the
Council.
   (B)   No commission or commissioner shall incur any form of indebtedness
without first obtaining consent of the Council. (Prior Code, § 2-901)
CHAPTER 3: ALCOHOL BEVERAGES
   Article
      
1.   GENERAL PROVISIONS
      
2.   LICENSE, FEES, PERMITS, COMPLIANCE
ARTICLE 1: GENERAL PROVISIONS
Section
   
3-11   Definitions
   
3-12   Restrictions of sale, manufacture, or consumption
   
3-13   Intoxication or drinking in public place, illegal possession
   
3-14   Private clubs
   
3-15   Restaurants
   
3-16   Hotels, motels, bed and breakfasts
§ 3-11 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this article, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   ALCOHOL. Ethyl alcohol whatever its origin, and shall include synthetic
ethyl alcohol but not denatured alcohol.
   ALCOHOLIC LIQUOR. Alcohol, beer, wine and spirits, and any liquid or solid
capable of being used as a beverage, but shall not include non-intoxicating
beer.
   AN AGENCY. A drugstore, grocery store, or general store designated by the
Commission as a retail distributor of alcoholic liquor for the State Liquor
Control Commission.
   BEER. Any beverage obtained by the fermentation of barley, malt, hops, or
any other similar product or substitute, and containing more alcohol than that
of non-intoxicating beer.
   BREWERY. An establishment where beer is manufactured or in any way prepared.
   COMMISSIONER or COMMISSION. The State Alcohol Beverage Control Commissioner.
   DEPARTMENT. The organization through which the Commission exercises powers
imposed upon it by this chapter.
   DISTILLERY. An establishment where alcoholic liquor, other than wine or
beer, is manufactured or in any way prepared.
   INTOXICATED. Having one’s faculties impaired by alcohol or other drugs to
the point where physical or mental control, or both, are markedly diminished.
   LOW-PROOF SPIRIT ALCOHOL PRODUCTS. Any alcoholic liquor beverage drink,
other than wine, beer, or nonintoxicating beer, containing one-half of 1%
(0.5%) or more of alcohol by volume, but not more than 15.5% alcohol by volume
obtained by distillation, mixed with drinkable water, fruit juices, flavoring
or coloring materials, other alcoholic or non-alcoholic beverages or other
ingredients in a solution.
   MANUFACTURE. To distill, rectify, ferment, brew, make, mix, concoct,
process, blend, bottle, or fill an original package with any alcoholic liquor.
   MANUFACTURER. Any person engaged in the manufacture of any alcoholic liquor,
and among others includes a distiller, a rectifier, a wine maker, and a brewer.
   NON-INTOXICATING BEER. Any beverage, obtained by the fermentation of barley,
malt, hops, or similar products or substitute, and containing not more alcohol
than that specified by W. Va. Code § 11-16-2.
   ORIGINAL PACKAGE. Any closed or sealed container or receptacle used for
holding alcoholic liquor.
   PERSON. An individual, firm, partnership, limited partnership, corporation,
or voluntary association.
   POWDERED ALCOHOL. An alcohol manufactured in a powder or crystalline form
for either direct use or reconstitution as an alcoholic liquor or food. For
purposes of this article, POWDERED ALCOHOL excludes any material intended for
industrial purposes
   PUBLIC PLACE. Any place, building, or conveyance to which the public has, or
is permitted to have, access, including restaurants, soda fountains, hotel
dining rooms, lobbies, and corridors of hotels, and any highway, street, lane,
park, or place of public resort or amusement; provided, that the term PUBLIC
PLACE shall not mean or include any of the above-named places, or any portion
or portions thereof, which qualify and are licensed under the provisions of
this chapter to sell alcoholic liquors for consumption on the premises;
provided, however, that the term PUBLIC PLACE shall not mean or include any
legally demarcated area designated solely for the consumption of beverages and
freshly prepared food that directly connects and adjoins any portion or
portions of a premises that qualifies and is licensed under the provisions of
this chapter to sell alcoholic liquors for consumption thereupon.
   SALE. Any transfer, exchange, or barter in any manner or by any means for a
consideration, and shall include all sales made by principal, proprietor,
agent, or employee.
   SELLING. Includes solicitation or receipt of orders; possession for sale;
and possession with intent to sell.
   SPIRITS. Any alcoholic beverage obtained by distillation and mixed with
potable water and other substances in solution, and includes brandy, rum,
whiskey, cordials, and gin.
   STATE LIQUOR STORE. A store established and operated by the Commission under
this chapter for the sale of alcoholic liquor in the original package for
consumption off the premises.
   WINE. Any alcoholic beverage obtained by the fermentation of the natural
content of fruits, or other agricultural products, containing sugar.
   WINERY. An establishment where wine is manufactured or in any way prepared.
(W. Va. Code § 60-1-5) (Prior Code, Chapter 3, § 1-1)
§ 3-12 RESTRICTIONS OF SALE, MANUFACTURE, OR CONSUMPTION.
   (A)   Alcohol, alcoholic liquors, beer, wine, non-intoxicating beer, and
spirits within the municipal boundaries of the city shall:
      (1)   Be sold only in sealed packages;
      (2)   Shall not be sold for consumption on the premises where sold. It
shall be unlawful for any person to open or consume any alcoholic beverages on
premises licensed for the sale of alcoholic beverages by the package; and
      (3)   Shall be manufactured only by persons having a state license and
under the provisions of the state.
   (B)   No sale shall be made to any person less than 21 years of age.
   (C)   Alcohol and alcoholic liquors shall not be:
      (1)   Consumed in a public place; and
      (2)   Shall not be sold to a person:
         (a)   Addicted to alcoholic beverages;
         (b)   Addicted to the use of narcotic drugs; and/or
         (c)   A person declared mentally incompetent by a court of legal
jurisdiction. (Prior Code, Chapter 3, § 1-2)
§ 3-13 INTOXICATION OR DRINKING IN PUBLIC PLACE, ILLEGAL POSSESSION.
   A person shall not:
   (A)   Appear in a public place in an intoxicated condition;
   (B)   Drink alcoholic liquor in a public place;
   (C)   Drink alcoholic liquor in a motor vehicle on any highway, street,
alley, or in a public garage;
   (D)   Give a drink of alcoholic liquor to another person in a public place;
or
   (E)   Possess any alcoholic liquor which is in violation of a part of this
chapter. (Prior Code, Chapter 3, § 1-3)
§ 3-14 PRIVATE CLUBS.
   (A)   Definitions. For the purpose of this section, the following
definitions shall apply unless the context clearly indicates or requires a
different meaning.
      APPLICANT. A private club applying for a license under the provisions of
this article.
      CODE. The official code of the state, as amended.
      COMMISSIONER. The State Alcohol Beverage Control Commissioner.
      LICENSEE. The holder of a license to operate a private club granted under
the provisions of this chapter, which license shall remain unexpired,
unsuspended, and unrevoked.
      PRIVATE CLUB. Any corporation or unincorporated association which either:
         (a)   Belongs to or is affiliated with a nationally recognized
fraternal or veterans organization, which is operated exclusively for the
benefit of its members, which pays no part of its income to its shareholders or
individual members, which owns or leases a building or other premises, to which
club are admitted only duly elected or approved dues-paying members in good
standing of such corporation or association, and their guests while in the
company of a member, and to which club the general public is not admitted, and
which club maintains in said building or on said premises a suitable kitchen
and dining facility with related equipment for serving food to members and
their guests;
         (b)   Is a non-profit social club, which is operated exclusively for
the benefit of its members, which pays no part of its income to its
shareholders or individual members, which owns or leases a building or other
premises to which club are admitted only duly elected or approved dues-paying
members in good standing of such corporation or association, and their guests
while in the company of a member, and to which club the general public is not
admitted, and which club maintains in said building or on said premises a
suitable kitchen and dining facility with related equipment for serving food to
members and their guests;
         (c)   Is organized and operated for legitimate purposes, which has at
least 100 duly elected or approved dues-paying members in good standing, which
owns or leases a building or other premises, including any vessel licensed or
approved by any federal agency to carry or accommodate passengers on navigable
waters of this state, to which club are admitted only duly elected or approved
dues-paying members in good standing of such corporation or association, and
their guests while in the company of a member, and to which club the general
public is not admitted, and which club maintains in said building or on said
premises a suitable kitchen and dining facility with related equipment, and
employs a sufficient number of persons for serving meals to members and their
guests; or
         (d)   Is organized for legitimate purposes and owns or leases a
building or other limited premises in any state, county, or municipal park, or
at any airport in which building or premises a club has been established, to
which club are admitted only duly elected and approved dues-paying members in
good standing and their guests, while in the company of a member, and to which
club the general public is not admitted, and which maintains in connection with
said club a suitable kitchen and dining facility and related equipment, and
employs a sufficient number of persons for serving meals in said club to said
members and their guests.
   (B) Sale of alcohol. Notwithstanding any other provisions of this code to
the contrary, licensees are hereby authorized to sell alcoholic liquors by the
drink, other than in sealed packages, but does not include bottle or original
container sales of alcoholic liquors to patrons, for consumption on the
premises of the licensees, to their members and their guests in accordance with
the provisions of this article, rules of the Commissioner, and as authorized
under W. Va. Code § 60-6-8. The licensees may keep and maintain on their
premises a supply of those lawfully acquired alcoholic liquors in such
quantities as may be appropriate for the conduct of operations thereof.(W. Va.
Code § 60-7-3) (Prior Code, Chapter 3, § 1-4)
§ 3-15 RESTAURANTS.
   (A)   Definition. For the purpose of this section, the following definitions
shall apply unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different
meaning.
      RESTAURANT.
         (a)   A place where meals are prepared on the premises and are
regularly served to the public for adequate pay each day the establishment is
open for business;
         (b)   Contain one or more public dining rooms, with adequate and
sanitary kitchen facilities and staff to prepare, cook, and serve suitable food
for its guests;
         (c)   Have staff available to serve meals prepared on the premises
during any time the establishment is open for business;
         (d)   Have a valid County Health Department food service permit and
any other applicable local, state, or federal permits, licenses, and the like,
required for food service establishments;
         (e)   Have at least 50% of its total sales comprised of the sale of
food prepared on the premises and non-alcoholic beverages consumed on the
premises; and for this purpose, if a RESTAURANT makes a minimum charge, cover
charge, or admission charge, or any other non-food or non-alcoholic beverage
charge, the amount so charged shall not be counted in computing total sales,
and shall not be counted as a food or beverage sale;
         (f)   Have a permanent seating capacity, at tables and chairs, not
counting bar stools, of at least 35 persons;
         (g)   The RESTAURANT must have written menus readily available to
patrons. A majority of the food listed in the menu shall be available for
consumption while the business is open;
         (h)   Have adequate sanitary facilities and separate restrooms for men
and women;
         (i)   Shall have approved fire exits, current and adequate fire
extinguishers for the premises, and meet all current fire and building codes in
effect for the municipality; and
         (j)   The restaurant must have more than 850 square feet of service
area, which shall notinclude any space at counters, bars, or lounges, or a
combination of a full-service operating kitchen arealarger than 500 square feet
with a service area of no less than 700 square feet.
   (B)   Eligibility for license. A license may be granted to a restaurant, as
defined under division (A) above, and divisions (C) and (D) below,
notwithstanding any other provisions of this code to the contrary, a license to
sell alcoholic liquors, other than in sealed packages, for consumption on the
premises of the licensees to guests in accordance with the provisions of this
article.
   (C) Private club restaurant, video lottery private club restaurant.
      (1)   PRIVATE CLUB RESTAURANT means an applicant for a private club or
licensed private club licensee that has a primary function of using the
licensed premises as a restaurant for serving freshly prepared meals and dining
in the restaurant area. The private club restaurant may have a bar area
separate from or commingled within the restaurant where seating requirements
for members and guests are met by including the restaurant area.
         (a)   Equipment in the kitchen shall be capable of preparing a freshly
cooked meal on the licensed premises. In addition, licensees shall have at
least enough food to serve one-fourth the number of seats in the private club
at any one time.
         (b)   A suitable kitchen shall contain equipment as follows:
            1.    One range with oven and no fewer than two burners, or a
microwave oven which has a variable control and a separate range with two
burners;
            2.   One sink with hot and cold running water;
            3.   One cold storage unit or refrigerator at least 17 cubic feet
in size
            4.   One sink with hot and cold running water;
            5.   One cold storage unit or refrigerator at least 17 cubic feet
in size; and
            6.   Cooking utensils and pots and pans sufficient for preparation
of the required meals.
         (c)   A suitable dining facility shall include the following: Plates
(other than of paper or similar construction), metal knives, forks, and spoons,
and drinking glasses and cups, in sufficient quantities to serve no fewer meals
than one-fourth the number of seats in the club. A meal may consist of one item
or any combination of items. For example, fresh, canned, and packaged chili,
soup, spaghetti, fresh salad, fresh or prepackaged sandwiches, freshly prepared
meats, and vegetables are acceptable. Items which, by themselves, do not
qualify as adequate are packaged potato chips and similar products; packaged
crackers; packaged nuts; packaged desserts (fruit pies, cakes, cookies, and the
like); and bar sausages and similar products. The key word in the definition of
meals is preparation. Meals shall be available from opening of the club until
closing. Limited menus will be acceptable after 10:00 p.m.(W. Va. Code Ch. 60
and 175 C.S.R. § 2)
      (2)   If video lottery is provided, video lottery terminals shall be
located in a separate room suitable for the location of video lottery terminals
with adult-only restricted access, the interior of which is not visible to
persons outside the room. Individuals under 21 years of age shall not be
admitted.(W. Va. Code § 29-22B-328(a)(1))
   (D)   Private club bar, video lottery private club bar. PRIVATE CLUB BAR
means an applicant for a private club or licensed private club licensee that
has a primary function for the use of the licensed premises as a bar for the
sale and consumption of alcoholic liquors and non-intoxicating beer or non-
intoxicating craft beer and wine when licensed for those sales, while providing
a limited food menu for members and guests, and meeting the criteria set forth
in this division (D) which:
      (1)   Operates a bar with a kitchen, including at least:
         (a)   A two-burner hot plate, air fryer, or microwave oven;
         (b)   A sink with hot and cold running water;
         (c)   A 17-cubic-foot refrigerator or freezer, or some combination of
a refrigerator and freezer which is not used for alcohol cold storage; and
         (d)   Kitchen utensils and other food consumption apparatus as
determined by the Commissioner.
      (2)   Food fit for human consumption available to be served during all
hours of operation on the licensed premises; and
      (3)   Maintains, at any one time, a food inventory capable of being
prepared in the private club bar’s kitchen. In calculating the food inventory,
the Commissioner shall include television dinners, bags of chips, or similar
products, microwavable food or meals, frozen meals, prepackaged foods, or
canned prepared foods.(W. Va. Code § 60 and 175 C.S.R. § 2)
   (E)   Adult-only access. If video lottery is provided, video lottery
terminals shall be located in a separate room suitable for the location of
video lottery terminals with adult-only restricted access, the interior of
which is not visible to persons outside the room. Individuals under 21 years of
age shall not be admitted.(W. Va. Code § 29-22)
§ 3-16 HOTELS, MOTELS, BED AND BREAKFASTS.
   [Reserved]   (Prior Code, Chapter 3, § 1-6)

§ 3-21 MUNICIPAL LICENSE TAX.
   Any municipality in this state is hereby authorized to levy a fee for
revenue purposes only upon any licensee whose premises are situate within such
municipality, which fee shall not exceed one-half the amount of the license fee
levied by this state under the provisions of §
3-26 of this article. Any such municipality is hereby authorized and empowered
to enact and adopt ordinances necessary for the collection and enforcement of
such fee.(W. Va. Code § 60-7-7) (Prior Code, Chapter 3, § 2-1)
§ 3-22 LICENSE NOT TRANSFERABLE; CHANGE OF LOCATION.
   No license issued under the provisions of this article shall be transferred
to another person, nor shall the location of the premises to which the license
relates be changed without the written consent of the Council, which consent
may be given or refused, in its discretion.(W. Va. Code §§ 11-16-7, 60-4-23,
60-4-22) (Prior Code, Chapter 3, § 2-2)
§ 3-23 EXCESSIVE NOISE AND DISTURBING THE QUIETUDE OF THE COMMUNITY.
   A licensee of a consumption on the premises establishment shall at all times
control the volume of music or other sounds originating within or from
adjoining parking, or other areas under the control of the licensee. A volume
in excess of a normal conversational tone at the public roadway on which the
licensed premises abuts shall be a violation of this section. (Prior Code,
Chapter 3, § 2-3)
§ 3-24 GRANDFATHERED.
   (A)   A tavern, club, or place of business at the adoption of this chapter
that was licensed and permitted to serve consumption on the premises where sold
shall be grandfathered.
   (B)   A grandfathered tavern shall not be required to comply with §
3-12(A) and (B), provided:
      (1)   The place of business shall remain under the ownership and license
of the present owner at the time of the adoption of this chapter. Any sale,
transfer, or change of ownership or proprietorship shall void the grandfather
clause;
      (2)   The place of business shall maintain a valid and continuous state
and municipal license (permit);
      (3)   The place of business shall have not been convicted of any state or
municipal violations or laws;
      (4)   The place of business shall maintain its location in accordance
with the municipal ordinances;
      (5)   The grandfather clause shall not exclude compliance with any other
municipal ordinance; and
      (6)   A license under this provision may be revoked for just cause by
vote of the governing body. (Prior Code, Chapter 3, § 2-4)
§ 3-25 LICENSE FEES IMPOSED.
   (A)   The city has the right to impose upon any private club that fall
within the city limits the following license fees:
      (1)   Fraternal or veteran organizations, or non-profit social clubs:
$375; and
      (2)   Private clubs, other than what is listed in division (A)(1) above:
      (1)   Less than 1,000 members: $500; and
      (2)   More than 1,000 members: $1,250.
   (B)   The fee for any such license issued following the first day of January
of any year and to expire on June 30 of such year shall be one-half the annual
fees noted in divisions (A)(1) and (A)(2) above. (Prior Code, Chapter 3, § 2-5)
§ 3-26 DUTIES OF STATE LICENSE HOLDERS TO REPORT TO THE CLERK TO SHOW LICENSE
AND TO PAY CITY LICENSE.
   All licensees shall report annually to the City Recorder to show their state
license and to pay city license fees. These licenses of both the city and the
state shall be displayed in plain view at the place of business, with an annual
year ranging from July 1 to June 30. (Prior Code, Chapter 3, § 2-7)
§ 3-27 REVOCATION OF LICENSE.
   The City Recorder shall automatically void all city licenses in place where
the state license has also been voided. All licenses holders have a duty to
report any state license that is voided to the City Recorder. (Prior Code,
Chapter 3, § 2-8)
§ 3-28 DISTRIBUTOR OR RETAILER OF WINES.
   (A)   (1)   No person shall engage in business in the capacity of
distributor or retailer of wines within the city without first obtaining a
license from said city.
      (2)   The city shall collect an annual fee for licenses issued under this
article as follows:
         (a)   Twenty-five hundred dollars per year, or faction thereof, for a
distributor’s license; and
         (b)   One hundred fifty dollars per year, or fraction thereof, for a
retailer’s license
   (B)   The license period shall begin on July 1 of each year and end on June
30 of the following year, and if the initial license is granted for less than a
year, the fee shall be computed in proportion to the number of quarters are
remaining in the fiscal year, including the quarter in which application is
made.
   (C)   The enforcement of this division (C) shall be consistent with and
subject to the provisions of W. Va. Code §§ 60-8-1 et seq., as amended. (Prior
Code, Chapter 3, § 2-9)
§ 3-29 TAX ON RETAIL PURCHASES OF INTOXICATING LIQUORS.
   Pursuant to W. Va. Code § 8-13-7, as amended, there is hereby imposed a tax
of 5% of the retail purchase prices of any and all intoxicating liquors
purchased from the Alcohol Beverage Control Commission, or from any person
licensed to sell wine at retail to the public under the provisions of W. Va.
Code § 60-8, within the corporate boundaries of the municipality. Such tax
shall be levied upon the purchaser of said intoxicating liquor or wine, and
shall be added to any collected with the retail purchase price of such
intoxicating liquor or wine. Such tax shall be received by the municipality
from the State Treasury pursuant to the rules and regulations adopted by the
said Alcohol Beverage Control Commissioner. Provided, however, that such tax
shall not be collected on intoxicating liquors, other than wine sold by or
purchased from holders of a license issued under the provision of W. Va. Code §
60-7. Provided further, such tax shall be collected upon all sales of wine to
holders of a license issued under the provisions of W. Va. Code § 60-7 from a
wine distributor licensed pursuant to the provisions of W. Va. Code §§ 60-3 et
seq. (Prior Code, Chapter 3, § 2-10) (Ord. passed 8-1-1983)

§ 4-1 REGULATING AND IMPOUNDING OF ANIMALS.
   The city shall have the power to regulate or prohibit the keeping of animals
or fowls, and to provide for the impounding, sale, or destruction of animals or
fowls kept contrary to the laws of this city, or running loose not under
control of the owner. (Prior Code, § 4-1)
§ 4-2 ANIMAL TAX; PERMIT FEE.
   This city shall have the power and authority to levy and collect an annual
license tax or permit fee upon the privilege of keeping any domestic or other
animal within the corporate limits of the city. (Prior Code, § 4-2)
§ 4-3 UNLAWFUL QUARTERING OF ANIMALS.
   It shall be unlawful for anyone to quarter any livestock or keep any fowl in
an area of less than ten acres, or to keep wild or exotic animals inside the
city limits. (Prior Code, § 4-3)
Editor’s note:
   This section was revised by the city on November 16, 2015.
§ 4-4 FORCIBLE RETAKING OF IMPOUNDED STOCK: PENALTY.
   Anyone who forcefully shall take possession of any animal impounded by the
city under this chapter without paying all fees shall be guilty of a
misdemeanor. (Prior Code, § 4-4)
§ 4-5 CRUELTY TO ANIMALS.
   (A)   (1)   It is unlawful for any person to intentionally, knowingly, or
recklessly,
         (a)   Mistreat an animal in cruel manner;
         (b)   Abandon an animal;
         (c)   Withhold:
            1.   Proper sustenance, including food or water;
            2.   Shelter that protects from the elements of weather; or
            3.   Medical treatment necessary to sustain normal health and
fitness or to end the suffering of any animal.
         (d)   Abandon an animal to die;
         (e)   Leave an animal unattended and confined in a motor vehicle when
physical injury to or death of the animal is likely to result;
         (f)   Ride an animal when it is physically unfit;
         (g)   Bait or harass an animal for the purpose of making it perform
for a person’s amusement;
         (h)   Cruelly chain or tether an animal; or
         (i)   Use, train, or possess a domesticated animal for the purpose of
seizing, detaining, or maltreating any other domesticated animal.
      (2)   Any person in violation of division (A)(1) above is guilty of a
misdemeanor and, upon conviction thereof, shall be fined not less than $300 nor
more than $2,000 or confined in jail not more than six months, or both.
   (B)   A person who intentionally tortures, mutilates, or maliciously kills
an animal, or causes, procures, or authorizes any other person to torture,
mutilate, or maliciously kill an animal, is guilty of a felony and, upon
conviction thereof, shall be confined in a correctional facility not less than
one nor more than five years and be fined not less than $1,000 nor more than
$5,000. As it relates to this section, TORTURE means an action taken for the
primary purpose of inflicting pain.
   (C)   A person, other than a licensed veterinarian or a person acting under
the direction or with the approval of a licensed veterinarian, who knowingly
and willfully administers or causes to be administered to any animal
participating in any contest any controlled substance or any other drug for the
purpose of altering or otherwise affecting said animal’s performance is guilty
of a misdemeanor and, upon conviction thereof, shall be fined not less than
$500 nor more than $2,000.
   (D)   Any person convicted of a violation of division (A) above forfeits his
or her interest in any animal and all interest in the animal vests in the
humane society or county pound of the county in which the conviction was
rendered and the person is, in addition to any fine imposed, liable for any
costs incurred or to be incurred by the humane society or county pound as a
result.
   (E)   For the purpose of this section, the term CONTROLLED SUBSTANCE has the
same meaning ascribed to it by W. Va. Code § 1-61-101(d).
   (F)   The provisions of this section do not apply to lawful acts of hunting,
fishing, trapping, or animal training or farm livestock, poultry, gaming fowl,
or wildlife kept in private or licensed game farms if kept and maintained
according to usual and accepted standards of livestock, poultry, gaming fowl,
or wildlife or game farm production and management, nor to humane use of
animals or activities regulated under and in conformity with the provisions of
7 U.S.C. §§ 2131 et seq., and the regulations promulgated thereunder, as both
statutes and regulations are in effect on the effective date of this section.
   (G)   Notwithstanding the provisions of division (A) above, any person
convicted of a second or subsequent violation of division (A) above is guilty
of a misdemeanor and shall be confined in jail for a period of not less than 90
days nor more than one year, fined not less than $500 nor more than $3,000, or
both. The incarceration set forth in this division (G) is mandatory unless the
provisions of division (H) below are complied with.
   (H)   (1)   Notwithstanding any provision of this code to the contrary, no
person who has been convicted of a violation of the provisions of division (A)
or (B) above may be granted probation until the defendant has undergone a
complete psychiatric or psychological evaluation and the court has reviewed the
evaluation. Unless the defendant is determined by the court to be indigent, he
or she is responsible for the cost of the evaluation.
      (2)   For any person convicted of a violation of division (A) or (B)
above, the court may, in addition to the penalties provided in this section,
impose a requirement that he or she complete a program of anger management
intervention for perpetrators of animal cruelty. Unless the defendant is
determined by the court to be indigent, he or she is responsible for the cost
of the program.
   (I)   In addition to any other penalty which can be imposed for a violation
of this section, a court shall prohibit any person so convicted from
possessing, owning, or residing with any animal or type of animal for a period
of five years following entry of a misdemeanor conviction and 15 years
following entry of a felony conviction. A violation under this section is a
misdemeanor punishable by a fine not exceeding $2,000 and forfeiture of the
animal.(W. Va. Code § 61-8-19)
§ 4-6 HUNTING PROHIBITED.
   (A)   No person shall hunt, kill, or attempt to kill any animal or fowl by
the use of firearms, bow and arrow, air rifle, or any other means within the
corporate limits of the municipality, provided:
      (1)   Unless specifically provided for by ordinance and a special hunting
permit approved and provided for by City Council; and/or
      (2)   Unless on property consisting of 25 acres or more.
   (B)   In addition to any other prohibitions which may exist by law, it shall
be unlawful for any person to shoot or discharge any firearms:
      (1)   Across or in any public road in this municipality, at any time;
      (2)   Within 500 feet of any school or church; or
      (3)   Within 500 feet of any dwelling house.
   (C)   Any person violating this section is guilty of a misdemeanor and, upon
conviction thereof, shall be fined not less than $50 nor more than $500. (Prior
Code, § 4-6)
Editor’s note:
   This section was revised by the city on November 16, 2015.
§ 4-7 NUISANCE CONDITIONS PROHIBITED.
   No person shall keep or harbor any animal or fowl in the city so as to
create noxious or offensive odors or unsanitary conditions which are a menace
to the health, comfort, or safety of the public. (Prior Code, § 4-7)
§ 4-8 ANIMALS RUNNING AT LARGE.
   No person, being the owner or having charge of cattle, horses, swine, sheep,
geese, ducks, goats, turkeys, chickens, or other fowl or animals, shall permit
them to run at large upon any public place, or upon any unenclosed lands or
upon the premises of another. (Prior Code, § 4-8)
§ 4-9 POISONING ANIMALS.
   (A)   It shall be unlawful for any person to poison, or attempt to poison,
any animal or fowl of another person, or maliciously maim, kill, or cause the
death of any animal or fowl of another person.
   (B)   No poisoned meat or any poisonous substance shall be cast into any of
the streets, public places, or lots or buildings in the city for the purpose of
destroying dogs or other animals. (Prior Code, § 4-9)
§ 4-10 CITY IS BIRD SANCTUARY.
   (A)   The entire area embraced within the boundaries of the city is hereby
designated as a bird sanctuary.
   (B)   It shall be unlawful to trap, hunt, shoot or attempt to shoot, or
molest in any manner, any bird or wild fowl, or rob bird nests or wild fowl
nests; provided, however, if starlings, pigeons, or similar birds are found to
be congregating in such numbers in a particular locality that they constitute a
nuisance or menace to health or property, and in the opinion of Council no
satisfactory alternative is found to abate such nuisance, then in such event
the Mayor shall then destroy such birds in such numbers and in such manner as
is deemed advisable by the Mayor under the supervision of the Chief of Police.
(Prior Code, § 4-10)
§ 4-11 CONTROL OF RABIES AND OTHER DISEASES.
   (A)   Each owner or person in charge of any dog, whether licensed or
unlicensed, or in charge of any other animal known to have or suspected of
having rabies or any other communicable disease, or known to have been bitten
by another animal having or suspected of having any such disease, shall
forthwith take such animal to a veterinarian for confinement and observation,
or securely confine such animal on his or her own premises, and, in either
case, notify the Mayor without delay, and he or she shall then obey the
directives given him or her by the Mayor. Animals so confined shall be
destroyed in a humane manner upon the finding of a veterinarian that they have
rabies or some other incurable communicable disease, and no animal shall be
released from such confinement until found by a veterinarian to be free of
rabies and other communicable disease.
   (B)   Rabid animals found at large within the city shall be destroyed
forthwith by the Humane Officer or by any police officer.
   (C)   Any person having knowledge of an animal known to have or suspected of
having rabies or any other communicable disease, shall forthwith notify the
Humane Officer and the Chief of Police, Mayor or City Recorder. If the owner or
person in charge of such animal can be found without undue delay, he or she
shall be notified by the Humane Officer, Chief of Police, Mayor, or City
Recorder to comply with the provisions of division (A) above forthwith;
otherwise, such animal shall be destroyed in a humane manner. (Prior Code, § 4-
11)
§ 4-12 ANIMAL WASTE.
   (A)   No person, neither the owner of an animal or pet, or any person having
charge of an animal or pet, shall allow any such animal to deposit animal
excrement or other animal waste, or they shall promptly remove and sanitarily
dispose of animal waste left on public or private property. The owner or
handler of any animal shall be responsible for the removal of any animal waste
deposited on public walks, recreation areas, public streets, or private
property other than the premises of the owner of the animal.
   (B)   Excessive accumulation of animal waste on a pet owner’s property
creates unsanitary conditions that are offensive to neighbors and unsafe for
people and pets. A person commits an offense if the person deposits, causes to
be deposited, or permits to accumulate any dry or wet solid waste upon any
public or private premises within the city in such a manner as to emit noxious
or offensive odors, or to become unsanitary or injurious to public health or
safety.
   (C)   Whoever violates any provision of this section shall be fined not less
than $100 nor more than $500 for each offense. Each day a section of this
section is violated shall constitute a separate offense. (Prior Code, § 4-12)
§ 4-13 HABITUAL ANIMAL NOISE.
   (A)   It shall be unlawful for any person to keep or harbor a dog, cat,
bird, or other animal which causes a noise disturbance by habitually howling,
barking, meowing, squawking, crying, or other noise making.
   (B)   HABITUAL HOWLING, BARKING, MEOWING, SQUAWKING, CRYING, or OTHER NOISE
MAKING shall be defined as repeated intervals of at least five minutes with
less than one minute of interruption. The noise must be audible off of the
owner’s or caretaker’s premises. (Prior Code, § 4-13)
§ 4-14 DUTY TO MAINTAIN PLACES WHERE PERMITTED ANIMALS ARE KEPT IN A SANITARY
CONDITION, AND THE LIKE.
   It shall be the duty of each owner or occupant of premises within the city
whereon any dog, cat, or other permitted animal which may lawfully be harbored
or maintained within the city to maintain the pen or other enclosure or place
where such animal is kept in a healthful and sanitary condition at all times,
free of offensive substances and liquids, at such place and in such manner as
not to constitute a hazard to the health or safety of any person, or an
annoyance to persons in the neighborhood thereof.
   (A)   No person owning or having custody of any animal shall permit any such
animal to defecate (soil) upon any school ground, public street, alley,
sidewalk, tree bank, park, or any other public grounds or any private property
within the municipality, other than the premises of the owner or person having
custody of the animal, unless said defecation (soiling) is removed immediately
and disposed of in an appropriate manner and container.
   (B)   Any person, upon conviction for failing to comply with this section,
shall pay a fine of $50 for the first offense and fine of $100 for each
additional offense. (Prior Code, § 4-14)
Editor’s note:
   This section was revised by the city on November 16, 2015.
§ 4-15 DELEGATION.
   Wherever, in the foregoing sections, that duties in supervision, licensure,
enforcement, and the like are assigned to a named official such as the Mayor,
Humane Officer, or the City Recorder, those duties are delegable for either
partial or complete accomplishment to the Chief of Police, his or her officers
and staff, and to any other city employees whose aid in their enforcement the
Mayor or City Recorder may deem advisable. (Prior Code, § 4-15)
§ 4-16 DEAD ANIMALS AND FOWL; DISPOSITION OF CARCASSES.
   (A)   It shall be unlawful for any person to deposit in any of the streets,
parks, public squares, or places, or upon any private lot or parcel of ground,
the carcass, or part of any carcass, of any animal, fowl, or bird within the
limits of the city, or at any point within one mile of the city limits if such
place outside the limits is so located that such carcass shall become offensive
to, or detrimental to, the health of the inhabitants of the neighborhood.
   (B)   It shall be unlawful to bury within the city or within one mile of the
city the carcass, or part of a carcass, of any animal, fowl, or bird which has
died or been killed within the city, or that has been brought into the city;
but all such carcasses shall immediately after death be disposed of in a lawful
and sanitary manner.
   (C)   However, residents shall be allowed to bury pets on their private
property in a sanitary manner. (Prior Code, § 4-16)
§ 4-17 RESPONSIBILITY FOR REMOVAL OF CARCASSES.
   (A)   (1)   When any dead animal, fowl, or bird is found in the streets,
public places, or private lots in the city, upon notice to the owner, such
owner shall remove the carcass and dispose of it in a lawful and sanitary
manner; failure to do so shall be a violation of this code.
      (2)   If the owner refuses or fails to do so within a reasonable time not
to excess 24 hours after such notice, the city may send a proper vehicle to
obtain such carcass and have it removed and disposed of, and render a bill for
such removal and disposal to the owner, if known, and shall place a duplicate
of such bill in the hands of the city collector for collection.
      (3)   The city collector shall have power to collect such amount in
accordance with state law and city code.
   (B)   When any animal, fowl, or bird shall be killed upon any of the streets
or public places within the city by any automobile, or other vehicle, being
driven over or upon the streets within the city, or by the horse or other
animal attached to any vehicle, it shall be the duty of the owner, driver, or
other person having such vehicle in his or her charge to at once remove such
carcass to the curbline, or if possible to some point out of the public view,
and to cover the carcass from view, and immediately thereafter remove, or cause
it to be removed, and lawfully disposed of in a sanitary manner. It shall be
violation for any person to refuse or neglect to carry out the provisions of
this division (B). (Prior Code, § 4-17)
§ 4-18 ADMINISTRATION AND ENFORCEMENT OF CHAPTER.
   (A)   The Mayor may appoint a Humane Officer or Officers with the
cooperation of the police to administer and enforce the provisions of this
chapter.
   (B)   The Chief of Police shall also be given the powers of the City Humane
Officer.
   (C)   The Mayor may combine together and form agreements with other
municipalities or county officials to assign duties as Humane Officer and
operate an animal shelter.
   (D)   The Mayor, with approval of the Council, may at his or her discretion,
empower Humane (Animal) Officers to issue citations for violations of this
chapter. (Prior Code, § 4-18)
§ 4-19 SEARCH WARRANTS.
   If a complaint is filed with the Municipal Court and the complaint proves
valid proof or cause, a search warrant may be issued, and if in such search and
of the provisions of this chapter are found to be apparent, all animals shall
be taken, and also all persons dealing in or apart of such cruelty. All animals
shall be taken to the Humane Society and also all persons shall be taken for
arraignment before the Municipal Judge or County Magistrate. (Prior Code, § 4-
19)
§ 4-20 NO NEED FOR SEARCH WARRANT.
   Any authorized officer may enter, without a warrant, any building in which
the pitting of animals against each other is taking place, and possess all
animals and persons taking part in the fighting of these animals. (Prior Code,
§ 4-20)
§ 4-21 PENALTY.
   Any person convicted of violating the provisions of this chapter, unless
otherwise provided for, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor, and if no specific
penalty is provided for, the violation thereof shall be a fine not exceeding
$1,000. Each day any such violation continues shall constitute a separate
offense. (Prior Code, § 4-21)
Editor’s note:
   This section was revised by the city on November 16, 2015.
§ 4-22 ANIMALS ON CITY PROPERTY.
   (A)   No person, being the owner or having charge of any animal, except
“seeing eye dogs,” shall fail to prevent such animal from going upon city
property when posted.
   (B)   Pets of any kind are prohibited on the grounds of the Pennsboro Miles
Stadium and Pennsboro Sullivan Gym.
   (C)   Nothing in this article shall be deemed to prevent or restrict the use
of trained K-9 units by law enforcement personnel.
   (D)   Nothing in this article shall be deemed to prevent or restrict the use
of officially certified service animals, as defined by the Department of
Justice published revised final regulations implementing the Americans with
Disabilities Act of 1990, being 42 U.S.C. §§ 12101 et seq. (ADA) for Title II
(state and local government services, being 42 U.S.C. §§ 12131 through 12165)
and Title III (public accommodations and commercial facilities, being 42 U.S.C.
§§ 12181 through 12189). Provided:
      (1)   Only dogs are recognized as service animals under Titles II and III
of the ADA, and a SERVICE ANIMAL is a dog that is individually trained to do
work or perform tasks for a person with a disability. The task(s) performed by
the dog must be directly related to the person’s disability;
      (2)   Dogs whose sole function is to provide emotional support, therapy,
comfort, or companion animals do not qualify as service animals under the ADA;
      (3)   Service dogs must be trained, qualified, and certified by an
authorized agency and registered with and approved by the city as an official
authorized service dog prior to being taken on city property;
      (4)   A service animal must be under the control of its handler. Under
the ADA, service animals must be harnessed, leashed, or tethered, unless the
individual’s disability prevents using these devices or these devices interfere
with the service animal’s safe, effective performance of tasks. In that case,
the individual must maintain control of the animal through voice, signal, or
other effective controls;
      (5)   A person with a disability can be asked to remove his or her
service animal from the premises if:
         (a)   The dog is out of control and the handler does not take
effective action to control it; or
         (b)   The dog is not housebroken.
      (6)   SERVICE ANIMALS are defined as dogs that are individually trained
to do work or perform tasks for people with disabilities. Examples of such work
or tasks include guiding people who are blind, alerting people who are deaf,
pulling a wheelchair, alerting and protecting a person who is having a seizure,
reminding a person with mental illness to take prescribed medications, calming
a person with post traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) during an anxiety attack,
or performing other duties. Service animals are working animals, not pets. The
work or task a dog has been trained to provide must be directly related to the
person’s disability.
   (E)   (1)   No person, neither the owner of an animal or pet, or any person
having charge of an animal or pet, shall allow any such animal to deposit
animal excrement or other animal waste, or they shall promptly remove and
sanitarily dispose of animal waste left on public or private property as
provided in §
4-12.
      (2)   Whoever violates any provision of this article shall be fined not
less than $100 nor more than $250 for each offense. Each day shall constitute a
separate offense. (Prior Code, § 4-22)
ARTICLE 1: LIVESTOCK AND FOWL
Section
   
4-100   Keeping farm animals
   
4-101   Swine or hogs

§ 4-100 KEEPING FARM ANIMALS.
   (A)   It shall be unlawful for anyone to quarter any livestock or fowl on an
area of less than ten acres without the consent of the City Council and a
permit issued by the City Recorder.
   (B)   No person shall keep any kind of livestock, poultry, fowl, or pigeon
within 150 feet of any structure owned by another and used for human
habitation, occupation, or assembly, whether the structure is in the same or
adjacent block or square; nor shall any livestock, fowl, poultry, or pigeon be
permitted by the owner thereof to run, fly, stray, or otherwise be at large in
any streets of the city or in any lot or premises not in the possession or
under the control of the owner of such livestock, poultry, fowl, or pigeon.
   (C)   No person shall keep, or permit to be kept, within the corporate
limits any goat, cow, chicken, or other animal or fowl in a pen, or otherwise
confined in any lot, to the annoyance, detriment, or inconvenience of any
neighbor or the public.
   (D)   No person, firm, or corporation shall erect or maintain any cattle or
horse barn, or other structure wherein animals are kept, within 200 feet of any
permanently improved, open and used street or avenue within the city, or within
200 feet of any structure owned by another or used for human habitation,
occupation, or assembly, whether the structure is in the same or adjacent block
or square.
   (E)   Each stable, pen, coop, and other enclosure or place where any animal
or fowl is kept shall be so located and of such construction as to have
sufficient sanitary drainage to keep it dry at all times; and it shall be the
duty of each person owning, harboring, or keeping any animal or fowl to
maintain each enclosure or other place where such animal or fowl is kept in a
clean and sanitary condition at all times, free of any unwholesome or offensive
substance, liquid, or odor and so as not to constitute a nuisance. (Prior Code,
§ 4-100)
Editor’s note:
   This section was revised by the city on November 16, 2015.
§ 4-101 SWINE OR HOGS.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to keep or permit to be kept any swine
or hog within the corporate limits. (Prior Code, § 4-101)
§ 4-102 SALE OF BABY FOWL.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to sell or offer for sale as pets or
novelties any artificially colored, sprayed, painted, or dyed baby chicks,
ducklings, goslings, turkeys, or other fowl. (Prior Code, § 4-102)
§ 4-103 ROOSTERS.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to keep or permit to be kept any
roosters within the corporate limits. (Prior Code, § 4-103)
ARTICLE 2: DOGS

§ 4-200 DEFINITION.
   For the purpose of this article, the following definition shall apply unless
the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   DOG. Includes all members of the canine family, of either sex or at least
six months of age, unless otherwise specified hereinafter. (Prior Code, § 4-
200)
§ 4-201 CRUELTY TO DOGS.
   (A)   No person shall cruelly or needlessly beat, torture, torment,
mutilate, kill, or willfully deprive necessary sustenance to any dog,
irrespective of whether any such dog is his or her own or that of another
person. No person shall impound or confine any dog in any place unprotected
from the elements or fail to supply the same with a sufficient quantity of food
and water, or abandon to die any maimed, sick, or diseased dog, or be engaged
in or employed at dog fighting, or pitting one dog to fight against another dog
or any similar cruelty to any dog, or receive money for the admission of any
person, or use, train, or possess a dog for the purpose of seizing, detaining,
or maltreating any other dog.
   (B)   Any person convicted of violating the provisions of this section shall
be guilty of a misdemeanor, and the violation thereof shall be a fine not
exceeding $1,000, or by imprisonment not exceeding 30 days, or both such fine
or imprisonment. Each day any such violation continues shall constitute a
separate offense. (Prior Code, § 4-201)
Editor’s note:
   This section was revised by the city on November 16, 2015.
§ 4-202 K-9 UNITS.
   (A)   Nothing in this article shall be deemed to prevent or restrict the use
of trained K-9 units by law enforcement personnel. No person owning a dog shall
encourage or permit any dog, or other animal, owned or controlled by him or her
to attack, fight with, or annoy any K-9 unit.
   (B)   No person shall attack, obstruct, or attempt to injure or impede any
K-9 unit engaged in police activities while such unit is under the control and
direction of an authorized law enforcement officer. Any such act shall be an
obstruction of a police officer and prosecuted as such.
   (C)   No person shall attack, obstruct, or attempt to injure or impede any
K-9 unit engaged in police activities while such unit is under the control and
direction of an authorized law enforcement officer. (Prior Code, § 4-202)
§ 4-203 DOGS AT LARGE TRESPASSING UPON OR DAMAGING PROPERTY OF ANOTHER.
   (A)   (1)   The owner of a dog or a person harboring or keeping a dog shall
not allow such dog to roam at large in the city.
      (2)   The owner of a dog or the person harboring or keeping a dog shall
confine such dog at the owner’s premises, or the premises of such person
harboring or keeping such dog.
      (3)   No person shall take any dog into the streets, sidewalks, or public
places of the city unless such dog shall be upon a leash, or under effective
control.
   (B)   No person having the possession of a dog shall lead or take such dog
upon the private property of another without permission, or permit any such dog
to soil on, damage, or destroy the yard, flowers, or shrubbery of another
person, or otherwise trespass upon the property of another without permission.
   (C)   Any owner or keeper of any dog who permits such dog to run at large
shall be liable for any damages or inconvenience inflicted upon the person or
property of another by such dog while so running at large. (Prior Code, § 4-
203)
§ 4-204 IMPOUNDING ANIMALS.
   (A)   The humane officer shall cause to be seized and impounded any dog or
other animal at large in the city, whether licensed or unlicensed.
   (B)   Any dog so seized shall be impounded at the Humane Society or County
Animal Shelter unless and until the Mayor shall designate a different shelter.
(Prior Code, § 4-204)
§ 4-205 RETENTION AND DISPOSITION OF IMPOUNDED DOGS.
   Any dog seized and impounded, as provided in this article, shall be detained
for a period of five days, and if not redeemed by the owner or by the person
harboring such dog within the period applicable, shall be disposed of in such
manner and by such person as the Mayor names and designates; provided, that
whenever the name of any person appears on the collar of any dog so seized,
such person or owner shall forthwith be notified of such seizure, by telephone
where practicable, but in all cases by notice in writing addressed to him or
her and deposited in the United States mail. (Prior Code, § 4-205)
§ 4-206 REDEMPTION OF IMPOUNDED DOGS.
   (A)   The owner of, or person harboring, a dog which has been seized or
impounded, as provided in this article, shall be entitled to redeem the dog by
paying to the Humane Society, County Animal Shelter, or person in charge of
other pound or shelter where the dog is impounded, the redemption fees and
boarding charges levied by the pound or shelter.
   (B)   Whenever more than one dog belonging to the same owner has been
impounded on the same day, a single offense shall be deemed to have occurred.
Otherwise, each dog belonging to the same owner which has been impounded on
separate days shall be deemed to constitute separate offenses. The Humane
Officer shall maintain records of offenses committed by dog owners, and such
records shall be available for public inspection during regular office hours.
In addition to the above redemption fee, a boarding fee for each dog impounded
shall be charged for each day, or a fraction thereof, that the dog has been
impounded.
   (C)   The owner of, or person harboring, a dog not bearing a tag which has
been seized or impounded shall be entitled to redeem his or her dog upon
establishing his or her title thereto to the satisfaction of the Humane Officer
in charge of the dog, by securing a license for the dog, if such dog is not
licensed, and by paying to the county pursuant to a statement furnished such
owner or person by the Humane Officer in charge of such dog a redemption fee
for each day, or fraction thereof, that the dog has been impounded. (Prior
Code, § 4-206)
§ 4-207 INTERFERENCE WITH PERSONS ACTING UNDER ARTICLE.
   No person shall hinder, molest, or interfere with any person authorized or
empowered to perform any duty under this article, nor shall any person attach a
license tag to any dog to which it was not issued, or remove a license tag from
the collar of any dog without the consent of its owner. (Prior Code, § 4-207)
§ 4-208 SEIZING OR ENTICING DOGS.
   Except for persons duly authorized herein, no person shall entice any
properly licensed dog into any enclosure for the purpose of taking off its
collar or tag, or, for such purpose, decoy or entice any dog out of the
enclosure or house of its owner or possessor, or seize or molest any dog which
is held by any person, or bring any dog into the city for the purpose of
impounding and killing the dog. (Prior Code, § 4-208)
§ 4-209 KEEPING VICIOUS DOG.
   No person shall own, keep, or harbor any dog known by him or her to be
vicious, dangerous, or in the habit of biting or attacking persons, whether or
not such dog wears a muzzle, and upon satisfactory proof that such dog is
vicious, dangerous, or in the habit of biting or attacking persons or other
dogs or animals, the Humane Officer may cause such dog to be destroyed. (Prior
Code, § 4-209)
§ 4-210 MUZZLING DOGS UNDER PROCLAMATION BY MAYOR.
   Whenever it is made to appear to the Mayor that there are good reasons for
believing that any dog within the city is mad, he or she may issue a
proclamation requiring that all dogs shall, for a period to be defined in the
proclamation, wear good, substantial muzzles, securely put on, so as to prevent
them from biting or snapping, and any dog going at large, during the period
defined by the Mayor, without such muzzle, shall be taken by the Humane Officer
and impounded, as provided herein. (Prior Code, § 4-210)
§ 4-211 OBSERVATION OF DOG BITING A PERSON.
   Every person owning or harboring a dog in the city which shall bite any
person shall forthwith place the dog, at his or her own expense, in the custody
and care of a licensed veterinarian. (Prior Code, § 4-211)
§ 4-212 CONFINEMENT OF FEMALE DOGS IN HEAT.
   Every person owning or harboring a female dog shall keep such dog confined
for 25 days during the period of estrus. (Prior Code, § 4-212)
§ 4-213 EXCREMENT.
   Neither the owner of a dog or any person having charge of a dog, whether
such dog is on a leash or not, shall allow any such dog in his, her, or their
charge to deposit animal excrement or other animal waste upon private or public
property, or to damage any private or public property otherwise. (Prior Code, §
4-213)
§ 4-214 VACCINATION OF DOGS.
   (A)   Any person who keeps or harbors a dog within the boundaries of the
city shall have such dog properly vaccinated or immunized against rabies, as
required by the W. Va. Code § 19-20A (vaccination of dogs and cats).
   (B)   Whoever obtains an unvaccinated dog shall at once have such dog
properly vaccinated against rabies. Failure to do so shall be a misdemeanor.
(Prior Code, § 4-214)
§ 4-215 COOPERATION WITH OTHER GOVERNMENT BODIES.
   In carrying out the intent and provisions of this article, the city is
expressly authorized to enter into agreements with other municipalities and the
County Commission for the purchase of necessary equipment and supplies,
employment of necessary personnel, operation and maintenance of a dog pound,
and all other matters relating to the provisions of this article, and to share
the cost thereof with other municipalities and the County Commission on a joint
and mutual basis. (Prior Code, § 4-215)
§ 4-216 ADMINISTRATION AND ENFORCEMENT OF ARTICLE.
   It shall be the duty of the Humane Officer or Officers appointed by the
Mayor, with the cooperation of the Police Department, to administer and enforce
the provisions of this article; and the Humane Officer or Officers shall,
whenever they encounter an offense under this article, issue a summons to such
offender for appearance in the Municipal Court. (Prior Code, § 4-216)
§ 4-217 BARKING OR HOWLING DOGS.
   (A)   No person shall own, maintain, or otherwise, by act or omission, keep
a dog which, by barking, howling, crying, or in any other noise-making manner,
disturbs the peace, comfort, or quiet of any neighborhood within the city.
   (B)   For purposes of enforcing this section, the Humane Officer, Mayor, or
police officer, when the Humane Officer is not on duty or scheduled to be
working, may cause a citation to be issued and served on the owner, owners, or
caretakers or providers of any such dog barking, howling, crying, or in any
other noise-making manner disturbing the peace, comfort, or quiet of any
neighborhood within the city. A citation may be issued without impounding the
dog if the owner, owners, or care takers or providers of any such dog are
immediately present, or make their presence known, and immediately take control
over such dog and cause the same to be and remain quiet, such as taking the dog
inside where it cannot be heard, and keeping it inside. The citation may be
issued and served after the impounding of said dog if the owner, owners, or
caretakers or providers are not present, or make their presence immediately
known to the Humane Officer, Mayor, or police officer on the premises where the
dog is present and violating this section, if the identity of such dog owner,
owners, or care taker or provider cannot be readily ascertained, if the dog is
running at large, or if such person fails to immediately take control over such
dog and cause the same to be and remain quiet, such as taking the dog inside
where it cannot be heard, and keeping it inside, provided that the citation
shall be issued and served on the dog owner, owners, or caretakers or providers
as soon after the dog has been impounded as possible, and the owner, owners, or
caretakers or providers of any such dog shall be afforded an opportunity to be
heard at the next regularly scheduled session of Municipal Court after service
of the citation on such person. Service of the citation on the dog owner,
owners, or caretakers or providers of any such dog may be in person, on any
person over the age of 16 years present at the residence of such person, or by
any other manner or method permitted by law, or in accordance with Rule 4 of
the “Rules of Civil Procedure” adopted and approved by the Supreme Court of
Appeals of the state. (Prior Code, § 4-217)
§ 4-218 RESTRICTION ON NUMBER OF DOGS.
   (A)   No person shall own, keep, or permit his or her premises to harbor
more than two dogs on any lot, premises, dwelling, building, structure, boat,
or living accommodation unless:
      (1)   Properly licensed as a commercial kennel in compliance with city
ordinance; or
      (2)   Approved for a special permit under the provisions of §
4-503.
   (B)   Nothing in this section shall be construed as limiting the authority
of the City Council to declare maintaining two or fewer adult dogs a nuisance
if it should find that such a nuisance exists, and to order the abatement of
that nuisance. Any person found in violation of this section shall have 30 days
from the date of notice of violation to apply to the Council for the required
permit. Any person who fails to apply for the required permit within 30 days
shall be subject to a fine of not more than $50 per day for each day following
the initial 30-day notice period. (Prior Code, § 4-218)
§ 4-219 REMOVAL OF DOGS FROM PUBLIC GATHERINGS.
   (A)   No person shall keep any dog at a public gathering after any Humane
Officer, police officer, Mayor, or the City Recorder has determined that the
presence or conduct of the dog may jeopardize the health, safety, or welfare of
any person attending the gathering.
   (B)   Any such dog shall be promptly removed from such public place by its
owner upon oral notification from the officer. (Prior Code, § 4-219)
§ 4-220 DOGS SUBJECT TO TAXATION; DECLARED TO BE PERSONAL PROPERTY.
   Any dog shall be declared to be personal property, and any dog above the age
of six months shall be subject to taxation. (Prior Code, § 4-220)
§ 4-221 COLLECTION OF HEAD TAX ON DOGS; DUTIES OF ASSESSOR AND SHERIFF;
REGISTRATION OF DOGS.
   (A)   It shall be the duty of the County Assessor and Sheriff, as required
by state law, to collect the municipal tax on dogs over six months of $1 for
every male or spayed female, and $2 for every unspayed female. If the tax is
not paid within 15 days of its assessment, then the Sheriff shall have the
right to impound the dog. For such services an extra $1.50 shall be added to
the fee. The Sheriff shall keep the dog for 15 days, after which if the
delinquent tax payer does not pay this tax the Sheriff shall sell the dog and,
after taking out the money required for the tax and up-keep of the dog, return
that sum to the delinquent taxpayer. Should the Sheriff fail to sell the dog he
or she shall dispose of it.
   (B)   When the tax is assessed the Assessor and Sheriff shall put down the
age, sex, color, character of hair (long or short), and breed, and the name and
address of the keeper of the dog. He or she shall then give him or her a
certificate of registration and a registration tag of such dog.
   (C)   The assessor shall be allowed to keep 10% of all tax collected and
return 90% back to the Treasurer of the city. (Prior Code, § 4-221)
§ 4-222 WEARING OF REGISTRATION TAG BY DOG.
   Every registered dog shall, at all times, wear a valid registration tag
issued as provided in this article. The failure to have displayed or worn on
any dog of such tag shall be first evidence that such dog is not registered and
the dog is subject to be impounded, sold, or destroyed.
   (A)   Every dog shall, at all times, wear a collar with the owner’s name,
telephone number, and/or address affixed thereto. Failure to have a collar
shall be prima facie evidence that such dog is not owned and such dog shall be
subject to be and shall be impounded, sold, or destroyed as provided.
   (B)   Every registered dog shall at all times wear a valid registration tag
issued as provided in this article. The failure to have displayed or worn on
any dog of such tag shall be first evidence that such dog is not registered and
the dog is subject to be impounded, sold, or destroyed. (Prior Code, § 4-222)
§ 4-223 FAILURE TO REGISTER DOG; ALTERATION OR FORGING REGISTRATION
CERTIFICATE.
   (A)   Any person who keeps or owns any dog subject to registration under the
provisions of this article who fails, refuses, or neglects to register such
dog, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and come under any penalty that may be
imposed by the County Assessor as an officer of this state.
   (B)   Any person who forges or alters any certificate or tag, or says such
to be valid when he or she knows it is invalid, or permits any dog owned by him
or her to wear fake or invalid tags, shall be also be under any penalties
imposed by the Assessor. (Prior Code, § 4-223)
§ 4-224 DOGS PROTECTED BY LAW; UNLAWFUL KILLING THEREOF; AGGRIEVED OWNER
REMEDY; PENALTY.
   Any dog which is registered, or any dog regardless of age who shall be owned
and kept by any person, shall be protected by the law and any person who shall
unlawfully steel, kill, or injure, administer poison, or knowing expose the
same, intentionally causing the death of some dog, shall be guilty of a
misdemeanor. (Prior Code, § 4-224)
ARTICLE 3: CATS

§ 4-300 DEFINITION.
   For the purpose of this article, the following definition shall apply unless
the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   CAT. All members of the feline family, of either sex, at least six months
old, unless otherwise specified hereinafter. (Prior Code, § 4-300)
§ 4-301 CRUELTY TO CATS.
   (A)   No person shall cruelly or needlessly beat, torture, torment,
mutilate, kill, or willfully deprive necessary sustenance to any cat,
irrespective of whether any such cat is his or her own or that of another
person. No person shall impound or confine any cat in any place unprotected
from the elements, or fail to supply the same with a sufficient quantity of
food and water, or abandon to die any maimed, sick, or diseased cat, or be
engaged in or employed at cat fighting, or pitting one cat to fight against
another cat, or any similar cruelty to any cat, or receive money for the
admission of any person, or use, train, or possess a cat for the purpose of
seizing, detaining, or maltreating any other cat.
   (B)   Any person convicted of violating the provisions of this section shall
be guilty of a misdemeanor, and the violation thereof shall be a fine not
exceeding $1,000, or by imprisonment not exceeding 30 days or both such fine or
imprisonment. Each day any such violation continues shall constitute a separate
offense. (Prior Code, § 4-301)
Editor’s note:
   This section was revised by the city on November 16, 2015.
§ 4-302 NOISY CATS.
   No person shall own or keep within the city any cat which shall, by
squalling, crying, or in any other manner whatsoever, disturb the peace and
quiet of any neighborhood. (Prior Code, § 4-302)
§ 4-303 ROAMING AT LARGE.
   No owner or keeper of any cat shall permit it to roam at large within the
city at any time, except on the property owned or occupied by the owner of such
cat. Any cat found roaming at large in violation of this section shall be
seized by the Animal Warden and forthwith impounded at the owner’s expense.
(Prior Code, § 4-303)
§ 4-304 RESTRICTION ON NUMBER OF CATS.
   (A)   No person shall own, keep, or permit his or her premises to harbor
more than two cats on any lot, premises, dwelling, building, structure, boat,
or living accommodation unless approved for a special permit under the
provisions of §
4-504.
   (B)   Nothing in this section shall be construed as limiting the authority
of the City Council to declare maintaining two or fewer adult cats a nuisance
if it should find that such a nuisance exists, and to order the abatement of
that nuisance. Any person found in violation of this section shall have 30 days
from the date of notice of violation to apply to the Council for the required
permit. Any person who fails to apply for the required permit within 30 days
shall be subject to a fine of not more than $50 per day for each day following
the initial 30-day notice period. (Prior Code, § 4-304)
§ 4-305 WEARING OF COLLAR BY CAT.
   Every cat shall at all times wear a collar with the owner’s name, telephone
number, and/or address affixed thereto. Failure to have a collar shall be prima
facie evidence that such cat is not owned and such cat shall be subject to be
and shall be impounded, sold, or destroyed as provided. The collar shall be a
break away safety collar for cats. (Prior Code, § 4-305)
§ 4-306 CATS AT LARGE TRESPASSING UPON OR DAMAGING PROPERTY OF ANOTHER.
   (A)   The owner of a cat, or a person harboring or keeping a cat, shall not
allow such cat to roam at large in the city. The owner of a cat, or the person
harboring or keeping a cat, shall confine such cat at the owner’s premises, or
the premises of such person harboring or keeping such cat. No person shall take
any cat into the streets, sidewalks, or public places of the city unless such
cat shall be upon a leash, or under effective control.
   (B)   No person having the possession of a cat shall lead or take such cat
upon the private property of another without permission, or permit any such or
cat to soil on, damage, or destroy the yard, flowers, or shrubbery of another
person, or otherwise trespass upon the property of another without permission.
   (C)   Any owner or keeper of any cat who permits such cat to run at large
shall be liable for any damages or inconvenience inflicted upon the person or
property of another by such cat while so running at large. (Prior Code, § 4-
306)

§ 4-400 KEEPING WILD AND EXOTIC ANIMALS.
   No person shall keep or harbor within the city any panther, wildcat, or
bobcat, or bear, wolf, fox, or any other wild or exotic animal of a species
normally dangerous to human beings, or not commonly described as domestic pet
or any skunk from which the perinea glands have not been removed, or any
venomous reptile or any snake of a constrictor species, except pursuant to
authority of a city license or permit which may be issued by special action of
the Council, however no dangerous animal shall be permitted. (Prior Code, § 4-
400)
§ 4-401 LIMITATIONS ON WILD AND EXOTIC ANIMALS.
   No exotic, wild, or reptilian animal shall be on public or city property or
roadway, or transported or taken to another person’s property, unless the same
is placed in a secure and animal approved device made for the transport and
securing of animals, and animals must remain in such. (Prior Code, § 4-401)
§ 4-402 ANIMALS AT LARGE.
   No owner or keeper of any exotic, wild, or reptilian animal shall permit it
to roam or be at large, or removed from its cage, within the city at any time
except on the owner’s property. (Prior Code, § 4-402)
§ 4-403 WOLVES.
   Wolves and wolf hybrids shall not be kept or maintained in the city. (Prior
Code, § 4-403)
§ 4-404 EXEMPT.
   Circuses, zoos, fairs, and the State Wild Life Department are exempt from
permit requirements and conditions of this article, however animals shall be
secured at all times. (Prior Code, § 4-404)
§ 4-405 NOTIFICATION OF EXOTIC ANIMALS.
   The City Recorder shall have the authority to report to the City Chief of
Police and Fire Department the type, number, and address for the location of
any special permit animals. (Prior Code, § 4-405)
§ 4-406 CHIEFS AUTHORIZED TO NOTIFY 911 CENTER.
   The City Chief of Police and/or Chief of the Fire Department may notify the
County 911 Center requesting that calls dispatching emergency personnel to that
location be notified of the type and number of special permit animals at that
location. (Prior Code, § 4-406)
