§ 4-500 BREEDING PERMIT.
   (A)   No person shall cause or allow any dog or cat owned, harbored, or kept
within the city to breed without first obtaining a breeding permit, as
described below. The term BREEDING PERMIT means a written authorization, issued
annually by the City Recorder, giving its lawful holder permission to breed a
dog or cat. Each breeding permit shall be valid for year from the date of
issuance, and may be renewed annually before its expiration date. Each
applicant for such a permit shall pay an annual fee of $30 per dog or cat. A
separate permit must be obtained for each owned dog or cat which is allowed to
breed.
   (B)   The Humane Officer shall enforce the animal breeding permit program to
allow the breeding of dogs and cats that are not sterilized consistent with
criteria herein. Under no circumstances shall such a permit be issued to a
person who has been convicted of animal cruelty or neglect. All breeding
permits shall contain the following terms and conditions.
      (1)   The owner of a female dog or cat that is not sterilized shall not
allow the breeding of more than one litter per animal in any household within
the permit year. Notwithstanding this provision, the City Clerk is hereby
authorized, upon application of a permittee, a one-time basis may be allowed
for the breeding of up to two dog or cat litters per breeding animal within any
domestic household within a permit year. In the event, that a permittee is
forced to euthanize a litter of dogs or cats for medical reasons, the City
Recorder may authorize the breeding of one additional litter of dogs or cats
within the same permit year by the permittee without penalty.
      (2)   The penalty for conviction of violation of division (A) above shall
be a fine of $150 for each violation. This penalty shall not be waived by the
transfer or abandonment of the animal by the non-compliant owner.
      (3)   The City Recorder may revoke any permit issued pursuant to this
section upon a finding that the permit holder has violated its terms and
conditions. Such a finding shall be made only after giving the owner of the
animal in question notice of the violations and an opportunity to explain such
violations to the City Recorder.
   (C)   Breeding permits shall not be issued for puppy or kitten mills, or
commercial breeding of animals. (Prior Code, § 4-500)

   [Repealed by city.]   (Prior Code, § 4-501)

§ 4-502 WILD OR EXOTIC ANIMAL PERMIT.
   A wild or exotic animal permit may be issued on approval of the Council,
with rules and conditions established by resolution for that permit. An annual
fee shall be collected each fiscal year in the amount of $20. Upon the failure
of any owner or occupant of any premises to comply with any of the provisions
of this article, such wild or exotic animal shall be deemed a nuisance, and as
such shall be removed or abated as provided by law. (Prior Code, § 4-502)
§ 4-503 RESTRICTION ON NUMBER OF DOGS; SPECIAL PERMIT.
   (A)   The intent of the special permit application is to allow responsible
pet owners to keep or harbor more than two dogs if adequate conditions exist in
which the animals will not cause damage, hazard, nuisance, or be a detriment to
any persons or property.
   (B)   Any person desiring to keep or harbor more than two dogs shall submit
a written application for a special permit with the City Recorder. The special
permit application shall include a copy of a site plan of the subject property
showing all structures, fences, and open space.
   (C)   The City Recorder may grant a special permit if the following
conditions are met:
      (1)   The subject property is larger than 6,500 square feet, unless the
dogs are kept predominately indoors;
      (2)   The dogs must be kept indoors; or in a secure area with a fence of
sufficient height and durability to prohibit the dog(s) from escaping; or in a
secure area effectively controlled by electronic device; and
      (3)   Adequate shelter, as defined by the Humane Association, be provided
for each dog.
   (D)   Applicants shall not be eligible for a special permit if they are
known in the neighborhood or community for causing disruptions related to dogs.
   (E)   Applicants shall maintain standards for cleanliness, sanitation,
freedom from offensive odors, noise, and overcrowding.
   (F)   Special permits are non-transferable. A change in the number or type
of dogs, or changes in the residence or ownership of the dogs shall require a
new special permit.
   (G)   The fee for a special permit shall be $25 per dog each year for any
dog over the limit of two.
   (H)   The City Recorder may revoke any permit issued pursuant to this
section upon a finding that the permit holder had violated its terms and
conditions. Such a finding shall be made only after giving the owner of the
animal in question notice of the violations and an opportunity to explain such
violations to the City Recorder.
   (I)   Any person aggrieved by the denial or granting of a special permit
shall have the right to appeal to the City Council. (Prior Code, § 4-503)
§ 4-504 RESTRICTION ON NUMBER OF CATS; SPECIAL PERMIT.
   (A)   The intent of the special permit application is to allow responsible
pet owners to keep or harbor more than two cats if adequate conditions exist in
which the animals will not cause damage, hazard, nuisance, or be a detriment to
any persons or property.
   (B)   Any person desiring to keep or harbor more than two cats shall submit
a written application for a special permit with the City Recorder. The special
permit application shall include a copy of a site plan of the subject property
showing all structures, fences, and open space.
   (C)   The City Recorder may grant a special permit if the following
conditions are met:
      (1)   The cats must be kept indoors; or in a secure area with a fence of
sufficient height and durability to prohibit the cat(s) from escaping; or in a
secure area effectively controlled by electronic device; and
      (2)   Adequate shelter, as defined by the Humane Association, be provided
for each cat.
   (D)   Applicants shall not be eligible for a special permit if they are
known in the neighborhood or community for causing disruptions related to cats.
   (E)   Special permits are non-transferable. A change in the number or type
of cats, or changes in the residence or ownership of the cats shall require a
new special permit.
   (F)   The fee for a special permit shall be $25 per cat each year for any
cat over the limit of two.
   (G)   A previously approved special permit may be rejected or revoked at any
time if the humane officer determines the issuance of a special permit has
caused damage, hazard, nuisance, dangerous conditions, or is a detriment to any
person or property.
   (H)   The City Recorder may revoke any permit issued pursuant to this
section upon a finding that the permit holder had violated its terms and
conditions. Such a finding shall be made only after giving the owner of the
animal in question notice of the violations and an opportunity to explain such
violations to the City Recorder.
   (I)   Any person aggrieved by the denial or granting of a special permit
shall have the right to appeal to City Council. (Prior Code, § 4-504)
§ 4-505 KENNEL PERMIT.
   (A)   Any person who desires to own or operate a kennel within the municipal
boundaries of the city must obtain a kennel permit.
   (B)   An annual fee of $50 shall be assessed for kennel permits.
   (C)   Kennels shall be inspected every six months and whenever determined
prudent by the Mayor.
   (D)   Kennel permits shall not be issued for the purpose of puppy or kitten
mills, or breading of animals.
   (E)   Kennel permits shall only be issued after completion of the same
standards as for a permit to keep animals or fowl. The Council shall reserve
the authority to refuse any kennel permit.
   (F)   Kennel permits shall be issued for the lodging and training of animals
only. (Prior Code, § 4-505)
ARTICLE 6: SPAYING AND NEUTERING
Section
   
4-600   Spaying and neutering
   
4-601   Violation
§ 4-600 SPAYING AND NEUTERING.
   It is the purpose of this article to promote the health, safety, and general
welfare of the residents of the city by reducing the number of stray dogs and
cats. The Council finds that each year millions of dogs and cats are euthanized
because they are not wanted. It is the purpose of this section to eliminate the
excessive number of unwanted animals and thereby stop the needless killing of
these animals by restricting the breeding practices of pet owners and breeders
through legislation that is both reasonable and enforceable. It shall be
unlawful to own, possess, or keep in the city any dog or cat over the age of
six months that has not been spayed or neutered except as provided herein.
   (A)   Owners must alter their dogs and cats, unless:
      (1)   The pet is less than six months old;
      (2)   The owner has obtained an unaltered animal permit from the City
Clerk to keep the pet intact, with the cost of such permit to be $75 per
animal, for the life of the animal. Half to be deposited in the General Fund
and half to be deposited with the authority taking possession of animals for
the city;
      (3)   A licensed veterinarian states, in writing, that the animal is
medically unfit to undergo the procedure; or
      (4)   The animal is kept in the city for fewer than 30 days in a one-year
period.
   (B)   To qualify for an unaltered animal permit, the owner must:
      (1)   Satisfy the City Recorder that the permit is sought for a proper
purpose, or purchase a breeding permit;
      (2)   Have the pet examined regularly by a licensed veterinarian;
      (3)   Have the pet vaccinated in accordance with city ordinance and state
law;
      (4)   Have the pet housed properly; and
      (5)   Have had no more than one violation of the animal code in the
preceding 24 months. (Prior Code, § 4-600)
§ 4-601 VIOLATION.
   (A)   Any person cited with a violation of §
4-600 shall have 15 days from the date of issuance of a summons for violation
to comply, and if so done his or her citation shall be dismissed.
   (B)   Any person convicted of violating the provisions of §
4-600 shall be fined $10 per day for each day such violation continues after
they have been notified to correct the violation. (Prior Code, § 4-601)
Editor’s note:
   This section was revised by the city on November 16, 2015.

§ 5-1 DEFINITIONS.
   (A)   Definitions. For the purpose of this article, the following
definitions shall apply unless the context clearly indicates or requires a
different meaning.
      ACT. W. Va. Code §§ 8-33 et seq.
      AUTHORITY. The organized corporate body known as the Municipal Housing
Authority.
      BUILDING DEPARTMENT. The office of the Building Inspector.
      BUILDING OFFICIAL. The Building Inspector, or his or her authorized
representative.
      CELLAR. A portion of a building located partly or wholly underground,
having one-half or more of its clear floor-to-ceiling height below average
grade of the adjoining ground.
      CHIEF ADMINISTRATOR AND APPOINTING AUTHORITY. The Mayor, with the
approval of the governing body when required.
      COMMISSIONER. One of the members of the Municipal Housing Authority,
appointed in accordance with the provisions of this chapter.
      DWELLING. Any building which is wholly or partly used, or intended to be
used, for living or sleeping by human occupants.
      DWELLING UNIT. Any room or group of rooms located within a dwelling and
forming a single habitable unit with facilities which are used for living,
sleeping, cooking, and eating.
      ELECTRICAL INSPECTOR. The Building Inspector, or his or her
representative, or such other person(s) who is invested with the duty of
administering and enforcing the Electrical Code.
      EXTERMINATION. The control and elimination of insects, rodents, or other
pests.
      FAMILY. One or more persons living together, whether related by blood,
marriage, adoption, or through having common housekeeping facilities.
      FAULTY WEATHER PROTECTION. Deterioration or ineffective waterproofing or
exterior walls, roof, foundations, or floors, including broken windows and
doors.
      HABITABLE ROOM. A room or enclosed floor space used or intended to be
used for living, sleeping, cooking, or eating purposes; excluding bathrooms,
water compartments, laundries, pantries, foyer, or communicating corridors,
closets, and storage space.
      INFESTATION. The presence within or around a dwelling of any insects,
rodents, or other pests.
      MULTIPLE DWELLING. Any building, or portions of any building, which is
designated, built, rented, leased, let, or hired out to be occupied as the home
or residence of more than two families living independently of each other, and
shall include flats and apartments.
      OCCUPANT. Any person(s) over the age of one year, sleeping, cooking, or
eating in or having actual possession of a dwelling unit or rooming unit.
      OPERATOR. Any person who has charge, care, or control of a building or a
part of said building.
      OWNER. Any person who alone, or jointly or severally with others, has
legal title to any dwelling unit or other properties with or without
accompanying actual possession thereof, or shall have charge, care, or control
of any dwelling or dwelling unit, or other properties as OWNER or agent of the
OWNER, or as executor, executrix, administrator, administered, trustee, or
guardian of the estate of the OWNER. Any such person representing the actual
owner shall be bound by the provisions of this chapter to the same extent as if
he or she were the OWNER.
      PARTIES IN INTEREST. The owner of the title or a mortgage, whose inters
if shown of record, or the agent of any such person and those in possession of
a dwelling.
      PERSON. Any individual, firm, corporation, association, partnership, or
organization of any kind.
      PLUMBING. All of the following supplied facilities and equipment: gas
pipes, gas-burning equipment, water pipes, garbage disposal units, waste pipes,
water closets, sinks, installed dishwashers, lavatories, bathtubs, shower
baths, and any other similar supplied fixtures, together with all connections
to water, sewer, or gas lines.
      PLUMBING INSPECTION DEPARTMENT. The office of the building inspector or
other such office as may be charged with the duty of enforcing the provisions
of the Plumbing Code.
      PLUMBING OFFICIAL. The Building Inspector, or his or her authorized
representative, or such other person who may be charged with the duty of
administrating the provisions of the Plumbing Code.
      ROOMING HOUSE. Any dwelling, or that part of any dwelling containing one
or more rooming units, in which space is rented by the owner or operator to
four or more persons who are not husband and wife, son, daughter, mother or
father, or sister or brother of the owner or operator.
      ROOMING UNIT. Any room or group of rooms forming a single habitable unit
used or intended to be used for living and sleeping, but not for cooking or
eating purposes.
      TECHNICAL CODE. Any Building Code, Plumbing Code, Electrical Code, or any
other codes which are adopted by the governing body and are applicable under
this chapter.
      TEMPORARY HOUSING. Any tent, trailer, or other structure used for human
shelter which is designed to be transportable and which is not attached to the
ground, to another structure, or to any utilities system on the same premises
for more than 30 consecutive days.
      SHARED AREA. Any area not capable of division, such as halls in which
occupants of more than one living unit or commercial or industrial unit follow
the same course of ingress or egress, or common utility rooms.
   (B)   Meaning of certain words. Whenever the words DWELLING UNIT, ROOMING
UNIT, and PREMISES are used in this chapter, they shall be construed as though
they were followed by the words “or any part thereof.”(Prior Code, § 5-1)

   Building Inspector, see §
5-5
§ 5-2 CREATION OF HOUSING AUTHORITY.
   (A)   There is hereby formed, created, and established a municipal building
commission, which shall have all of the powers set forth in W. Va. Code §§ 8-33
et seq., referred to in this article as “the Act,” and which shall be known as
the City Municipal Housing Authority.
   (B)   The City Municipal Housing Authority shall be a public corporation and
shall have perpetual existence in accordance with the Act.
   (C)   The Mayor shall appoint Commissioners of the Housing Authority, and
these shall be confirmed by Council.
   (D)   (1)   The Board of said Housing Authority shall consist of five
members, of whom no more than two-thirds shall be from the same political
party; no member shall hold any office (other than the office of notary public)
or employment under the United States of America, the state, any county,
municipality, or political subdivision thereof, or any political party; all
members shall be residents of the city, and no member shall receive any
compensation for services as such, but shall be reimbursed by said Board for
reasonable and necessary expenses authorized and actually incurred in the
discharge of his or her duties.
      (2)   The Commissioners who are first appointed shall be designated to
serve for terms of one, two, three, four, and five years respectively.
      (3)   As the term of each initial appointee expires, the successor who
shall fill the vacancy created by such expiration shall be appointed for a term
of five years. Each member of the Board shall have one vote on all matters
coming before the Board. Any individual who is a resident of the city shall be
eligible to serve as a member of the Board. The city shall inform the authority
of its appointments or reappointments to the Board by delivering to the
Commission a copy of the order or resolution making such appointment or re-
appointment.
      (4)   If any member of the Board dies, resigns, or for any other reason
ceases to be a member of the Board prior to expiration of his or her term, the
Council shall appoint another individual to serve the unexpired portion of the
term of such individual. Such member shall remain a member of the Board until
his or her successor is appointed.
   (E)   For inefficiency, misconduct, or neglect of duty, a Commissioner shall
be removed by the Mayor, but a Commissioner shall be removed only after he or
she has been given an opportunity to be heard at a hearing, either in person or
by Council. A copy of the charges shall be given to him or her at least ten
days before the date of such hearing. In the event of the removal of any
Commissioner, a record of the proceedings, together with charges and findings
thereon, shall be fixed in the office of the Municipal Recorder.
   (F)   The City Municipal Housing Authority shall not undertake any projects
or financing therefor without the prior written approval of the City Council.
   (G)   All powers and authority of the Commission shall be as described in
the W. Va. Code §§ 8-33-3 and 8-33-4, as amended from time to time. (Prior
Code, § 5-2)
§ 5-3 BUILDINGS COMMISSION CREATED.
   (A)   There is created an enforcement agency to be known as the Buildings
Commission. Such agency shall be composed of the Mayor, the Building Inspector,
and one member at large, to be selected by and to serve at the will and
pleasure of the Mayor. The Director of Health, or his or her representative,
and the Fire Chief shall serve as ex officio members of the Commission. The
Mayor shall serve as Chairperson, and the Commission shall elect a Vice-
Chairperson. The City Recorder shall serve as Secretary of the Commission. A
majority of the Commission shall constitute a quorum. A permanent record shall
be kept in the City Recorder’s office, and shall be open to inspection by any
party in interest. The Commission shall have authority to make rules and
regulations, not contrary to law, for the purpose of carrying into effect the
purpose of this article.
   (B)   In order to perform its duties effectively and protect the public
interests, the Commission, or any member thereof, or any person delegated by
the Commission for the purpose, shall have authority to go upon and inspect any
building or any part thereof, provided, that such entrance and inspection shall
be made in such a manner as to cause the least possible inconvenience to the
persons in possession.
   (C)   Upon information received from any person or as a result of its own
investigation, the Commission may issue a complaint in Municipal Court against
any building and the owner thereof. Such complaint shall definitely locate the
building, shall describe the conditions complained of, and the court shall set
a date and place for a hearing on the question of whether the building is unfit
for human habitation or is unsafe, unsanitary, dangerous, or detrimental to the
public welfare. The complaint shall be served upon the owner in accordance with
the law of the state, and shall, in addition thereto, be posted in a
conspicuous place on the premises affected by the complaint. Service shall be
made at least ten days prior to the hearing, except that in case of an
emergency endangering the life or health of the occupants of the building or
other parties, the time may be shortened. At such hearing, the owner may appear
in person or by agent or counsel, and may examine any witnesses who testify and
may offer evidence in his or her own behalf. Either the Commission or the owner
may have the entire evidence taken down and preserved, and shall pay the
expense thereof, but the question of who shall be finally liable therefor shall
await the final determination of the cause. A lessee whose interests are
substantially affected may appear and be heard in the same manner as the owner.
In the case of the non-residence of the owner or other circumstances requiring
publication of notice, a copy of the complaint may be published in a newspaper
published in the city once a week for three successive weeks.
   (D)   (1)   If, in the opinion of the court, at such hearing that the
building in question is unfit for habitation or is unsafe, unsanitary,
dangerous, or detrimental to the public welfare, the court shall enter an
order, as recommended by the Commission or, in the court’s opinion, requiring
that such building be closed or demolished, or in a proper case, setting forth
such repairs as are considered necessary in order to make the building
reasonably suited for human habitation, or to make it safe and sanitary and not
dangerous or detrimental to the public. The order shall fix a date when such
work shall be begun and a date for its completion, which latter date may, for
cause, be extended. The owner may, within the time fixed in the order therefor,
notify the court and Commission of his or her intention to comply with the
order, in which case the work shall be done under the supervision of the City
Building Inspector. When the work has been completed in accordance with the
order and approved by the Building Commission, an order shall be entered by
such Commission approving the work to the court and closing the case. If the
owner shall fail to proceed with the work in the manner or according to the
schedule set forth in the order, it shall be the duty of the Commission to take
the work in hand and complete it as though the owner had never elected to
perform it himself or herself.
      (2)   If, within the time provided in the order, the owner fails to
notify the Commission of his or her election to do the work required, the
Commission shall proceed to have such work done, either by contract or by the
purchase of necessary material and the employment of workers and equipment.
   (E)   (1)   Following completion of the work ordered by the Building
Commission, the Building Inspector shall certify to the Commission the costs of
such repairs, alterations, improvements, closing, or removal or demolition of
such building. The City Recorder shall record such certificate as a lien in the
office of the Clerk of the County Commission, which lien shall not exceed the
assessed value of the property as recorded in the office of the County
Assessor.
      (2)   As alternative to division (D)(1) above, the Commission may
instruct the City Solicitor to institute a civil action in a court of competent
jurisdiction against the land owner or other responsible party for all costs
incurred by the municipality with respect to the property, and for reasonable
attorney’s fees and court costs incurred in the prosecution of the action. In
such case, not less than ten days prior to instituting a civil action as
provided for in this section, the City Recorder of the municipality shall send
notice to the land owner by certified mail, return receipt requested, advising
the land owner of the governing body’s intention to institute such action. Such
notice shall be sent to the most recent address to the land owner of record in
the office of the Assessor of the county where the subject property is located.
If, for any reason, such certified mail is returned without evidence of proper
receipt thereof, then in such event the governing body shall cause a Class II
legal advertisement to be published in a newspaper of general circulation in
the county wherein the subject property is located, and post notice on the
front door or other conspicuous location on the subject property.
   (F)   The owner or lessee of the property shall have the right to apply to
the Circuit Court of the county for a temporary injunction restraining the
Commission pending final disposition of the cause, and a hearing shall be had
by the court within 20 days, or as soon thereafter as possible, to enter such
final order or decree as law and justice may require. Costs shall be imposed in
the discretion of the court. Fines for non-compliance shall be assessed from
the date of first order given, and each day thereafter shall constitute a
separate offense.
   (G)   (1)   Whoever shall contemptuously and in bad faith violate or fail to
comply with any order of the Buildings Commission or Municipal Court shall, for
each and every such violation and non-compliance respectively, be deemed guilty
of a misdemeanor and punishment shall be a fine not exceeding $1,000. Each day
any such violation continues shall constitute a separate offense. Provided,
that no conviction shall be had hereunder without such order having been
entered at an open session of the Municipal Court wherein the violator was
present, or without personal service of the order having been made upon the
violator. The imposition of one penalty for any violation shall not excuse the
violation or permit it to continue, and all violators shall be required to
correct or remedy such violations or defects in a reasonable time. When not
otherwise specified, each day that prohibited conditions continue shall
constitute a separate offense.
      (2)   Where any such structure is owned by a corporation rather than by
an individual, then the officer of the corporation responsible for the
maintenance of the structure shall be jointly and severally liable with the
corporation hereunder.
      (3)   The above penalties shall be in addition to other remedies of the
Buildings Commission. (Prior Code, § 5-3)
Editor’s note:
   This section was revised by the city November 16, 2015.
§ 5-4 DUTIES OF MUNICIPAL COURT.
   The Municipal Court shall:
   (A)   Upon timely receipt of a request for a hearing, give written notice to
the parties concerned of the time and place of the hearing;
   (B)   Hold a hearing and hear all competent testimony offered by the
Building Official, or his or her designee, and any party concerned relative to
the substandard building or structure;
   (C)   Make written findings of fact as to whether or not the building or
structure in question is substandard within the terms of this chapter;
   (D)   If the building or structure is found to be substandard and a public
nuisance, issue an order directing the appropriate party or parties concerned
to abate the nuisance by repair, vacation, or demolition of the building or
structure, as the facts may warrant under the standards provided in this
chapter, within a reasonable time not to exceed 30 days;
   (E)   If the party or parties concerned fail(s) to comply with the order
provided herein, cause such building or structure to be repaired, vacated, or
demolished as the facts may warrant under the standards provided in this
chapter;
   (F)   Cause the cost of such work performed by the city to be charges as a
tax lien against the real property upon which the nuisance was abated, and to
assess a fine against the said party or parties in accordance with §
1-106. Fines for non-compliance shall be assessed from the date of the first
order given, and each day thereafter shall constitute a separate offense; and
   (G)   Where it reasonably appears that immediate action to repair, vacate,
or demolish a substandard building or structure is necessary to protect life or
property, the Municipal Court shall cause such immediate repair, vacation, or
demolition and charge the costs to the property owner. (Prior Code, § 5-4)
§ 5-5 BUILDING INSPECTOR.
   (A)   There is hereby created the position of Building Inspector, who shall
be appointed by the Mayor with the consent of Council. The Building Inspector
shall serve at the will and pleasure of the Mayor and/or Council.
   (B)   He, she, or they shall demonstrate suitable knowledge of building and
construction standards, and familiarity of the State Building Code, being W.
Va. Code § 15A-11-5, the provisions thereof shall be controlling within the
designated limits of the city. One copy of the code, certified by the City
Recorder, shall be available to the public for inspection and use during all
regular business hours.
   (C)   The Building Inspector shall administer and enforce the Building Codes
of the city and all other laws, ordinances, and regulations under which
building, construction, and occupancy permits are required, and shall conduct
inspections of properties throughout the city in connection with such
administration and enforcement. The Building Inspector shall report any persons
who violate such Building Codes, laws, regulations, and ordinances to the Mayor
and City Council.
   (D)   He or she shall have the authority to delegate his or her authority to
such deputies, assistants, and other personnel as may be assigned to his or her
office by Mayor and City Council.
   (E)   It shall be the duty of all municipal officers and employees to
cooperate with the Building Inspector upon his or her request whenever, it may
be necessary, in order to faithfully discharge the duties of his or her office.
   (F)   (1)   In order to ensure compliance with the technical code, the
Building Inspector (Official) is authorized to enter, examine, and survey at
all reasonable times all dwellings, dwellings units, rooming units, and other
properties.
      (2)   The owner or occupant of every dwelling, dwelling unit, and rooming
units, or the person in charge thereof, shall give the Building Inspector free
access to such dwelling, dwelling unit, rooming unit, or other properties, and
its premises, at all reasonable times for the purpose of such inspection,
examination, or survey.
   (G)   (1)   Whenever the Building Official feels that an emergency exists
which requires immediate action so as to protect the health and welfare of the
community, he or she may, without notice, issue an order reciting the existence
of such emergency and requiring such action be taken as he or she deems
necessary to meet the emergency. Such an order is effective immediately.
      (2)   The subject of such an order, however, still retains the right to a
hearing subject to the provisions laid down in §
5-4.
   (H)   Whenever the Building Official determines that there are reasonable
grounds to believe that there has been a violation of any provisions of the
technical code, or whenever a petition filed by a least five residents to this
effect and a preliminary investigation by the Building Official discloses that
there is a basis for such charges, the Building Official shall give notice of
such alleged violation to all parties in interest. Such notice shall:
      (1)   Be in writing;
      (2)   Include a statement of the reasons why it is being issued;
      (3)   Allow a reasonable time for the performance of any act it requires;
      (4)   Be served upon the owner, his or her agent, or the occupant as the
case may require, and in accordance authorized by the laws of this state; and
      (5)   Advise the recipient that, upon his or her request, a hearing will
be held as described in §§
5-4 or
5-13. (Prior Code, § 5-5)
Editor’s note:
   This section was revised by the city on November 16, 2025.
§ 5-6 DIRECTOR OF HEALTH.
   A Director of Health may be appointed as needed to serve on any board, and
shall be appointed by the Mayor with consent of the Council. (Prior Code, § 5-
6)
§ 5-7 REGULATIONS OF HEALTH.
   The authority and the procedure set forth in this article shall not be
construed as exclusive, but shall be in addition to other police powers
possessed by the city for dealing with conflagrations, health conditions, and
other problems affecting the safety and welfare of the inhabitants of the city.
(Prior Code, § 5-7)
§ 5-8 ALL COMMISSIONS TO REPORT TO MAYOR.
   All commissions, housing authorities, and inspectors shall file with the
Mayor an annual report of their activities for the preceding year, and shall
make recommendations with reference to such additional legislation or other
action as it deems necessary to carry out the provisions of this chapter.
(Prior Code, § 5-8)
§ 5-9 SEVERABILITY.
   If any provision of this chapter, or the application thereof to any person
or circumstances, shall be held invalid by any court of competent jurisdiction,
such invalidity shall not affect the other provisions, or application thereof,
of this chapter which can be given effect without the invalid provision or
application, and to this end, the provisions of this chapter are hereby
declared to be severable. (Prior Code, § 5-9)
§ 5-10 CONFLICTS.
   In the event that any portion of this chapter conflicts with the provisions
of any ordinance of this city, the provisions which establish the higher
standard for the promotion and protection of the health and safety of the
people shall prevail. (Prior Code, § 5-10)
§ 5-11 NO DUTY TO ENFORCE.
   Nothing in this chapter shall be construed as requiring the city to enforce
the prohibitions in this chapter against all or any properties which may
violate the article. In the city’s prosecutorial discretion, and as the city’s
resources permit, this article may be enforced only as to a limited number of
problem properties per year. Nothing in this chapter, or the absence of any
similar provisions from any other city law shall be construed to impose a duty
upon the city to enforce such other provisions of law. (Prior Code, § 5-11)
§ 5-12 TRANSFER OF OWNERSHIP.
   No owner of any building upon whom a notice has been served that violations
of this chapter exist in such a building or its premises shall sell, transfer,
grant, mortgage, ease, or otherwise dispose of said property until compliance
with such notice or order has been secured, or until the owner furnishes to the
purchaser, transferee, grantee, mortgagee, or lessee a true copy of the notice
or order, and at the same time shall have given adequate notification to the
Building Official of his or her intent to enter into such transaction. The
notification must include the name and address of the person or persons to whom
the sale, transfer, grant, mortgage, or lease is proposed. A purchaser who has
been informed of the existence of any notice or order is hereby bound by this
code. (Prior Code, § 5-12)
§ 5-13 HARDSHIPS AND APPEALS.
   (A)   Where the literal application of the provisions of the technical code
would appear to cause undue hardship on an owner or tenant, or if it is claimed
that the provisions of the technical code have been misinterpreted, the owner
or tenant may appeal the decision of the Building Official to the Building
Commission. The Building Commission shall have jurisdiction to hear and decide
appeals where it is alleged there is error in any order, requirement, decision,
or determination made by the Building Official in the enforcement of the
technical code.
   (B)   The Building Commission shall have the power to affirm or reverse,
wholly or partly, or modify the order, requirement, decision, or determination
appealed from, and may make such order, requirement, decision, or determination
as ought to be made, and such order shall be binding on the owners and
occupants of the structure or building affected.
   (C)   The proceedings of such a hearing, including the findings and decision
of the Building Official, shall be summarized, reduced to writing, and entered
as a matter of public record. Such record shall also include a copy of every
notice or order issued. Any person aggrieved by any decision of the Building
Commission may seek relief in Municipal Court and then in any court of
competent jurisdiction. (Prior Code, § 5-13)
§ 5-14 CONDEMNATION.
   Any dwelling or dwelling unit condemned as unfit, pursuant to the standards
of this chapter, shall be vacated within 30 days after issuance of the order of
condemnation. (Prior Code, § 5-14)
§ 5-15 REOCCUPATION.
   No dwelling or dwelling unit which has been condemned and evacuated as unfit
for human occupancy shall be reoccupied without written authorization by the
Building Official. Such authorization shall not be given until the defects have
been eliminated. (Prior Code, § 5-15)
§ 5-16 PENALTIES.
   (A)   Any person convicted of violating the provisions of this chapter, or
fails to comply with any of its mandatory provisions, shall be deemed guilty of
a misdemeanor, and if no specific penalty is provided for the violation
thereof, shall be fined not exceeding $1,000. Each day any such violation
continues shall constitute a separate offense.
   (B)   In addition, any condition caused or permitted to exist in violation
of any of the provisions of this chapter shall be deemed a public nuisance.
(Prior Code, § 5-16)
Editor’s note:
   This section was revised by the city on November 16, 2015.
§ 5-17 MUNICIPAL INSPECTION.
   The Building Inspector or Code Enforcement Officer of the municipality, or
his or her representative, shall have plenary power and authority to enter for
inspection of private premises to aid in the enforcement of any state law or
municipal ordinance; provided, that this section shall not be construed as
purporting to authorize an unreasonable search and seizure prohibited by
Section Six, Article Three of the Constitution of this state.(W. Va. Code § 8-
12-15) (Prior Code, § 5-17)

ARTICLE 1: BUILDING CODE AND PERMITS

§ 5-100 ADOPTION OF BUILDING CODE.
   (A)   There is enacted and adopted by reference, as though they were copied
herein fully, for the purpose of establishing rules and regulations, the State
Building Code, as promulgated by the State Fire Commission pursuant to W. Va.
Code § 15A-11-5, the provisions thereof shall be controlling within the
designated limits of the city. One copy of the code, certified by the City
Recorder, shall be available to the public for inspection and use during all
regular business hours.
   (B)   Any existing town ordinance that is more stringent or imposes a higher
standard than is required by the above referenced codes shall govern, provided
such ordinance is not inconsistent with the laws of the state and is not
contrary to recognized standards and good engineering practices.
   (C)   Any existing city ordinance that is less stringent or imposes a lower
standard than is required by the above referenced codes is hereby amended to
comply therewith. (Prior Code, § 5-100)
Statutory reference:
   Similar provisions, see W. Va. Code § 8-12-13
§ 5-101 PERMIT REQUIRED.
   (A)   It shall be unlawful for any owner or authorized agent who intends to
construct, enlarge, alter, repair, move, demolish, or change the occupancy of a
building or structure, or to erect, install, enlarge, alter, repair, remove,
convert, or replace any electrical, gas, mechanical, or plumbing system, the
installation of which is regulated by code, or cause any such work to be done,
to do so without first obtaining a building permit from the City Council.
   (B)   Each owner or agent shall not:
      (1)   Construct, alter, or add to any building or any appurtenant
structure or feature within the city;
      (2)   Destroy, raze, or demolish any edifice, structure, or building
within the city;
      (3)   Construct, install, repair, extend, alter, remove, or dismantle any
plumbing system or device, or any part thereof; and
      (4)   Construct, install, erect, repair, extend or alter, remove, or
dismantle any electrical wiring apparatus, fixture, or device, or any part
thereof. No person shall connect with a supply or current wires or wiring, or
equipment, within any building or other structure within the city, unless and
until such wiring or equipment to be so connected shall have been approved, in
writing, by an electrical inspector.
   (C)   Each person desiring to perform any work which requires a building or
demolition permit must submit an application to the City Recorder, accompanied
by the plans, specifications, cost, and location of the proposed work for
review by the city. Although the Recorder may, at the option of the Council, be
permitted to issue a provisional permit, such provisional permit does not
become effective until ratified by City Council at a regular or special meeting
called for such purpose. Any work performed under the provisional permit issued
by the Recorder prior to approval thereof by the City Council shall be at the
risk of the permit holder. City Council may condition its approval of any
building permit upon such reasonable terms and conditions as it deems
appropriate to protect the health, safety, and welfare of the citizens of the
city.
   (D)   All permits issued hereunder shall expire six calendar months from the
date of approval thereof by the City Council, and will not be renewed without
express approval of City Council. Upon showing of diligent prosecution during
the initial six-month period of the work for which the permit was originally
issued, the City Council may, for an additional fee of $100, in its discretion,
renew the permit for an additional period of six months. Any permit issued
after a period of 18 months must reapply as if this was a first permit. (Prior
Code, § 5-101)
Editor’s note:
   This section was revised by the city on May 2024.
§ 5-102 BUILDING PERMIT FEES.
   (A)   Fees charged for building permits shall be:
      (1)   A $20 application fee on all building permits;
      (2)   A base fee of $20 for improvements, remodeling, and repairs of a
value more than $500 and less than $1,000;
      (3)   A base fee of $35 shall be charged for construction over $1,000,
plus $2 for each $1,000, or any part thereof, with a maximum fee of $750;
      (4)   A base fee of $50 and $2.50 for each $1,000, or any part thereof,
for commercial and industry, with a maximum fee of $7,500;
      (5)   Mobile home and manufactured housing shall be $250;
      (6)   All demolition permits and building razing permits are $150;
      (7)   Grading only shall be $5 per $1,000; and
      (8)   Renewal fees shall be $100.
   (B)   If any fines and/or court costs are levied, this shall not excuse or
be taken in place of building permit fees. (Prior Code, § 5-102)
Editor’s note:
   This section was revised by the city on November 16, 2015.
§ 5-103 CONTRACTORS REQUIREMENT.
   Contractors, or any person performing work on any property in the city,
shall view or obtain a building permit before any work is performed. Permits
shall be checked for date, location, type of work to be performed, and approval
by proper authority. Conditions of §§
5-100 and
5-101 shall apply. (Prior Code, § 5-103)
§ 5-104 PENALTIES.
   Any person convicted of violating the provisions of this article, or fails
to comply with any of its mandatory provisions, shall be deemed guilty of a
misdemeanor and, if no specific penalty is provided for, the violation thereof
shall be a fine not exceeding $1,000. For violations in excess of $250,000, the
violation thereof shall be a fine not exceeding $2,000. Each day any such
violation continues shall constitute a separate offense. (Prior Code, § 5-104)
Editor’s note:
   This section was added by the city on November 16, 2015.
ARTICLE 2: SUBSTANDARD BUILDINGS AND STRUCTURES
Section
   
5-200   Declaration of nuisance
   
5-201   Definitions

§ 5-200 DECLARATION OF NUISANCE.
   (A)   The City Council, recognizing that there are many existing buildings
which constitute a menace and a detriment to the health, safety, morals, and
general welfare of the people of this city, declares any dwelling or other
building unfit for human habitation due to dilapidation, defects increasing the
hazard of fire, accidents, or other calamities, lack of ventilation, light, or
sanitary facilities, or other conditions, or any building or structure, whether
used for human habitation or not, which, because of conditions prevailing
therein, is unsafe, unsanitary, dangerous, or detrimental to the public welfare
is declared to be a nuisance, and may be repaired, improved, vacated, closed,
or demolished, and such nuisance abated as provided.
   (B)   (1)   The Buildings Commission shall be the enforcement agency and,
upon information received from any person or as a result of its own
investigation, the Commission may report to the City Council and upon their
authority, shall issue a complaint in the Municipal Court against any building
and the owner thereof.
      (2)   Such complaint shall definitely locate the building, shall describe
the conditions complained of, and the court shall set a date and place for a
hearing on the question of whether the building is unfit for human habitation
or is unsafe, unsanitary, dangerous, or detrimental to the public welfare.
   (C)   In order to perform its duties effectively and protect the public
interests, the Commission, or any member thereof, or any person delegated by
the Commission for this purpose, shall have authority to go upon and inspect
any building or any part thereof, provided, that such entrance and inspection
shall be made in such a manner as to cause the least possible inconvenience to
the persons in possession.
   (D)   As provided in §
5-3 of this chapter, the Commission has plenary power and authority to require
the owner to pay for the costs of repairing, altering, or improving, or of
vacating and closing, removing, or demolishing any dwelling or building. (Prior
Code, § 5-200)
Editor’s note:
   This section was revised by the city on November 16, 2015.
Statutory reference:
   Similar provisions, see W. Va. Code § 8-12-16
§ 5-201 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this article, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   OWNER or LANDOWNER. A person who individually or jointly with others:
      (1)   Has legal title to the property, with or without actual possession
of the property;
      (2)   Has charge, care, or control of the property as owner or agent of
the owner;
      (3)   Is an executor, administrator, trustee, or guardian of the estate
of the owner;
      (4)   Is the agent of the owner for the purpose of managing, controlling,
or collecting rents; or
      (5)   Is entitled to control or direct the management or disposition of
the property.
   SUBSTANDARD. The following buildings or structures shall be deemed
SUBSTANDARD.
      (1)   Those whose interior walls or other vertical structural members
list, lean, or buckle to such an extent that a plumb line passing through the
center of gravity falls outside to the middle third of the base.
      (2)   Those which, exclusive of the foundation, show 33% or more of
damage or deterioration of the supporting member or members, or 50% of damage
or deterioration of the non-supporting, enclosing, or outside walls or
covering.
      (3)   Those which have floors or roofs which are overloaded, have
improperly distributed loads, or have insufficient strength to be reasonably
safe for the purpose used.
      (4)   Those which have been damaged by fire, flood, wind, hail,
vandalism, casualty, or other cases so as to have become dangerous to life,
health, safety, or welfare of the occupants or the public.
      (5)   Those which are so dilapidated, decayed, unsafe, unsanitary, or
which so utterly fail to provide the amenities essential to decent living that
they are unfit for human habitation, or are likely to cause sickness or
disease, so as to endanger the health, safety, or welfare of the occupants.
      (6)   Those having light, air, and sanitation facilities which are
inadequate to protect the health, safety, or welfare of the occupants.
      (7)   Those having inadequate stairways, elevators, fire escapes, or
other means of egress in case of emergency.
      (8)   Those having any piece, part, or attachment so insecurely fixed as
to be in danger of falling or being dislodged by the elements and injuring
persons or property.
      (9)   Those which, because of their condition, are unsafe, unsanitary, or
dangerous to the health, safety, or welfare of the public.
      (10)   Those existing in violation of any provision of the Building Code,
Fire Code, or other ordinances of this city.
      (11)   Any swimming pool, septic tank, or other in-ground structure which
endangers the health, safety, or welfare of the public.
      (12)   Those used in violation of the laws relating to controlled
dangerous substances. (Prior Code, § 5-201)
Editor’s note:
   This section was revised by the city on November 16, 2015.
Statutory reference:
   Similar provisions, see W. Va. Code § 8-12-16
§ 5-202 STANDARDS FOR REPAIR, VACATION, OR DEMOLITION.
   The following are the standards in ordering the abatement of a public
nuisance by repair, vacation, or demolition of substandard buildings or
structures.
   (A)   If the building or structure can reasonably be repaired so that it
will no longer exist in violation of the terms of this article, it shall be
ordered repaired. An order to repair may include a requirement to close and
secure any or all exterior openings.
   (B)   If the building or structure is in such condition as to make it
dangerous to the health, safety, or welfare of its occupants, or if deemed
necessary for the abatement of the nuisance, it shall be ordered vacated.
   (C)   If the building or structure is damaged, decayed, or deteriorated to
such a degree that it is not feasible to repair such building or it is not
structurally safe, the building or structure, or any portion thereof, shall be
ordered demolished. (Prior Code, § 5-202)
§ 5-203 ABATEMENT.
   If any owner, occupant, or person in charge of any premises to whom a notice
of violation or order has been issued fails to comply with the terms of such
notice, or with the terms imposed by the Municipal Court, as the case may be,
the Building Code Official, upon consultation with the Mayor and City Council,
may have such violation and/or public nuisance abated or the provisions of such
order carried out, after reasonable notice to such owner, occupant, or person
in charge of the premises of his or her intention to do so, and collect all
abatement costs, with 1% per month interest added from the date of the notice,
from the owner, occupant, or person in charge, by distress or sale, in the same
manner in which taxes levied upon real estate for the benefit of the city are
authorized to be collected; and the abatement costs shall remain a lien upon
the premises, or part of the premises, the same as taxes levied upon real
estate, which lien may be enforced by any court having jurisdiction, as other
liens against real estate are enforced. In case of non-resident owners of real
estate, such notice may be served upon any tenant, occupant, assignee, or
rental agent, or by publication once a week for not less than two consecutive
weeks in a newspaper circulated in the city. (Prior Code, § 5-203)
§ 5-204 CLANDESTINE DRUG LAB SITES AND CHEMICAL DUMPSITES.
   (A)   General provisions.
      (1)   Purpose and intent. The purpose of this article is to reduce public
exposure to health risks where law enforcement officers have determined that
hazardous chemicals from a suspected clandestine drug lab site or associated
dumpsite may exist. The City Council finds that such sites may contain
suspected chemicals and residues that place people, particularly children or
adults of child bearing age, at risk when exposed through inhabiting or
visiting the site, now and in the future.
      (2)   Interpretation and application. In their interpretation and
application, the provisions of this article shall be construed to protect the
public health, safety, and welfare. Where the conditions imposed by any
provision of this article are either more or less restrictive than comparable
provisions imposed by any other law, ordinance, statute, or regulation of any
kind, the regulations which are more restrictive or which impose height
standards or requirements shall prevail. Should any court of competent
jurisdiction declare any section or subpart of this article to be invalid, such
decision shall not affect the validity of the article as a whole or any part
thereof, other than the provision declared invalid.
      (3)   Fees. Fees for the administration of this article may be
established and amended periodically by resolution of the City Council.
      (4)   Definitions. For the purpose of this section, the following
definitions shall apply unless the context clearly indicates or requires a
different meaning.
         CHEMICAL DUMP SITE. Any place or area where chemicals or other waste
materials used in a clandestine drug lab have been located.
         CHILD. Any person less than 18 years of age.
         CLANDESTINE DRUG LAB. The unlawful manufacture or attempt to
manufacture controlled substances.
         CLANDESTINE DRUG LAB SITE. Any place or area where law enforcement has
determined that conditions associated with the operation of an unlawful
clandestine drug lab exist. A CLANDESTINE DRUG LAB SITE may include dwellings,
accessory structures, a chemical dump site or any land.
         CONTROLLED SUBSTANCE. A drug, substance, or immediate precursor as may
be defined in W. Va. Code Ch. 60A. The term shall not include distilled
spirits, wine, malt beverages, intoxicating liquors, or tobacco.
         HOUSEHOLD HAZARDOUS WASTES. Waste generated from a clandestine drug
lab. Such wastes shall be treated, stored, transported, or disposed of in a
manner consistent with the State Department of Health, the State Department of
Environmental Protection, and the County Health Department rules and
regulations.
         MANUFACTURE. In places other than a pharmacy, shall mean and include
the production, cultivation, quality control, and standardization by
mechanical, physical, chemical, or pharmaceutical means, packing, repacking,
tableting, encapsulating, labeling, relabeling, filing, or by other process of
drugs.
         OWNER. Any person, firm, or corporation who owns, in whole or in part,
the land, buildings, or structures associated with a clandestine drug lab site
or chemical dump site.
         PUBLIC HEALTH NUISANCE. All dwellings, accessory structures, and
buildings or adjacent property associated with a clandestine drug lab site are
potentially unsafe due to health hazards and are considered a PUBLIC HEALTH
NUISANCE.
   (B)   Administration.
      (1)   Law enforcement notice to other authorities. Law enforcement
authorities that identify conditions associated with a clandestine drug lab
site or chemical dump site that places neighbors, visiting public or present
and future occupants of the dwelling at risk for exposure to harmful
contaminants and other associated conditions must promptly notify the
appropriate municipal, child protection, and public health authorities of the
property location, property owner, if known, and conditions found.
      (2)   Declaration of property as a public health nuisance. If law
enforcement determines the existence of a clandestine drug lab site or chemical
dump site, the property shall be declared a public health nuisance.
      (3)   Notice of public health nuisance to concerned parties. Upon
notification by law enforcement authorities, the City Building Official shall
promptly issue a declaration of public health notice for the affected property
and post a copy of the declaration at the probable entrance to the dwelling or
property. The Building Official shall also notify the owner of the property by
mail and notify the following parties:
         (a)   Occupants of the property;
         (b)   Neighbors at probable risk;
         (c)    The City Police Department; and
         (d)   Other state and local authorities, such as the State DEP and the
County Health Department which are known to have public and environmental
protection responsibilities that are applicable to the situation.
      (4)    Property owner’s responsibility to act. The Building Official
shall also issue an order to abate the public health nuisance, including the
following.
         (a)   Immediately vacate those portions of the property, including
building or structure interiors, which may place the occupants or visitors at
risk.
         (b)   1.   Within ten calendar days, contract with appropriate
environmental testing and cleaning firms to conduct an on-site assessment,
complete clean up, and remediation testing and follow-up testing, and determine
that the property risks are sufficiently reduced to allow safe human occupancy
of the dwelling.
            2.   The property owner shall immediately notify the city of
actions taken and reach an agreement with the city on the clean up schedule.
The city shall consider practical limitations and the availability of
contractors in approving the schedule for clean-up.
         (c)   Provide written documentation of the clean up process, including
a signed, written statement that the property is safe for human occupancy and
that the clean up was conducted in accordance with applicable state law and/or
guidelines.
      (5)   Property owner’s responsibility for costs. The property owner shall
be responsible for all costs of vacation or clean up of the site, including
contractor’s fees and public costs for services that were performed in
association with a clandestine drug lab site or chemical dump site clean up.
Public costs may include, but are not limited to:
         (a)   Posting of the site;
         (b)   Notification of affected parties;
         (c)   Expenses related to the recovery of costs, including the
assessment process;
         (d)   Laboratory fees;
         (e)   Clean-up services;
         (f)   Administrative fees to be billed at a current per hour rate for
the services rendered; and/or
         (g)   All other associated costs, including court costs and attorney
fees, that may be incurred relative to the costs of vacation or clean-up of the
site and enforcement of the terms of this section.
      (6)   Recovery of public costs.
         (a)   If, after service of notice of the declaration of public health
nuisance, the property owner fails to arrange appropriate assessment and clean
up, the City Building Official is authorized to proceed in a prompt manner to
initiate the on-site assessment and clean up.
         (b)   If the city is unable to locate the property owner within seven
days of the declaration of public health nuisance, the city is authorized to
proceed in a prompt manner to initiate the on-site assessment and clean up.
         (c)   The city may abate the nuisance by removing the hazardous
structure or building, or otherwise, according to the State Code.
         (d)   If the city abates the public health nuisance, in addition any
other legal remedy, the city shall be entitled to recover all costs, plus an
additional 25% of the costs for administration. The city may recover costs by
civil action against the person or persons who own the property.
      (7)   Authority to modify or remove declaration of public health
nuisance.
         (a)   The Building Official is authorized to modify the declaration
conditions or remove the declaration of public health nuisance.
         (b)   Such modifications or removal of the declaration shall only
occur after documentation from a qualified environmental or cleaning firm
stating that the health and safety risks, including those to neighbors and
potential dwelling occupants, are sufficiently abated or corrected to allow
safe occupancy of the dwelling.
   (C)   Violations and penalties. Upon a finding that a person is responsible
for a civil violation of this chapter, the Municipal Judge shall impose a civil
sanction of not less than $500 nor more than $1,000, for each violation. Each
day in which a violation of this chapter continues or the failure to perform
any act or duty required by this chapter or by the Municipal Judge continues
shall constitute a separate civil offense. (Prior Code, § 5-204)
Statutory reference:
   Clandestine drug laboratories, see W. Va. Code § 60A-4-411
ARTICLE 3: REGISTRATION OF PROPERTY
Section
   
5-300   Registration of vacant buildings; registration fees; procedures for
administration and enforcement
   
5-301   Registration of uninhabitable property
§ 5-300 REGISTRATION OF VACANT BUILDINGS; REGISTRATION FEES; PROCEDURES FOR
ADMINISTRATION AND ENFORCEMENT.
   (A)   Definitions. For the purpose of this section, the following
definitions shall apply unless the context clearly indicates or requires a
different meaning.
      OWNER. A person who, individually or jointly with others, has legal title
to the property, with or without actual possession of the property, or has
charge, care, or control of the property as owner or agent of the owner, or is
an executor, administrator, trustee, or guardian of the estate of the owner, or
is the agent of the owner for the purpose of managing, controlling, or
collecting rents, or is entitled to control or direct the management or
disposition of the property.
      VACANT BUILDING. A building or other structure, residential or
commercial, that is unoccupied or unsecured, or occupied by one or more
unauthorized persons for more than 30 days continuous.
         (a)   Provided, that a new building under construction or a building
that, by definition, is exempted by ordinance of the municipality, is not
deemed a vacant building.
         (b)   Provided, however, that the governing body of a municipality
shall, on a case-by-case basis, upon request by the property owner, exempt a
vacant building from registration upon a finding for good cause shown that the
person will be unable to occupy the building for a determinant period of time.
         (c)   Provided, a building or other structure, residential or
commercial, actively listed and advertised for sale shall be exempt from
registration for a period of one year.
      VACANT PROPERTY. A property on which no building is erected and no
routine activity occurs.
   (B)   Registration.
      (1)   Ninety days after a building, residential or commercial, becomes
vacant, it shall be subject to registration. An owner shall provide, on a form
provided by the city, in writing the name, address, and location of the
property, and address and telephone numbers of all owners, and where a person
responsible for care and emergencies can be contacted.
      (2)   Vacant buildings shall be subject to an initial $30 administrative
fee plus a $25 residential registration fee or a $100 commercial registration
fee shall be charged for the first year. The second year, a $150 residential or
a $300 commercial renewal fee will apply. The third year, a registration fee of
$350 residential or $700 shall apply. The fourth year, and each year
thereafter, a registration fee of $500 residential or a $1,000 commercial shall
apply.
      (3)   Vacant property shall be subject to an initial $30 administrative
fee plus a $25 registration fee for the first year. The second year, and every
year thereafter, a $75 fee shall apply.
      (4)   Failure to comply within 15 days of notification of registration
required, the owner shall be guilty of a misdemeanor. Fines and/or court costs
will not excuse or replace payment of fees required.
   (C)   Owner, resident. Any owner of a vacant building residing outside of
the state shall provide the name and address of a person who resides within the
state who is authorized to accept service of process and notices of fees due
under this section on behalf of the owner, and who is designated as a
responsible, local party or agent for the purposes of notification in the event
of an emergency affecting the public health, safety, or welfare.
   (D)   Challenging a determination. A property owner may challenge any
determination made pursuant to this section in the City Municipal Court, and
that determination may be appealed to the Circuit Court of the county.
   (E)   Civil action. The municipality shall have the authority to institute a
civil action against the property owner and/or file a lien on real property for
unpaid and delinquent vacant building registration fees as provided for in W.
Va. Code § 8-12-16c.
   (F)   Maintenance. Owners shall maintain the vacant building or property to
a standard deemed reasonable by the governing body. The city may, following
notice to the owner, act in Municipal Court to bring the vacant building or
property into compliance with the standards, or otherwise eliminate the public
nuisance caused by any non-compliant conditions; provided, that nothing in this
section is to be interpreted to impose a duty, obligation, or requirement that
a municipality must undertake such repairs, demolition, or maintenance measures
which remain as obligations and responsibilities of the owner. Cost of the
repairs, demolition, and maintenance and related legal and administrative costs
incurred by the municipality are to be paid by the owner. Collection of these
costs may be enforced in civil proceedings against the owner.
   (G)   Collection of fees. The City Recorder shall deposit the fees collected
equally into the Community Improvement Fund, police account, and fire fee
account:
      (1)   For the purpose to improve public safety efforts, especially for
police and fire personnel, who most often contend with the dangerous situations
manifested in vacant properties;
      (2)   To monitor and administer this section; and
      (3)   Repair, close, or demolish a vacant structure.(W. Va. Code § 8-12-
16c) (Prior Code, § 5-300)
Editor’s note:
   This section was revised by the city on November 16, 2015.
§ 5-301 REGISTRATION OF UNINHABITABLE PROPERTY.
   (A)    The Mayor of the city, with approval of the Council, may appoint a
Code Enforcement Officer to investigate and determine whether real property
violates provisions of the applicable building code of the municipality.
   (B)   (1)   An owner of real property improved by a structure that is
uninhabitable and violates the applicable building code adopted by the
municipality is subject to a registration fee, and shall be assessed a fee of
$500 and additional fee of $1,000 each year thereafter such violation
continues.
      (2)   OWNER or PROPERTY OWNER means a person who individually or jointly
with others:
         (a)   Has legal title to the property, with or without actual
possession of the property;
         (b)   Has charge, care, or control of the property as owner or agent
of the owner;
         (c)   Is an executor, administrator, trustee, or guardian of the
estate of the owner;
         (d)   Is the agent of the owner for the purpose of managing,
controlling, or collecting rents; or
         (e)   Is entitled to control or direct the management or disposition
of the property.
   (C)   After inspecting the property, if the officer determines the property
is uninhabitable and violates the applicable Building Code, then:
      (1)   The officer shall post a written notice on the property, which
shall include:
         (a)   An explanation of the violation(s);
         (b)   A description of the registration;
         (c)    The date the fee will be assessed;
         (d)   An explanation of how to be removed from the registration;
         (e)   An explanation of the appeals process; and
         (f)   A statement that if the fee is not paid, then the property is
subject to forfeiture.
      (2)   Within five business days of the inspection and the posting of the
property, the officer shall, by certified mail, send a copy of the notice that
was posted to the owner(s) of the property at the last known address according
to the county property tax records.
   (D)   Within 45 days of receipt of the notification by the owner(s), the
property owner may:
      (1)   Make and complete any repairs to the property that violate the
applicable Building Code; or
      (2)   Provide written information to the officer showing that repairs are
forthcoming in a reasonable period of time.
   (E)   After the repairs are made, the owner may request a re-inspection of
the property to ensure compliance with the applicable Building Code. If the
officer finds the violations are fixed, the owner is not subject to the
registration and no fee will be incurred.
   (F)   The officer may re-inspect the property at any time to determine where
in the process the repairs fall.
   (G)   Within 90 days of receipt of the notification by the owner(s), the
property owner has the right to appeal the decision of the officer to the
Municipal Court.
   (H)   If an appeal is not filed within 90 days, the property is registered
and the fee is assessed to the owner(s) on the date specified in the notice.
The notice of the fee shall be recorded in the office of the Clerk of the
County Commission of the county where the property is located and if different,
in the office of the Clerk of the County Commission of the county where the
property is assessed for real property taxes.
   (I)   If the enforcement agency affirms the registration and assessment of
the registration fee, the property owner has the right to appeal the decision
of the enforcement agency to the Circuit Court within 30 days of the decision.
If the decision is not appealed in a timely manner to the Circuit Court, then
the property is registered and the fee is assessed on the date specified in the
notice. The notice of the fee shall be recorded in the office of the Clerk of
the County Commission of the county where the property is located and if
different, in the office of the Clerk of the County Commission of the county
where the property is assessed for real property taxes.
   (J)   A fee assessed under this section shall be recorded in the same manner
as a lien is recorded in the office of the Clerk of the County Commission.
   (K)   If the fee is paid, then the municipality shall record a release of
the fee in the office of the Clerk of the County Commission of the county where
the property is located and if different, in the office of the Clerk of the
County Commission of the county where the property is assessed for real
property taxes.
   (L)   If an owner fails to pay the fee, then the officer shall annually post
the written notice on the property and send the written notice to the owner(s)
by certified mail.
   (M)   If a registration fee remains delinquent for two years from the date
it was placed on record in the Clerk of the County Commission in which the
property is located and assessed, the municipality may take action to receive
the subject property by means of forfeiture. Should the municipality take the
steps necessary to receive the subject property, the municipality then becomes
the owner of record and takes the property, subject to all liens and real and
personal property taxes.
   (N)   The City Recorder shall deposit the fees collected equally into the
Community Improvement Fund, police account, and fire fee account.(W. Va. Code §
8-12-16a) (Prior Code, § 5-301)
Editor’s note:
   This section was revised by the city on November 16, 2015.
