§ 8-201 ADVERTISING BY OUTDOOR BILLBOARDS OR SIGNS.
   Every person engaged in the business of outdoor advertising by billboards or
signs within this municipality shall pay an annual license fee of $100. (Prior
Code, § 8-18)
§ 8-202 AUCTIONEERS.
   Every person carrying on the business of auctioneer shall pay an annual
license fee of $15. (Prior Code, § 8-19)
§ 8-203 BOWLING LANES AND BILLIARD, POOL, BAGETELLE TABLES.
   The annual license fee to keep or maintain a bowling lane, a billiard, pool,
or bagetelle table, or a table of like kind, for public use, where any charge
is made for the use thereof, shall be $25, but, if more than one such lanes or
tables be kept or maintained in the same building by the same person, the fee
shall be $25 for the first one and $15 for each additional one. (Prior Code, §
8-20)
§ 8-204 BROKERS AND REAL ESTATE DEALERS.
   (A)   The annual license fee to practice the business of stock and
securities broker, or broker other than pawnbroker, by buying and selling for
others stocks, securities, or property, for commission, compensation, or
reward, shall be $50.
   (B)   The annual license fee to practice the business of real estate broker
shall be $50. The annual license fee to practice the business of real estate
salesperson shall be $25. The term REAL ESTATE BROKER, within the meaning of
this section, shall include all persons, partnerships, associations, and
corporations who, for a fee, commission, or compensation, or who with the
intention or expectation of receiving or collecting said fee, commission, or
compensation, lists, sells, purchases, exchanges, rents, manages, leases,
auctions, negotiates, attempts to negotiate, or assists in the procuring of a
purchaser of real estate.
   (C)   The term REAL ESTATE SALESPERSON shall mean and include any person
employed or engaged by a licensed real estate broker to do or deal in any
activity listed in this section for a fee, commission, or compensation.
   (D)   Neither the term REAL ESTATE BROKER nor REAL ESTATE SALESPERSON shall
be held to include any person, partnership, association, or corporation, who,
as a bona fide owner or lessor, shall perform any aforementioned act.
   (E)   This section shall not apply to licensed practicing attorneys who, in
the normal course of their profession, are acting in behalf of clients. (Prior
Code, § 8-21)
§ 8-205 COIN OPERATED MERCHANDISE, SERVICES, MUSIC, AMUSEMENT, AND THE LIKE
DEVICES.
   (A)   Persons owning and operating coin-operated merchandise, service,
music, amusement, or vending machines shall obtain annual licenses and pay the
fees prescribed in this section. The liability for the licensee to operate any
type of coin-operated merchandise, service, amusement, music, or vending
machines shall be upon the owner of the machine. The leasing of such a machine
shall not be considered as a transfer of ownership. Where a leasor-leasee
relationship exists, the leasor shall be liablefor the applicable license and
fee.
   (B)   The annual license fee to own and operate a coin-operated baggage or
parcel checking device, which is used for the storage of baggage or parcels or
any character, shall be $0.50 for each section of any such device which is
operated on the coin-in-the-slot principle; the annual license fee to own and
operate any coin-operated toilet locker or device, sanitary napkin device, or
bed vibrator device shall be $0.50 for each such locker or device. The
municipality shall not furnish decal stamps for these devices; however, the
owner shall identify each machine by installing on each device an
identification label, plainly legible and visible, in such a manner that the
machine need not be moved to observe the identification label, and the
identification label shall contain the name of the owner, his or her license
owner, and his or her address within the municipality.
   (C)   The annual license fee to own and operate a total of 20 or more coin-
operated merchandise, service, amusement, or music devices of the following
types shall be: $0.01 devices, $50; $0.05 devices, $150; $0.10 devices, $250;
over $0.10 devices, $300. The operator of more than one type of such devices
shall pay the highest fee prescribed. The annual license fee to own and operate
less than 20 amusement or music devices shall be upon a per-device basis as
follows: $0.01 devices, $2; $0.05 devices, $5; $0.10 devices, $10; over $0.10
devices, $12.50. Any device taking more than one denomination of coin shall be
licensed on the basis of the largest denomination of coin taken, or the total
of the coins necessary to make the device function or operate.
   (D)   The aforementioned fees are not proratable if taken out during the
license year, nor shall paid fees be refundable if a license is revoked,
suspended, or if the business ceased during the license year.
   (E)   The provisions of this section shall not be applicable to any pay
telephone, postage stamp vending machines, or currency changing machines
operated on the coin-in-the-slot principle.
   (F)   No license fee shall be required of persons keeping or maintaining
such machines or devices owned by them in their own licensed stores, except
where the principal business of the store is the operation of such machines and
devices. Any person exempt from such license, however, shall obtain from the
Municipal Recorder a license receipt, at a cost not to exceed $0.50 each,
showing that he or she is exempt. To obtain such license exemption, he or she
shall make an affidavit and produce such other evidence showing him or her to
be entitled to an exemption as the Municipal Recorder may require. Such
affidavit and evidence shall be on a form to be prescribed by the Municipal
Recorder.
   (G)   The owner of a coin-operated merchandise, service, amusement, music,
or a vending machine is liable for the payment of the license fee and, upon his
or her refusal or failure to pay such fee, the Municipal Recorder, or his or
her agents, may take such machine or device into possession and deliver it to
the Chief of Police, or the Chief of Police on his or her own initiative or
upon the order of the Municipal Recorder, or his or her agents, may take such
machine or device into possession. In either event, such machine or device
shall be impounded until such license fee is paid. In the event the license fee
and penalties are not paid to the Municipal Recorder within ten days after the
date of impounding, then the Chief of Police shall sell such machine or device
in the manner provided by law for the sale of personal property for taxes. The
proceeds from such a sale shall be used to pay the license fee and penalties
due on such a machine or device, and the Chief of Police’s costs, including
cost of impounding and storage. The balance, if there is one, shall be
forfeited to the city. (Prior Code, § 8-22)
§ 8-206 SAME: NON-PROFIT ORGANIZATIONS.
   No license fee shall be required under the provisions of §
8-205 of any person keeping or maintaining within the municipality any coin-in-
the-slot machines or devices which are not gambling devices under the laws of
this state if the owner, operator, or sponsor of such machines or devices
attaches to his or her license application the affidavit of the chief official
of a non-stock corporation or non-profit organization, stating that:
   (A)   Not less than 20% of the gross receipts from such machines or devices
are payable to the non-stock corporation or non-profit organization;
   (B)   The gross receipts paid to such non-stock corporation or non-profit
organization shall be used solely for benevolent, patriotic, civic,
educational, or philanthropic purposes; and
   (C)   The execution of the affidavit has been authorized by a duly
constituted meeting of the trustees, directors, or members of such non-stock
corporation or non-profit organization. (Prior Code, § 8-23)
§ 8-207 COLLECTION AGENCIES.
   (A)   The annual license fee to engage in the business of a collection
agency shall be $100. Each applicant for such a license shall file with the
Municipal Recorder a continuing surety bond in the form prescribed by the
Municipal Recorder. Each bond shall be in the amount of $5,000, conditioned
that such agency or its agent will pay all damages resulting from any unlawful
act or action by such agency in connection with the conduct of the business.
   (B)   Within this section, COLLECTION AGENCY shall mean all persons, firms,
corporations, and associations directly or indirectly engaged in the business
of soliciting from, or collecting from, others any account, bill, or
indebtedness due or asserted to be owed or due another person. (Prior Code, §
8-24)
§ 8-208 EMPLOYMENT AGENTS; EXEMPTION.
   (A)   (1)   The annual license fee to conduct the business of an employment
agent to receive applications for employment, and to hire or contract with
persons for employment, shall be $200.
      (2)   The annual license fee for an agency or registry used for
employment of registered professional nurses, practical nurses, or
undergraduate nurses shall be $25, provided that the provisions of this section
shall not be applicable to any agency or registry operated by a professional
registered nurses association for the benefits of its registrants and not for
profit.
   (B)   The term EMPLOYMENT AGENT, within this section, shall mean and include
all persons, firms, corporations, church, and charitable associations, which
furnish, to persons seeking employment, information enabling or tending to
enable them to secure such employment, or which furnish, to employers seeking
laborers, information enabling or tending to enable them to secure such
laborers, or shall keep a register of persons seeking employment. (Prior Code,
§ 8-25)
§ 8-209 FORTUNE TELLING.
   The annual license to act as a fortune teller, palmist, phrenologist,
spiritualist, medium, clairvoyant, mind reader, or any other person who
performs the art or profession of telling the past or forecasting the future
shall be $200. Persons who perform said art or profession as a non-profit basis
shall be exempt from the above license. (Prior Code, § 8-26)
§ 8-210 HAWKERS AND PEDDLERS; EXEMPTIONS.
   (A)   Definitions. For the purpose of this section, the following
definitions shall apply unless the context clearly indicates or requires a
different meaning.
      HAWKER AND PEDDLER. Any person, either principal or agent, whether a
resident of the city or not, who travels by foot, wagon, automobile, vehicle,
or any other type of conveyance, from town to town, or from place to place,
selling or bartering, or carrying for sale or barter, or exposing therefor, any
goods, wares, or merchandise, or foodstuffs or beverages, offering and exposing
the same for sale or making sales and delivering articles to inerrant/
purchasers either on foot or from animal, cart, or vehicle, or any parson who
travels from town to town, or place to place in the same town, offering to
perform personal services for household repairs and improvements, or solicits
or induces any person to sign any contracts relating to household repairs and
improvements, including, but not limited to, contracts for replacements,
improvements, or installation.
      ITINERANT MERCHANT/TRANSIENT MERCHANT or ITINERANT VENDOR. Any person,
firm, or corporation, whether as owner, agent, consignee, or employee, and
whether a resident of the municipality or not, who, for the purpose of carrying
on such business who engages temporarily within the municipality, in any public
or quasi-public place, including, but not limited to, a hotel, motel, rooming
house, store room, building, part of a building, tent, vacant lot, railroad
car, vehicle, or trailer, temporarily occupied for the purpose of making retail
sales of goods to the public in the business of selling and delivering goods,
wares, and merchandise, or taking orders for future delivery for goods,
merchandise, or services, offering to perform personal services for household
repairs and improvements, or solicits or induces any person to sign any
contracts relating to household repairs and improvements, including, but not
limited to, contracts for replacements, improvements, or installation to or at
homes, apartments, or other residential premises in the municipality.
      MOBILE FOOD VENDING UNIT. A food service establishment within a vacant
lot, table, tent, pushcart, vehicle, or towed type vehicle used to store,
prepare, display, service, or sell food or drink, or distribute it free of
charge for consumption in a place other than in or on the unit.
      MOBILE FOOD VENDOR/ITINERANT FOOD VENDER. Any person, firm, or
corporation, whether as owner, agent, consignee, or employee, and whether a
resident of the municipality or not, engages temporarily within the
municipality in the business of selling and delivering food or drink, or
distributes it free of charge from a mobile food vending unit in any public,
private, or restricted place.
   (B)   License required. No person shall engage in the business of a hawker,
peddler, itinerant vendor, mobile food vendor, solicitor, canvasser, or
salesperson within the city unless a license has been obtained to do so.
   (C)   Location. No peddler or itinerant shall have any exclusive right to
any location, nor shall he or she be permitted to operate in any congested area
where his or her operations might impede or inconvenience the public. For the
purpose of this section, the judgment of a police officer or the Mayor,
exercised in good faith, shall be deemed conclusive as to whether the area is
congested or the public impeded or inconvenienced.
   (D)   Time restrictions. No person shall sell, offer for sale, hawk, or
peddle in the city any of the items listed unless the time for sale is found to
be reasonable and within the hours established in the license for the sale of
these items.
   (E)   Compliance with other laws. Nothing contained within this section
shall, in any way, exempt any applicant from compliance with all state,
federal, county, and municipal statutes, ordinances, and regulations,
including, but not limited to, W. Va. Code §§ 11-12-20 et seq., and law
relating to taxation, public health, consumer protection, licensing, and the
like.
   (F)   Exemptions. The following persons are hereby exempt from the
provisions of this article.
      (1)   Any person that is organized and operated exclusively for
religious, educational, philanthropic, benevolent, fraternal, or charitable
purposes not operated for pecuniary profit, where no part of the net earnings
inures to the benefit of any person, shareholder, or individual, or where the
solicitation, sale, or delivery shall be conducted within an organization and
only among the members thereof.
      (2)   Any person defined in this article that is employed by or
represents a business, firm, or corporation which is located within the city
limits, who is otherwise licensed under the general store licensing provisions
of the city.
      (3)   Commercial travelers or selling agents who sell only to entities
who purchase tangible personal property for purpose of resale to others.
      (4)   FARMERS MARKET, which means any person selling agricultural
products grown or produced in the county or adjacent state counties, from a
parked motor vehicle or temporary stand on the days, and at the times and
locations specified for farmers market by Council.
      (5)   State, county, and municipal fairs, festivals, and carnivals which
are community sponsored and approved by the municipality.
   (G)   Application and fee for license.
      (1)   A hawker, peddler, itinerant vendor, mobile food vendor, solicitor,
canvasser, or salesperson prior to transacting any business within the
corporation boundaries must appear at City Hall, and apply for and obtain a
license, entitled “solicitor’s license,” by written application. Such person
shall state his or her full name, address, Social Security number, telephone
number, driver’s license number, motor vehicle make, model, color, and license
number, and if applicable, the applicant’s state transient vendor business
registration certificate number and date thereof, such certificate being
required by W. Va. Code § 11-12-20; the nature of the goods, services,
contracts, and the like to be sold or offered for sale; and any other
reasonable and pertinent license information.
      (2)   (a)   The fee for a solicitor’s license shall be $25 for a one
time, one day license.
         (b)   The fee for a solicitor’s license shall be $50 for a one-month
license.
         (c)   The fee for a solicitor’s license shall be $200 for a six-month
license.
         (d)   A $10 application fee shall be included as an administrative fee
on all licenses.
      (3)   A $250 bond, at the discretion of the City Recorder, may be
required before a license shall be issued. Such deposit shall be held by the
City Recorder for a period of 90 days after such person ceases to do business
within the city, and after satisfying all claims which shall be made against
him or her. The City Recorder shall, after a written request has been made,
return such deposit or such portion thereof as remains in his or her hands to
the person who deposited it.
   (H)   License to be carried and displayed. The transient vendor shall keep
the business registration certificate in his or her possession at all times
when conducting business within this municipality. He or she shall publicly
display the certificate whenever conducting business in this city. A licensee
shall be posted conspicuously in a place of business or, in the case of
transient merchants, in some other conspicuous place, or carry his or her
current valid license upon his or her person and shall display such license to
any consumer, law officer, or city official if requested to do so.
   (I)   Penalty. Any person engaging in or carrying out any business activity,
trade, or employment for which a license is required by the terms of this
article, whether without obtaining a license therefor before commencing the
same, or by continuing the same after the termination of the effective period
of any such license, shall be fined not less than $50 or more than $500, plus
the cost of the appropriate solicitor’s license. Each day’s continuation of
such violation shall constitute a separate offense. (Prior Code, § 8-27)
§ 8-211 HOTELS AND RESTAURANTS.
   The annual license fee to operate the business of a hotel or motel shall be
$2, and an additional $0.25 shall be charged for each bedroom in excess of
seven such bedrooms. The annual fee for the operation of a restaurant shall be
$2, and an additional $0.25 shall be charged for each five chairs or stools, or
spaces, where persons are fed in excess of ten. No fee, however, for a hotel,
motel, or restaurant shall exceed $10. (Prior Code, § 8-28)
§ 8-212 JUNK DEALERS AND THEIR AGENTS.
   (A)   Definitions. For the purpose of this section, the following
definitions shall apply unless the context clearly indicates or requires a
different meaning.
      JUNK. Old or scrap gold, copper, brass, rope, rags, batteries, paper,
rubber, automobile parts, iron, steel, and other old scrap ferrous or non-
ferrous metals.
      JUNK DEALER’S AGENT. All persons who buy or sell junk for, or on behalf
of, a junk dealer, but the term JUNK DEALER’S AGENT shall not be construed to
include any persons regularly employed upon a salary by a regularly licensed
junk dealer engaged in such business within the city.
      ITINERANT JUNK COLLECTOR. Such persons who gather junk from place to
place with the aid of a cart or vehicle, hand drawn or propelled, who have no
fixed place of business.
      NON-RESIDENT JUNK DEALER or NON-RESIDENT JUNK DEALER’S AGENT. All persons
who act as junk dealers, or junk dealer’s agents, who are non-residents of the
municipality, and who buy or solicit for the purchase of junk within the
municipality.
   (B)   Annual license. The annual license to act as a resident junk dealer
shall be $25; to act as a junk dealer’s agent, $10; to act as a itinerant junk
collector, $2; to act as a non-resident junk dealer or non-resident junk
dealer’s agent, $150.
   (C)   Non-resident junk dealers, agents. Any non-resident junk dealer, or
his or her agent, may/may not purchase junk from a resident junk dealer without
complying with the provisions of this section. (Prior Code, § 8-29)
§ 8-213 PAWNBROKERS.
   The annual license fee to engage in the business of pawnbroker shall be
$100. The term PAWNBROKER shall include any person, firm, partnership,
association, or corporation engaged in the business of lending, money on
deposit or pledge of personal property or other valuable thing, other than
securities or printed evidence of indebtedness, or in the business of
purchasing personal property for the purpose of reducing or smelting such
property into any form different from their condition or construction when
purchased and reselling or marketing the product. (Prior Code, § 8-30)
§ 8-314 STORES.
   (A)   For the purpose of this section, the term SPECIAL STORE shall mean and
include any store or any mercantile establishment in which goods, wares, or
merchandise or any kind, except cigarettes, tobacco products, or soft drinks,
are purchased, ordered, sold, or offered for sale, either at retail or
wholesale, and which contains no coin-operated device(s) owned and operated by
the store proprietor. The term GENERAL STORE shall mean and include any store
(s) or any mercantile establishment(s) in which goods, wares, or merchandise of
any kind are purchased, ordered, sold, or offered for sale, either at retail or
wholesale. Within this section, no coin-operated device or devices shall be
construed to be a store.
   (B)   Every person establishing, operating, or maintaining one or more
general stores within the city under the same general management, supervision,
or ownership shall pay an annual license fee of $15 per store. Every person
establishing, operating, or maintaining one or more special stores within the
city under the same general management, supervision, or ownership shall pay an
annual license fee of $5 per store.
   (C)   The establishment, operation, or maintenance of stores by the
following shall be exempt from the license fee imposed by this article:
      (1)   The United States of America, the state, and its political
subdivisions;
      (2)   Religious or charitable organizations; and
      (3)   Any person(s) engaged within the city in the business of producing
agricultural products who, individually or collectively, sell in such store
only agricultural products which he, she, or they have produced. (Prior Code, §
8-31)
§ 8-315 THEATRES AND PUBLIC SHOWS.
   The annual license fee to keep or maintain a theater, opera house, or other
permanent place for public shows shall be $20 and $10 for such place that
operates less than four days each week. (Prior Code, § 8-32)
§ 8-316 THEATRICAL PERFORMANCES.
   The annual license fee to exhibit to the public any theatrical performance,
other than one exhibited by the holder of a license under the provisions of §
8-315, shall be $5 per week or fraction of a week. This section shall not apply
to performances given by amateurs, educational institutions, or non-profit
literary, dramatic, benevolent, religious, or patriotic organizations. (Prior
Code, § 8-33)

ARTICLE 3: PROPERTY TAXES AND OTHER TAXES

§ 8-301 PROPERTY TAX; CLASSES OF TAXABLE PROPERTY.
   This municipality shall have the authority to tax real and personal property
within the municipal boundaries at its true and actual value for each of the
following three classes of property:
 
Class of Property
          All tangible personal property exclusively in agriculture, including
          horticulture and grazing; all products of agriculture (including
Class I   livestock) while owned by the producer; all monies, and all notes,
          bonds, bills and accounts receivable, stocks, and any other tangible
          property.
          All property owned, used, and occupied by the owner exclusively for
Class II  residential purposes; all farms, including land used for horticulture
          and grazing, occupied and cultivated by their owners or bona fide
          tenants.
          Property that includes all real and personal property situated
Class III outside of municipalities exclusive of Classes I and II and is
          therefore not taxable by this municipality.
Class IV  All real and personal property situated inside of municipalities
          exclusive of Classes I and II.
(Prior Code, § 8-35)
§ 8-302 MAXIMUM PROPERTY TAX LEVY RATES; EXCESS LEVY.
   (A)   The maximum property tax levy rates for each property class per $100
valuation that can be assessed without requiring a vote from the electorate
are:
 
Class I Class II Class IV
12.50   0.25     0.50
 
   (B)   This municipality may impose an excess levy lasting up to three years
for a special or general purpose if such a levy is approved by at least 60% of
the votes cast in the special levy election. The maximum rates for each $100 of
assessed value are:
 
Class I Class II Class IV
6.25    12.50    0.25
 
   (C)   The Council, being of the opinion that the maximum levies for the
current expenses will not provide sufficient funds for the payment of the
current expenses of the city, including expenditures for the purposes
hereinafter set forth, and that an election should be held to increase such
levies, it is hereby ordered:
      (1)   The purpose for which additional funds are needed is as follows: To
resurface streets.
      (2)   (a)   The approximate total amount for said purpose is $21,129;
         (b)   The separate and aggregate assessed valuation of each class of
taxable property within the city, a municipality, is for the year 1973 as
follows: Class I, $463,950; Class II, $1,599; Class IV, $2,174,430; and
aggregate, $4,237,430;
         (c)   The proposed additional rate of .levy in cents on each class of
property is as follows: Class I, 6.25; Class II, 12.5; and Class IV, 0.25; and
         (d)   The proposed years to which the additional levy shall apply are
the fiscal years beginning July 1, 1974, July l, 1975, and July 1, 1976.
      (3)   The question of such additional levy shall be submitted to a vote
at a special election to be held on March 12, 1974;
      (4)   Notice calling such election shall be given by publication of this
order at least once each week for two successive weeks before said election in
the “Pennsboro News,” a newspaper of general circulation in the territory in
which the election is held. Printed copies of this order shall also be posted
at each place of voting at least ten days before said election. All the
provisions of the laws concerning general elections shall apply as far as they
are practicable, except that a separate ballot shall be used at such election
when held in connection with any other election; and
      (5)   The ballot to be used at such election shall be in form as follows:
 
“Special election to authorize additional levies for the fiscal years beginning
July 1, 1974, July 1, 1975, and July 1, 1976, and for the purpose of resurfacing
streets, according to order of the Council of the City of Pennsboro entered on
the 19th day of February 1974.
 
   The additional levy shall be on Class I Property, 6.25; on Class II Property,
12.5; on Class IV Property, 0.25.
 
For the Levies   ( )
 
Against the Levies   ( )”
 
(Prior Code, § 8-36)
§ 8-303 PRESERVATION OF PRIOR TAXING POWERS OF CITIES.
   This city may include, by Charter provision and may continue to exercise,
all powers of taxation, other than property taxation, which were set forth in
the Special Legislation Charter of this city in effect on the date of
ratification of the municipal home rule amendment. (Prior Code, § 8-37)
§ 8-304 PUBLIC UTILITIES TAX.
   (A)   This municipality shall have the power to levy and collect an excise
tax on the privilege of purchasing or using, within this municipality, public
utility services and tangible personal property from public utilities. The
purchaser shall pay to the public utilities the amount of the tax levied, not
exceeding 2% of the gross sale which shall be added to the cost, and shall be
collected by said public utility who shall give account to this municipality.
   (B)   This section for such a tax shall also include a uniform way for the
collecting of such levies and the method of payment and accountability
provided, that the tax authorized by this section shall not take place unless
said public utility is notified, in writing, 60 days in advance; provided, that
this tax shall not be imposed on coin operated phones a specific charge for
telephone calls to points outside the municipality. (Prior Code, § 8-38)
§ 8-305 AMUSEMENT TAX.
   (A)   For the purpose of this section, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
      ADMISSION CHARGE. Any charge for the right or the privilege to enter any
place; it shall include a charge made for season tickets or subscriptions, a
minimum service charge, a cover charge, or a charge made for the use of seats
and tables, reserved or otherwise, and similar accomodations. It shall include
charges for the rental of property or the rendering of service unless persons
not utilizing such property or services are admitted free; and if a lesser
charge is made to persons not utilizing such property or services, the lesser
charge shall constitute the admission charge. The term ADMISSION CHARGE shall
also include all parking charges where the charge is determined by the number
of passengers in an automobile.
      CITY CLERK. The collector of city taxes for the City of Pennsboro, State
of West Virginia.
      PERSON. An individual, firm, corporation company, partnership,
association, and unincorporated association, and any person acting in a
fiduciary capacity.
      PLACE. Includes circuses, dance halls, auditoriums, stadiums, athletic
pavilions, exhibition halls, amusement parks, golf courses and golf ranges,
night clubs, cabarets, theatres of all kinds, lecture halls, archery and
shooting ranges, autoracing, movie theaters, swimming pools, bowling alleys,
skating rinks, and all kinds of places where any form of diversion, recreation,
sport, or pastime is offered or provided.
   (B)   There is hereby imposed and levied upon every person who pays an
admission charge to any place located within the limits of the city a tax of 2%
on each admission charge, except those who are admitted free of charge.
   (C)   The tax levied by this section shall not be applicable to admission
charges to be used exclusively for charitable, eleemosynary, educational, or
religious purposes, or school events.
   (D)   Every person receiving an admission charge, upon which a tax is levied
under this section, shall collect the amount of tax imposed upon the person
paying an admission charge. Said tax shall be deemed to be held in trust by the
person required to collect the same until remitted to the City Clerk as
hereinafter provided. The tax imposed under this section shall be collected at
the time the admission charge is paid.
   (E)   Every person collecting any tax imposed by this section shall, on or
before the fifteenth day of each month, file with the City Clerk a statement
upon forms provided by the City Clerk indicating the amount of taxes collected
by such person during the preceding calendar month, and such further
information as the City Clerk may deem necessary to determine the amount of the
tax collected and payable. A remittance for the amount of the tax collected
during said preceding calendar month shall accompany the statement.
   (F)   Every person required to collect a tax imposed by this section who
fails to collect the same or fails to remit the tax shall be personally liable
to the city for the amount of the tax. Any person required to collect and remit
the tax imposed by this section who fails to remit the amount of the tax when
due, in addition to all other penalties, pay a penalty of 5% of the amount due
for each month thereafter elapsing, and before payment there shall be added an
additional penalty of 5%.
   (G)   The price (exclusive of the taxes to be paid by the person paying for
admission) at which every admission ticket or card is sold shall be
conspicuously and indelibly printed, written, or stamped on the face or back of
that part of the ticket which is taken up by the management of the place to
which admission is granted.
   (H)   Every person paying an admission charge to a temporary or transient
place, as defined in division (A) above, shall also be subject to the tax
levied by this section, and every person operating or conducting such a
temporary or transient place shall collect and remit such tax as hereinafter
provided.
   (I)   Prior to conducting such a temporary or transient place, a permit
shall first be obtained from the City Clerk. Every person conducting such
temporary or transient place shall file a statement and remittance covering the
taxes collected on the day following the conclusion of operations, or at such
reasonable time or times as the City Clerk shall determine; provided, however,
that before a permit shall be issued under this section, the applicant for the
same shall deposit with the City Clerk a sum of money, or bond in lieu thereof,
conditioned upon the faithful compliance with the provisions of this section in
an amount to be determined by the City Clerk as sufficient to cover the amounts
which shall become due and owing the city upon the conclusion of temporary or
transient operations.
   (J)   If any person required to collect and remit the tax imposed by this
section fails to file a statement and a remittance, or if the City Clerk has
reasonable cause to believe that an erroneous statement has been filed, the
City Clerk may proceed to determine the amount due to the city, and in
connection therewith shall make investigations and take such testimony and
other evidence as may be necessary; provided, however, that notice and
opportunity to be heard be given any person who may become liable for the
amount owing prior to any determination by the City Clerk.
   (K)   The City Clerk shall have power to adopt rules and regulations not
inconsistent with the provisions of this section for the purpose of carrying
out and enforcing the payment, collection, and remittance of the tax herein
levied; and a copy of such rules and regulations shall be on file and available
for public examination in the City Clerk’s office. Failure or refusal to comply
with any rules and regulations promulgated under this section shall be deemed a
violation of this section.
   (L)   Every person who willfully violates any of the provisions of this
section shall be guilty of a misdemeanor, and upon conviction thereof shall be
liable to a fine or penalty of not less than $50 nor more than $200, or by
imprisonment in the county jail not to exceed ten days, or by both such fine
and imprisonment for each offense. (Prior Code, § 8-39)
§ 8-306 TAX ON PURCHASES OF INTOXICATING LIQUORS IN MUNICIPALITIES; PRIVATE
CLUB FEES.
   (A)   This municipality shall have the power to levy and collect a tax upon
the purchases of intoxicating liquors from the Alcohol Beverage Control
Commission within such municipality. Provided, that this municipality shall not
levy or collect any tax on the intoxicating liquors sold by or purchased from
holders of a license. This tax shall be levied upon the purchaser and shall be
added to, and collected with, the price of purchase. The tax shall not exceed
3% of the purchase price.
   (B)   A copy of this section, to impose such a tax sale, must be certified
by the Mayor and sent to the State Alcohol Beverage Control Commission, who
shall collect all taxes and redistribute them back to this municipality at a
quarterly rate.
   (C)   This municipality also has the power to tax private clubs within the
city limits. The maximum tax for each club is: non-profit social clubs, $375;
private clubs, with less than 1,000 members $500; and private clubs, and more
than 1,000 members, $1,250. (Prior Code, § 8-40)
§ 8-307 LICENSE TAX ON HORSE RACING AND DOG RACING.
   (A)   This municipality shall have the power to impose a daily tax on any
horse or dog racing track within the city limits.
   (B)   Such tax shall not exceed that which is imposed by the state for the
daily operation of said track.
   (C)   Such tax shall not be applicable to any affair in which horse or dog
racing is conducted for not more than six days. (Prior Code, § 8-41)
§ 8-308 MOTOR VEHICLE OPERATOR’S TAX.
   This municipality shall have the power to levy and collect an annual motor
vehicle operator’s license tax not to exceed $2. This tax shall only apply to
inhabitants of this municipality. (Prior Code, § 8-42)
§ 8-309 DOMESTIC ANIMAL TAX.
   This municipality shall have the power to levy and collect an annual license
tax upon the privilege of keeping a domestic animal within the corporate limits
of this municipality. (Prior Code, § 8-43)
ARTICLE 4: BUDGETING
Section
   
8-401   Budget meeting by Municipal Council
   
8-402   Submission of levy estimate to State Tax Commission
   
8-403   Publication of levy estimate
   
8-404   Audit and review by Tax Commissioner
   
8-405   Laying the levy
   
8-406   Revisions of levy estimate during the fiscal year
   
8-407   General revenue sharing planned use report
   
8-408   Coal severance tax; budgeting
§ 8-401 BUDGET MEETING BY MUNICIPAL COUNCIL.
   (A)   No later than between March 7 and March 28 of each year, this
Municipal Council shall meet to construct the municipal budget (levy estimate)
for the next fiscal year.
   (B)   During this period, this Municipal Council shall identify its
projected revenues and expenditures for the coming year, and prepare the levy
estimate on the forms and in accordance with the system of accounts required by
the State Tax Commissioner. (Prior Code, § 8-44)
§ 8-402 SUBMISSION OF LEVY ESTIMATE TO STATE TAX COMMISSION.
   No later than March 29, this Municipal Council must mail or deliver two
copies of the completed budget (levy estimate) to the State Tax Commissioner.
(Prior Code, § 8-45)
§ 8-403 PUBLICATION OF LEVY ESTIMATE.
   (A)   On or before March 29, the municipality shall begin publication of the
levy estimate. It shall be published once a week for two successive weeks in
two newspapers of general circulation and of opposite politics published in the
area.
   (B)   If there is only one such newspaper, it shall be published in that
one. If there is no such newspaper, the levy estimate shall be published in the
most widely read newspaper in the municipality. (Prior Code, § 8-46)
§ 8-404 AUDIT AND REVIEW BY TAX COMMISSIONER.
   The Tax Commissioner will audit and review the levy estimate prior to the
third Tuesday in April. The Commissioner will notify the Municipal Council by
letter of the results of his or her audit, and review and request for any
change. (Prior Code, § 8-47)
§ 8-405 LAYING THE LEVY.
   This Municipal Council shall meet on the third Tuesday in April to
officially lay the levy. This entails the hearing of objectives and the
adopting of the levy rates to be used during the next fiscal year. (Prior Code,
§ 8-48)
§ 8-406 REVISIONS OF LEVY ESTIMATE DURING THE FISCAL YEAR.
   Changes in the municipal budget which result in a change in the balance of
any department or unclassified line item, or a change in the amount of revenue
from any source, shall be submitted in letter form to the Tax Commissioner for
his or her written approval. (Prior Code, § 8-49)
§ 8-407 GENERAL REVENUE SHARING PLANNED USE REPORT.
   As a supplement to the levy estimate, this municipality shall submit to the
State Tax Commissioner a planned use report for funds to be received from
general revenue sharing. This report shall be submitted on the forms and in
accordance with the system of accounts provided by the State Tax Department.
(Prior Code, § 8-50)
§ 8-408 COAL SEVERANCE TAX; BUDGETING.
   (A)   This municipality shall create a Coal Severance Tax Revenue Fund,
which shall be the depository for monies distributed to this municipality under
the provisions of the State Code. Monies in such Coal Severance Tax Revenue
Funds may be expended by the governing body of this municipality for such
public purposes as the governing body shall determine to be in the best
interest of the people of its municipality; provided, however, that said Coal
Severance Tax Revenue Fund monies shall not be budgeted for personal services
in an amount to exceed one-fourth of the total funds available in such fund.
   (B)   The coal severance tax estimate shall be made on the forms provided by
the State Tax Department, and shall be submitted to the State Tax Department by
June 15 of each year. (Prior Code, § 8-51)

§ 8-501 REPORTS, AND THE LIKE, TO CONFORM TO FISCAL YEAR.
   All reports, settlements, accounts, and statements of municipalities which
are now, or which may hereafter be, required by law shall be kept and made to
conform to the fiscal year. (Prior Code, § 8-52)
§ 8-502 AUDITS AND ACCOUNTS.
   The Tax Commissioner shall be the chief inspector of all audits of the city,
however, this municipality has the right that it may, by ordinance, make a
system for budgeting, accounting, and record keeping, and for the conduct of
the transactions of this municipality. (Prior Code, § 8-53)
§ 8-503 CAPITAL RESERVE FUND.
   (A)   This municipality shall have the power to establish a special fund
known as the Capital Reserve Fund. The Fund shall consist of unexpended
balances and other funds which may be transferred to the Reserve Fund with the
approval of the State Tax Commissioner.
   (B)   This Fund shall be used to purchase or improve public or municipal
works. Expenditures shall be made from the Fund only in accordance with an
appropriation made pursuant to the annual budget.
   (C)   If this municipality accumulates its Capital Reserve Fund for more
than two years, it shall be transmitted to the State Sinking Fund Commission on
or before September 1 of each year. The proceeds can be withdrawn from this
Fund upon reasonable notice, in writing, to the State Sinking Fund Commission.
(Prior Code, § 8-54)
§ 8-504 SPECIAL ACCOUNT FOR FEDERAL AND STATE GRANTS-IN-AID AUTHORIZED.
   In addition to the special fund account authorized by the provisions in § 8-
503, the governing body of this municipality shall have plenary power and
authority to establish a special account for the deposit of funds received
from, and granted by, the United States of America or the state, and shall
provide for the expenditure and appropriation of such funds in accordance with
the applicable laws and regulations promulgated by the government authority
making such grants. The funds so received and held in such special account
shall not be considered as revenue in determining the amount of real and
personal property takes to be levied for the regular fiscal budget of this
municipality. (Prior Code, § 8-55)
§ 8-505 SINKING FUNDS.
   (A)   This municipality shall have the power and authority to transfer to
the general funds of this municipality as follows:
      (1)   Any unexpended balances used to pay the interest or principal of
any municipal bonds that were left over after the bonds were paid off for,
provided in division (C) below, to fully pay and discharge such bonded
indebtedness; and
      (2)   Any balance remaining in any fund levied and collected under
authority of any special levy election.
   (B)   The State Sinking Fund Commission is authorized to remit to this
municipality when the issuances of bonds had been made, to be credited to the
General Fund of this municipality, any balances of funds remaining under the
supervision and control of the State Sinking Fund Commission when the bonded
indebtedness for the payment of which such funds were raised and paid to the
State Sinking Fund Commission has been fully paid and discharged, or when
provision has been made, as herein after provided in division (C) below, to
fully pay and discharge such bonded indebtedness.
   (C)   (1)   All outstanding bonds of any series shall, prior to the maturity
date thereof, be deemed to have been fully paid and discharged within the
meaning and with the effect expressed in divisions (A) and (B) above when there
shall have been deposited with the Sinking Fund Commission:
         (a)   Either monies in amount which shall be sufficient; or
         (b)   Securities put into the sinking fund which will be invested by
the State Sinking Fund Commission so that the monies along the interest can be
applied to the paying of the bill.
      (2)   The Sinking Fund Commission shall take all funds not needed for
payment of the interest on the city bond and invest at a date which will mature
on the same day as the bonds so the funds can be used for the payment of the
bonds. All interest collected from the investment of the funds, or left over
after all bonds are paid for, shall be returned back to this municipality.
      (3)   In any case when monies are returned from the sinking funds to this
municipality, they are not to be spent for the payment of current municipal
funds but as the governing body shall elect for the liquidating of existing
non-bonded indebtedness, if any, of this municipality, or for existing or
planned capital improvements of such municipality, or for the liquidation of
other bonded indebtedness of this municipality, or for any combination of such
use. (Prior Code, § 8-56)
§ 8-506 PAYMENT OF MONEY OUT OF MUNICIPAL TREASURY; PENALTY.
   (A)   No money shall be paid out of the treasury, except upon the order of
the Mayor, Treasurer, or Municipal Recorder which has been duly signed;
provided, that such signature may be made by any mechanical or electrical
device that the governing body may choose. Such machine shall be kept in the
office of the Recorder or Treasurer for safe keeping.
   (B)   If any of the above officers should allow someone to make, or if they
themselves should make, an unauthorized signing, then they shall be liable
jointly or severally for the amount of any loss resulting to the municipality.
   (C)   If any individual, other than the individuals authorized to do so,
shall sign the name of any municipal officer authorized to sign such order by
the use of any such mechanical or electrical device, or otherwise, upon any
warrant, order, or check, he or she shall be guilty of forgery, and if any
individual shall utter or attempt to employ as true such forged warrant, order,
or check, knowing the same to be forged, he or she shall be guilty of a felony.
(Prior Code, § 8-57)
§ 8-507 INVESTMENT OF MUNICIPAL FUNDS.
   All municipal funds, the investment of which is not governed by other
provisions of this article and not required for the payment of current
obligations, may be invested by the Treasurer or Recorder in the following
classes of securities and accounts, and not otherwise; which securities and
accounts mature on such dates as will make available such amount of cash as is
required:
   (A)   Certificates or other obligations of the United States in which the
faith and credit of the United States is pledged;
   (B)   Certificates of deposit secured by:
      (1)   Obligations of the United States of America;
      (2)   General obligations of revenue bonds of the state;
      (3)   General obligation bonds of other states;
      (4)   General obligation bonds of any county or any County Board of
Education; or
      (5)   General obligation bonds of any municipality of this state.
   (C)   (1)   Interest bearing savings accounts, which are insured by the
Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation or a savings and loan association insured
by the Federal Savings and Loan Insurance Corporation Building and Loan
Association, which are insured by the Federal Savings and Loan Insurance
Corporation; provided, that the amount invested is not more than would be
insured unless the banking institution or savings and loan association would
place a bond on the money.
      (2)   The security of the bonds is to be determined by the City Treasurer
or Recorder. (Prior Code, § 8-58)
§ 8-508 HOW AND BY WHOM SYSTEM OF ACCOUNTING FOR LOCAL OFFICES PRESCRIBED.
   The system of keeping accounts by the Recorder shall be done in the
following matter. All accounts shall show the receipt, use, and disposition of
all public property under the municipalities control and the income (if any)
derived from them, and all sources of such public income, and the amounts due
and received from each source, all receipts vouchers and other documents kept
and necessary to identify and prove the validity of every transaction, and all
statements and reports made, or required to be made, for the internal
administration of the office to which they pertain, and all reports published,
or thet may be required to be published, for the information of the people
regarding any and all details of the financial administration of such public
affairs. (Prior Code, § 8-59)
§ 8-509 SEPARATE ACCOUNTS FOR DIFFERENT APPROPRIATIONS OF FUNDS, DEPARTMENT
UNDERTAKINGS, AND THE LIKE; TRANSFER OF UNEXPENDED BALANCES.
   Separate accounts shall be kept for every appropriation of funds made by
this municipality, showing the date and manner of each payment made out of the
funds provided by such appropriation or levy, the name, address, and vocation
of each person, organization, corporation, or association to whom paid, and for
what purpose paid. Separate accounts shall be kept for each department, public
improvement, undertaking institution, and public service industry under the
jurisdiction of every city agency; and all service rendered by property
transferred from one department, public improvement, undertaking institution,
or public service industry to another shall be paid for at its true and full
value by the department, public improvement, undertaking institution, or public
service industry receiving the same,and no department, public improvement,
undertaking institution, or public service industry shall benefit in any
financial manner whatever by an appropriation or fund made for the support of
another department, public improvement, undertaking institution, or public
service industry. All unexpended balances or appropriations shall be
transferred to the credit of the fund from which they originally appropriated,
or levied whenever the account with an appropriation is closed. (Prior Code, §
8-60)
§ 8-510 MANAGEMENT ACCOUNTING.
   (A)   The Municipal Council may formulate its own requirements for a system
of management accounting for the planning, management, reporting, and control
of city expenditures. The requirements may include methods for recording the
collection of all revenues, amounts available for expenditure, encumbrances,
and expenditures for all funds and its own internal system of accounts.
   (B)   The expenditures and encumbrances of a spending unit shall not exceed
the approved appropriation of the fiscal year unless a budget amendment has
been authorized by the Municipal Council and approved by the State Tax
Department. (Prior Code, § 8-61)
§ 8-511 BORROWING POWER.
   This municipality shall have plenary power and authority to borrow money on
the general faith and credit of the municipality for any municipal purpose, in
the manner and subject to the limitations provided by law for the issuance of
general obligation bonds. (Prior Code, § 8-62)
§ 8-512 SPECIAL CHARGE FOR MUNICIPAL SERVICES.
   (A)   The special services of street lighting, street cleaning, and police
and fire protection within the city shall be continued, maintained, and
improved, in part, at the charge and expense of the users thereof, as herein
provided, so long as this section remains in effect.
   (B)   The users of said special services of street lighting, street
cleaning, and police and fire protection are hereby declared to be the
occupants, whether tenants or owners of all residential premises (which shall
include houses, apartments, and trailers), boarding houses, rooming houses,
hotels, business houses, business establishments, business premises, commercial
buildings, hospitals, nursing homes, restaurants, business and professional
offices, bakeries, processing and manufacturing plants, factories, and all
other similarly occupied premises within the city, and such special services
shall be continued, maintained, and improved for such users.
   (C)   For the continuance, maintenance, and improvement of the said special
services of street lighting, street cleaning, and police and fire protection by
the city there is hereby imposed upon the users thereof, that is to say: each
residential premises (which shall include house, apartments, and trailers),
boarding houses, rooming house, hotels, business houses, business
establishments, business premises, commercial buildings, hospitals, nursing
homes, restaurants, business and professional offices, bakeries, processing and
manufacturing plants, factories, and similar premises, from and after the first
day of February, 1977, an annual fee or charge of $8, payable in amount of $1
each on the first day of March, May, June, August, September, November,
December of 1977, and February 1, 1978.
   (D)   If such fee or charge, as aforesaid in division (C) above, is not paid
within 15 days following the date upon which the same is due and payable, a
penalty of 5% shall be added thereto and collected from the user.
   (E)   The City Clerk shall prepare an alphabetical list showing the name/
nature of all the users of such special services, with their respective
addresses, against such fee or for such special services shall be and is
charged, which said list shall be file in the office of the City Clerk and open
for public inspection.
   (F)   Statements of the fees or charges, in the amount herein provided in
division (C) above, shall be rendered by the City Clerk in connection and
conjunction with the statement for other services for which a special charge is
made. Such fees or charges shall be paid to the City Clerk at the offices of
the Clerk in the city building by all users of such special services, and the
failure of any such user to receive a statement of such or charge shall in no
manner impair or affect the validity of the said charge or the right to collect
the same.
   (G)   Any person feeling aggrieved by the imposition of a charge hereunder
may protest the same in writing filed with the City Clerk, and shall have the
right to be heard thereon in person or by agent or attorney before the City
Council. If the Council finds the said charge to be erroneous or improper, it
shall correct or annul the same as the circumstances may require.
   (H)   The said city, acting by and through its proper officials, may proceed
in active suit, attachment, or any other appropriate remedy provided by law, to
collect the charges, fees, and penalties herein provided in the event of
delinquency in the payment thereof by the user.
   (I)   All funds and income derived under and by virtue of this section shall
be segregated and used exclusively for the continuance, maintenance, and
improvement of the services of street lighting, street cleaning, and police and
fire protection within the city. (Prior Code, § 8-63)
§ 8-513 PREPARATION, PUBLICATION, DISPOSITION OF FINANCIAL STATEMENTS.
   This municipality shall prepare in a format prescribed by the State Tax
Commissioner a financial statement revealing:
   (A)   The receipts and expenditures of the city during the previous fiscal
year arranged under descriptive headings; and
   (B)   The name of anyone who received more than $50 from any fund during the
year, how much he or she was paid, and for what purpose. (Prior Code, § 8-64),

§ 9-1 ABANDONED REFRIGERATORS AND OTHER AIRTIGHT APPLIANCES.
   (A)   It shall be unlawful for any person to abandon, discard, or knowingly
permit to remain on premises under such person’s control, in a place accessible
to children, any refrigerator or other airtight or semi-airtight container
which has a capacity of one and one-half cubic feet or more and an opening of
50 square inches or more, and which has a door or lid equipped with a hinge,
latch, or other fastening device capable of securing such door or lid, without
rendering such equipment harmless to human life by removing such hinges,
latches, or other hardware which may cause a person to be confined therein.
   (B)   This section shall not apply to an icebox, refrigerator, or other
airtight or semi-airtight container located in that part of a building occupied
by a dealer, warehouse operator, or repair person.
   (C)   The imposition of any penalty for a violation of this section shall
not excuse the violation or excuse the violator from complying with the
provisions of this section. Each day that such violation continues shall
constitute a separate offense. The application of any applicable city ordinance
provision shall not preclude the removal of the prohibited conditions, and the
city shall have the right, in addition to any city ordinance or state code
provisions, to enforce the provision of this section by use of any other legal
remedy or court order. (Prior Code, § 9-1)
§ 9-2 POSSESSION OF MARIJUANA.
   No person shall knowingly or intentionally possess an amount of marijuana,
less than 15 grams in weight, unless the marijuana was obtained directly from,
or pursuant to, a valid prescription or order of a licensed medical
practitioner while acting in the course of his or her professional practice.
(Prior Code, § 9-2)
§ 9-3 JUDGE MAY DISMISS PROCEEDINGS.
   (A)   Whenever any person who has not previously been convicted of any
offense under the Uniform Controlled Substance Act, to wit, W. Va. Code Ch.
60A, or under any statute of the United States or any state relating to
narcotic drugs, marijuana, or stimulants, depressants, or hallucinogenic drugs
pleads guilty to, or is found guilty of, possession of any amount of marijuana
weighing less than 15 grams in violation of division (A)(1) below, the
Municipal Judge may discharge the person and dismiss proceedings against him
after any fine or jail sentence imposed hereunder has been paid or served. The
Municipal Judge, in determining whether or not to discharge the defendant and
to dismiss the proceedings against him or her, shall take into account the
following factors:
      (1)   The attitude of the defendant toward the offense mentioned herein;
and
      (2)   Whether or not the defendant has sought professional counseling in
relation to the possession of marijuana, as well as the nature and extent of
such counseling and the defendant’s response to such counseling; provided, that
the defendant has been advised of the availability of such counseling and has
had at least 30 days’ time thereafter to begin participation in such
counseling.
   (B)   (1)   It is unlawful for any person knowingly or intentionally to
possess a controlled substance, specifically a drug, substance, or immediate
precursor in Schedules I through V as set forth in W. Va. Code §§ 60A-2-204,
60A-2-206, 60A-2-208, 60A-2-210, and 60A-2-212 (W. Va. Code §§ 60A-2-204 et
seq.), unless the substance was obtained directly from, or pursuant to, a valid
prescription or order of a practitioner while acting in the course of his or
her professional practice, or except as otherwise authorized.
      (2)   Discharge and dismissal under this section shall be without
adjudication of guilt, and is not a conviction for purposes of this section or
for purposes of disqualifications or disabilities imposed by law upon
conviction of a crime. The effect of such dismissal and discharge shall be to
restore such person in contemplation of law to the status he or she occupied
prior to such arrest and trial. No person as to whom such dismissal and
discharge have been affected shall be thereafter held to be guilty of perjury,
false swearing, or otherwise giving a false statement by reason of his or her
failure to disclose or acknowledge such arrest or trial in response to any
inquiry made of him or her for any purpose. (Prior Code, § 9-3)
§ 9-4 BREATHING, INHALING, OR DRINKING CERTAIN INTOXICATING COMPOUNDS.
   (A)   (1)   No person shall intentionally breathe, inhale, or drink any
compound, liquid, or chemical containing acetone, amylacetate, benzol or
benzene, butyl acetate, butyl alcohol, carbon tetrachloride, chloroform,
cyclohexanone, ethanol or ethyl alcohol, ethyl acetate, hexane, isopropanol or
isopropyl alcohol, isopropyl acetate, methyl “cellosolve” acetate, methyl ethyl
ketene, methyl isobutyl ketene, toluol or toluene, trichloroethylene, tricresyl
phosphate, xylol or xylene, or any other solvent, material substance, chemical,
or combination thereof, having the property or releasing toxic vapors for the
purpose of inducing a condition of intoxication, stupefaction, depression,
giddiness, paralysis, or irrational behavior, or in any manner changing,
distorting, or disturbing the auditory, visual, or mental processes.
      (2)   For the purposes of this section, any condition so induced shall be
deemed to be an intoxicated condition.
   (B)   This section does not apply to:
      (1)   Any person who commits any act described herein pursuant to the
direction or prescription of a licensed physician or dentist authorized to so
direct or prescribe, including the inhalation of anesthesia for medical or
dental purposes; or
      (2)   To any alcoholic liquor or non-intoxicating beer, as defined in W.
Va. Code § 60-1-5.(W. Va. Code § 61-8-11) (Prior Code, § 9-4)
§ 9-5 SALE OF DEXTROMETHORPHAN.
   (A)   As used in this section, FINISHED DRUG PRODUCT means a drug legally
marketed under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (21 U.S.C. §§ 321 et
seq.) that is in finished dosage form.
   (B)   A person may not knowingly or willfully sell or trade a finished drug
product containing any quantity of dextromethorphan to a person under 18 years
of age.
   (C)   A person under 18 years of age, unless an emancipated minor, may not
purchase a finished drug product containing any quantity of dextromethorphan.
   (D)   A person making a retail sale of a finished drug product containing
any quantity of dextromethorphan shall require and obtain proof of age from the
purchaser before completing the sale, unless, from the purchaser’s outward
appearance, the person making the sale would reasonably presume the purchaser
to be at least 25 years of age.
   (E)   This section does not apply to a medication containing
dextromethorphan that is sold pursuant to a valid prescription.(W. Va. Code §
60A-4-417)
   (F)   Any person violating the provisions of this section is guilty of a
misdemeanor, and shall be fined not less than $100 nor more than $250. (Prior
Code, § 9-5)
