§ 9-300 BREACH OF PEACE.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to conduct himself or herself in a
noisy, boisterous, belligerent, violent, or tumultuous manner, which causes
disturbances to the peace and quiet of others. No person shall knowingly permit
such conduct upon any premises owned or possessed by such person or under such
person’s control.
(Prior Code, § 9-300)
§ 9-301 DISORDERLY CONDUCT.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to be a disorderly person within the
corporate limits of this city, as follows:
   (A)   Any person who shall act in a violent or tumultuous manner toward
another, whereby any person is placed in fear of safety of such person’s life,
limb, or health;
   (B)   Any person who shall act in a violent or tumultuous manner toward
another, whereby property of any person is placed in danger of being destroyed
or damaged;
   (C)   Any person who shall endanger lawful pursuits of another by acts of
violence, angry threats, or abusive conduct;
   (D)   Any person who shall cause, provoke, or engage in any fight, brawl, or
riotous conduct so as to endanger the life, limb, health, or property of
another;
   (E)   Any person who shall assemble or congregate with another or others for
the purpose of causing, provoking, or engaging in any fight or brawl;
   (F)   Any person who shall jostle or roughly crowd, or push, any person in
any public place;
   (G)   Any person who shall collect in bodies or crowds for unlawful
purposes;
   (H)   Any person who shall assemble or congregate with another or others for
the purpose of, or with the intent to, engage in unlawful gambling;
   (I)   Any person who shall act in a dangerous manner toward another;
   (J)   Any person who shall, by acts or threats of violence, interfere with
another’s pursuit of a lawful occupation;
   (K)   Any person who shall congregate with another or others in or on any
public way so as to halt the flow of vehicular or pedestrian traffic, and
refuses to clear such public way when ordered by city police; and
   (L)   Any person who shall direct words to another, which can be reasonably
calculated to incite an assault.
(Prior Code, § 9-301)
§ 9-302 DISTURBANCE OF RELIGIOUS WORSHIP.
   If any person willfully shall interrupt, molest, or disturb any assembly of
people met for the worship of God, such person shall be guilty of a
misdemeanor.
(Prior Code, § 9-302)
§ 9-303 DRUNKENNESS.
   A person shall not:
   (A)   Appear in a public place or in public view in an intoxicated
condition;
   (B)   Drink alcoholic liquor on any highway, street, alley, or in any public
square;
   (C)   Drink alcoholic liquor in a motor vehicle parked on any highway,
street, and alley, or in any public square; and/or
   (D)   Tender a drink of alcoholic liquor to another in a public place.
(Prior Code, § 9-303)
§ 9-304 FALSE EMERGENCY ALARM.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to intentionally make, turn in, or give
a false report of need for fire, police, or ambulance assistance, or to aid in
the commission of such an act.
(Prior Code, § 9-304)
§ 9-305 LOITERING.
   It shall be unlawful for any person, without legitimate business or purpose,
to loaf, loiter, wander, or idle in, upon, or about any way or place
customarily open to public use.
(Prior Code, § 9-305)
§ 9-306 LOITERING ON SCHOOL PROPERTY.
    No person not a student in regular attendance shall loiter in or about any
school, school building, or school grounds in violation of any posted rules or
regulations governing the use of any such school without written permission
from the principal.
(Prior Code, § 9-306)
§ 9-307 PROFANE, OBSCENE, INDECENT, OR VULGAR LANGUAGE; THREATS OVER TELEPHONE.
   If any person shall profanely curse, swear at, or abuse another, or use
profane, obscene, indecent, or vulgar language over any telephone wire or
system in this city, or, being in this city, shall use such language while
talking to another person out of the city, or over a telephone shall threaten
to commit a crime against any person, such person shall be guilty of a
misdemeanor.
(Prior Code, § 9-307)
§ 9-308 WILLFUL DISRUPTION OF GOVERNMENTAL PROCESS.
   If any person willfully interrupts or molests the orderly and peaceful
process of any department, division, agency, or branch of this city government,
such person shall be guilty of a misdemeanor. However, any assembly in a
peaceable, lawful, and orderly manner for a redress of grievances shall not be
a violation of this section.
(Prior Code, § 9-308)
§ 9-309 PUBLIC NUISANCES AFFECTING MORALS AND DECENCY.
   The following are hereby declared to be public nuisances affecting public
morals and decency:
   (A)   All places where intoxicating liquors are manufactured, sold,
bartered, or given away in violation of law, or where persons are permitted to
resort for the purpose of drinking intoxicating liquors kept for sale, barter,
or distribution in violation of law, and all liquors, bottles, kegs, pumps,
bars, and other property kept at and used for maintaining such a place;
   (B)   Any vehicle used for any illegal purpose;
   (C)   All indecent or obscene pictures, books, pamphlets, magazines, and
newspapers;
   (D)   Betting, bookmaking, or selling baseball pools or race horse pools,
and all apparatus used in such connection; and/or
   (E)   Gambling houses where minors under the age of 18 years are permitted
to enter and are permitted to loaf and loiter therein; where punchboards, slot
machines, race horse pools, baseball pools, or any other scheme, device, or
apparatus is kept and promoted which constitutes a game of chance, gambling
device, or any other scheme by whatsoever name known which is classed as and is
defined by state statute as a game of chance.
(Prior Code, § 9-309)
§ 9-310 OBSCENITY.
   (A)   Right of free speech preserved. Nothing herein shall be construed to
limit the free exercise of free speech or picketing by any organization, group,
or individual for the purpose of upholding community standards.
   (B)   Definitions. For the purpose of this section, the following
definitions shall apply unless the context clearly indicates or requires a
different meaning.
      ADULT BOOK STORE. An establishment having, as a substantial or
significant portion of its stock in trade, books, magazines, films for sale or
viewing on premises by use of motion picture devices or any other coin-operated
means, and other periodicals which are distinguished or characterized by their
emphasis on matter depicting, describing, or relating to “obscene matter,” or
an establishment with a segment or section devoted to the sale or display of
such matter.
      ADULT MOTION PICTURE THEATER. An enclosed building with a capacity of 50
or more persons used regularly and routinely for presenting material having as
a dominant theme material distinguished or characterized by an emphasis on
matter depicting, describing or relating to “obscene matter,” for observation
by patrons therein.
      ADULT MINI MOTION PICTURE THEATER. An enclosed building with a capacity
for less than 50 persons used for presenting material distinguished or
characterized by an emphasis on matter depicting, describing, or relating to
“obscene matter,” for observation by patrons therein.
      ADULT ENTERTAINMENT CABARET. A public or private establishment which is
licensed to serve food and/or alcoholic beverages, which features topless
dancers, strippers, male or female impersonators, or similar entertainers.
      DISTANCES. Measured in a straight line, without regard to intervening
structures or objects, from the nearest portion of the building used as a
business or enterprise described in this division (B), to the nearest property
line of the premises of a church or public or private elementary or secondary
school, or the nearest boundary of a city or public park or playground.
      OBSCENE MATTER. To the average individual applying contemporary state
standards, matter which:
         (a)   Considered as a whole, appeals to prurient interests;
         (b)   Depicts or describes ultimate sexual acts, both normal and
perverted, actual or simulated, masturbation, sodomy, fellatio, cunnilingus,
bestiality, sadism, excretory functions, or livid exhibition of the genitals;
and/or
         (c)   Considered as a whole lacks serious literary, artistic,
political, or scientific value.
   (C)   Regulated uses. Regulated uses include all adult uses which include,
but are not limited to, the following:
      (1)   Adult book store;
      (2)   Adult motion picture theater;
      (3)   Adult mini motion picture theater; and
      (4)   Adult entertainment cabaret.
   (D)   Permitted in certain zones. Adult uses shall be permitted only in the
area of the city which is zoned a commercial district, as set forth in the
zoning chapter (Chapter 10, Article 4), and shall be subject to the restriction
that no adult uses shall be allowed within 1,000 feet of any pre-existing
church or other place of public worship, public or private elementary or
secondary school, to a city or public park or playground, or any residential
district.
   (E)   Miscellaneous provisions and penalties.
      (1)   (a)   No adult use shall be conducted in any manner that permits
the observation of any material depicting, describing, or relating to “obscene
matter” from any public way or from any property not licensed as an adult use.
         (b)   This division (E) shall apply to any display, decoration, sign,
show window, or other opening.
      (2)   (a)   Any person violating any of the provisions of this section
shall be fined not less than $50 nor more than $100 and, in the discretion of
the Judge, imprisoned for a term not to exceed 30 days.
         (b)   Each offense and each day such violation shall continue shall be
regarded as a separate offense.
(Prior Code, § 9-310)
§ 9-311 INDECENT EXPOSURE.
   Any person who shall make an obscene or lewd exposure of the person to
public view shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
(Prior Code, § 9-311)
§ 9-312 PROSTITUTION.
   (A)   Any person who shall keep, set up, maintain, or operate any house,
place, building, hotel, tourist camp, other structure, or part thereof, or
vehicle, trailer, or other conveyance for the purpose of prostitution,
lewdness, or assignation; or who shall own any place, house, hotel, tourist
camp, other structure, or part thereof, or trailer or other conveyance knowing
the same to be used for the purpose of prostitution, lewdness, or assignation;
or who shall let, sublet, or rent any such place, premises, or conveyance to
another with knowledge or good reason to know of the intention of the lessee or
renter to use such place or premises for prostitution, lewdness, or
assignation; or who shall offer to secure another for the purpose of
prostitution, or for any other lewd or indecent act; or who, for another or
others, shall direct, take, or transport, or offer to take or transport, or aid
or assist in transporting, any person to any such house, place, building,
hotel, tourist camp, other structure, vehicle, trailer, or other conveyance; or
who shall aid, abet, or participate in doing any acts herein prohibited, shall
be guilty of a misdemeanor.
   (B)   Any person who shall engage in prostitution, lewdness, or assignation,
or who shall solicit, induce, entice, or procure another to commit an act of
prostitution, lewdness, or assignation; or who shall reside in, enter, or
remain in any house, place, building, hotel, tourist camp, or other structure,
or enter or remain in any vehicle, trailer, or other conveyance for the purpose
of prostitution, lewdness, or assignation; or who shall aid, abet, or
participate in the doing of any of the acts herein prohibited, shall be guilty
of a misdemeanor.
(Prior Code, § 9-312)
§ 9-313 PEEPING AND PROWLING.
   It shall be unlawful for any person, in the daytime or nighttime, to go upon
the premises of any person for the purpose of peeping into or prowling around
the same. Any person violating this section shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
(Prior Code, § 9-313)
§ 9-314 GAMBLING; KEEPING OR EXHIBITING TABLE, MACHINE, OR DEVICE.
   (A)   Any person who shall keep or exhibit a gaming table, commonly called
A.B.C. or E.O. table, or faro bank, or keno table, or any slot machine,
multiple coin console machine, multiple coin console slot machine, or device in
the nature of a slot machine, or any other gaming table or device of like kind,
under any denomination, or which has no name, whether the game, table, bank,
machine, or device be played with cards, dice, or otherwise, or shall be a
partner, or concerned in interest, in keeping or exhibiting such table, bank,
machine, or gaming device of any character, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
Any such table, faro bank, machine, or gaming device, and all money staked or
exhibited to allure persons to bet at such table, or upon such gaming device,
may be seized and, upon conviction, shall be fined not less than $100 nor more
than $1,000, and by order of the Municipal Court all money so seized shall be
forfeited to the municipality and paid into the Municipal Treasury, and the
table, faro bank, machine, or gaming device shall be completely destroyed.
Provided, however, that the provisions of this section shall not extend to
coin-operated, non-payout machines with free play feature or to automatic
weighing, measuring, musical, and vending machines which are so constructed as
to give a certain uniform and fair return in value or services for each coin
deposited therein, and in which there is no element of chance.
(W. Va. Code § 61-10-1)
   (B)   If any person knowingly permits a gaming table, bank, or device, such
as is mentioned in the preceding section, to be kept or exhibited on any
premises in his or her occupation, he or she shall be guilty of a misdemeanor,
and, upon conviction, shall be fined not less than $100 nor more than $1,000.
(W. Va. Code § 61-10-2)
   (C)   If any person shall act as doorkeeper, guard, or watch, or employ
another person to act as such, for a keeper or exhibitor of any such gaming
table, bank, or device, or shall resist, or by any means or device, prevent,
hinder, or delay the lawful arrest of such keeper or exhibitor, or the seizure
of the table, bank, or device, or money exhibited or staked thereat, or shall
unlawfully take the same from the person seizing it, he or she shall be guilty
of a misdemeanor, and, upon conviction, shall be fined not exceeding $1,000.
(W. Va. Code § 61-10-3)
   (D)   If any person bet or play at any such gaming table, bank, or device,
as is mentioned in this section, or if at any hotel or tavern, or other public
place, or place of public resort, he or she play at any game except bowls,
chess or backgammon, draughts, or a licensed game, or bet on the sides of those
who play at any game, whether the game be permitted or licensed or not, he or
she shall be guilty of a misdemeanor, and, upon conviction, shall be fined not
less than $5 nor more than $100.
(W. Va. Code § 61-10-4)
   (E)   (1)   The establishment of a video lottery, as licensed and authorized
by the state, with the exception of sale of state lottery tickets, or
charitable or public service organizations, shall be subject to the following
limitations.
         (a)   No public entrance to a video gaming or lottery establishment
within the city shall be located within 3,000 feet of the closest public
entrance of any church or place of worship.
         (b)   No video gaming or lottery establishment within the city shall
be located within 1,000 feet of another such establishment already providing
video lottery or having a license to do so, or any library, public park, public
playground, school, children daycare center, nursing or personal care home,
continuous care facility, or rehabilitation facility that is located within the
city.
         (c)   One parking space shall be required for each video lottery
machine on premises, in addition to any other parking required in accordance
with ordinances adopted by the city related to off-street parking.
         (d)   Any establishment shall not be located within 1,000 feet as
measured from each property line of a residential district.
         (e)   For the purpose of this section, the distance shall be measured
along a straight line, without regard to intervening structures or objects,
from the nearest portion of the parcel of real estate upon which an
establishment providing video lottery is located to the nearest property line
of the premises of another video lottery or gambling establishment, church or
place of worship, library, public park, public playground, school, children
daycare center, nursing or personal care home, continuous care facility, or
rehabilitation facility.
         (f)   1.   The City Council may waive the space provisions as set
forth in divisions (E)(1)(a) through (E)(1)(e) above, provided that:
               a.   The proposed use will not be contrary to the public
interest or adversely affect the value, use, or enjoyment of nearby property,
and that the spirit and intent of this section will be observed;
               b.   The proposed use will not enlarge or encourage the
development of a district or geographical area in which there is a
proliferation of gambling and/or video lottery;
               c.   There are not substantial objections by property owners
within the immediate area of the proposed location;
               d.   There will be compliance with the parking provisions of
this section and any other off-street parking ordinance adopted by the city
which is applicable; and
               e.   There has been compliance with all other applicable
ordinances and regulations of the city and applicable statutes and regulations
of the state.
            2.   Prior to initiation and establishing a video lottery business,
the applicant must provide evidence of full compliance, to City Council with
all other ordinances and regulations of the city and applicable statutes and
regulations of the state.
            3.   A private club restaurant or private club video lottery shall
adhere to the following:
               a.   Be in compliance with W. Va. Code Ch. 60, State Control of
Alcoholic Liquors;
               b.   Be in compliance with Title 175, Legislative Rule, Alcohol
Beverage Control Commissioner, Series 2 Private Club Licensing (175 CSR 2).
               c.   Be in compliance with §
1-5 shall be only authorized in private club restaurants within the municipal
boundaries of the city. All video lottery establishments shall be first
authorized by the Council of the city.
            4.   Prior to initiation and establishing a video lottery business,
the applicant must provide evidence of full compliance to the City Council with
all other ordinances and regulations of the city, and applicable statutes and
regulations of the state.
§ 9-315 SAME; BETTING.
   (A)   If any person at any place, public or private, bet or wage money or
other thing of value on any game of chance, or shall knowingly furnish any
money or other thing of value to any other person to bet or wage on any such
game, he or she shall be guilty of a misdemeanor, and, upon conviction, shall
be fined not less than $5 nor more than $300.
(W. Va. Code § 61-10-5)
   (B)   If the keeper of a hotel or tavern permit unlawful gaming at his or
her house, or at any outhouse, booth, arbor, or other place appurtenant thereto
or held therewith, he or she shall be guilty of a misdemeanor, and, upon
conviction, be fined not less than $20 nor more than $100, and shall forfeit
his or her license.
(W. Va. Code § 61-10-6)
   (C)   No person playing at any game or making a wager, or having a share in
any stake or wager, or betting on the hands or sides of others playing at any
game or making a wager, shall cheat, or by fraudulent means win or acquire for
himself or herself, or another, money or any other valuable thing.
(W. Va. Code § 61-10-9)
   (D)   POOLROOM, wherever used in this section, means any room where any pool
ticket, chance voucher, or certificate is sold entitling or purporting to
entitle the holder or promisee thereof, or any other person, to money or other
thing of value, contingent upon the result of any horse race, prizefight, game
of chance, game of skill or science, or other sport or contest. No person shall
set up or promote, or be connected with or interested in, the management or
operation of any poolroom. The buying, selling, or transferring of tickets or
chances in any lottery is hereby prohibited.
(W. Va. Code § 61-10-10)
   (E)   Except as otherwise provided by law, no person shall set up, promote,
or be concerned in managing or drawing a lottery or raffle for money or other
thing of value; knowingly permit such lottery in any house under his or her
control; knowingly permit money or other property to be raffled for in such
house, or to be won therein by throwing or using dice or by any other game of
chance; knowingly permit the sale in such house of any chance or ticket, or
share of a ticket in a lottery, or any writing, certificate, bill, token, or
other device purporting or intended to guarantee or assure to any person, or to
entitle him or her to a prize, or a share of or interest in a prize to be drawn
in a lottery. No person shall, for himself or herself, or any other person,
buy, sell, transfer, or have in his or her possession for the purpose of sale
or with intent to exchange, negotiate, or transfer, or aid in selling,
exchanging, negotiating, or transferring a chance or ticket, or a share of a
ticket, in a lottery or any such writing, certificate, bill, token, or device.
However, this section shall not be deemed to apply to that certain type or form
of lottery or raffle designated and familiarly known as “policy” or “numbers.”
(W. Va. Code § 61-10-11) (Prior Code, § 9-315)
§ 9-316 VACANT LOTS AND TEMPORARY STRUCTURES USED FOR ENTERTAINMENT PURPOSES.
   No vacant lot, temporary structure of any kind, or lot or part of a lot
appurtenant to any building in the city shall be used, or permitted by the
owner or person in control thereof to be used, for any kind of amusement,
performance, singing, playing on musical or other instruments, dancing,
preaching, exhorting, or lecturing without first obtaining the consent in
writing of three-fourths of the resident housekeepers in the block where the
performance, or other such activity, is to be conducted, and in the block
confronting the same block, nor shall such activity be conducted after 10:00
p.m. or in a manner to disturb the peace or quiet of the neighborhood within
any of the blocks above mentioned; provided, that singing or playing on musical
instruments as a part of the performance connected with theatres, moving
picture shows, or open air concerts, when it does not disturb the peace and
quiet of the neighborhood, may be permitted to continue on secular days and
while a part of such performance or concert until 11:00 p.m.
(Prior Code, § 9-316)
§ 9-317 WEARING MASKS, HOODS, OR FACE COVERINGS.
   (A)   Except as otherwise provided in this section, no person, whether in a
motor vehicle or otherwise, while wearing any mask, hood, or device whereby any
portion of the face is so covered as to conceal the identity of the wearer,
shall:
      (1)   Come into or appear upon any walk, alley, street, road, highway, or
other thoroughfare dedicated to public use;
      (2)   Come into or appear in any trading area, concourse, waiting room,
lobby, or foyer open to, used by, or frequented by the general public;
      (3)   Come into or appear upon or within any of the grounds or buildings
owned, leased, maintained, or operated by the state or city;
      (4)   Ask, request, or demand entrance or admission to the premises,
enclosure, dwelling, or place of business of any other person within this city;
or
      (5)   Attend or participate in any meeting upon private property of
another, unless written permission for such meeting has first been obtained
from the owner or occupant thereof.
   (B)   The provisions of this section do not apply to any person:
      (1)   Under 16 years of age;
      (2)   Wearing a traditional holiday costume;
      (3)   Engaged in a trade or employment where a mask, hood, or device is
worn for the purpose of ensuring the physical safety of the wearer;
      (4)   Using a mask, hood, or device in theatrical productions, including
use in Mardi Gras celebrations or similar masquerade balls;
      (5)   Wearing a mask, hood, or device prescribed for civil defense
drills, exercises, or emergencies;
      (6)   Wearing a mask, hood, or device for the sole purpose of protection
from the elements or while participating in a winter sport; or
      (7)   Wearing a mask, or device for a medical- or health-related reason,
including pandemic.
(Prior Code, § 9-317)
§ 9-318 SPITTING.
   (A)   No person shall expectorate or spit in or upon any parking lot,
footpath, sidewalk, or other public place in the city, or in or upon any part
of any public vehicle carrying passengers for hire, or in or upon any part of
any public building under the control of the city, county, or state, or of the
Board of Education.
   (B)   The proprietors of public vehicles carrying passengers for hire shall
keep posted conspicuously, in each and every one of their cars and public
vehicles, notices forbidding such expectorating or spitting.
(Prior Code, § 9-318)
§ 9-319 PUBLIC URINATION OR DEFECATION.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to urinate or defecate on any street,
sidewalk, or parking lot accessible to the public or in any other place in
public view.
(Prior Code, § 9-319)
§ 9-320 RIOTS AND UNLAWFUL ASSEMBLIES.
   (A)   No person shall incite or participate in any riot, rout, or unlawful
assembly. For the purposes of this section, RIOT mean a public disturbance
involving:
      (1)   An act or acts of violence by one or more persons part of an
assemblage of three or more persons, which act or acts constitute a clear and
present danger of, or result in, damage or injury to the property of any other
person, or to the person of any other individual; or
      (2)   A threat or threats of the commission of an act or acts of violence
by one or more persons part of an assemblage of three or more persons acting,
individually or collectively, where the performance of the threatened act or
acts of violence would constitute a clear and present danger of, or would
result in, damage or injury to the property of any other person or to the
person of any other individual.
   (B)   (1)   For the purposes of this section, INCITE A RIOT means, but is
not limited to, urging or instigating other persons to riot, but shall not be
deemed to mean the mere oral or written advocacy of ideas or expression of
belief not involving advocacy of any act or acts of violence or assertion of
the rightness of, or the right to commit, any such act or acts.
      (2)   For the purposes of this section, if three or more persons meet for
a purpose which, if executed, would make them rioters, and having done nothing
separate without carrying their purpose into effect, it is an unlawful
assembly; but if an unlawful assembly moves forward towards the execution of
its unlawful design, it become a rout; and if the design is carried into actual
execution, it constitutes a riot.
   (C)   Riots, routs, and unlawful assemblies shall be dispersed forthwith by
the city police, and all persons present at the scene of any riot, rout, or
unlawful assembly shall, upon command of any law enforcement officer, to
disperse forthwith and to obey such command, and peacefully disengage
themselves from such riot, rout, or unlawful assembly and leave the scene
thereof, and persons who fail to obey such command shall be subject to
immediate arrest.
(Prior Code, § 9-320)
§ 9-321 NOISE.
   No person shall make, continue, or cause to be made by the use of any horn,
bell, radio, or loud speaker, or by the operation of any instrument or device,
any unreasonably loud, disturbing, and unreasonable noise of such a character,
intensity, and duration as to disturb the peace and quiet of the community or
to be detrimental to the life or health of any individual, and no person shall
willfully conduct himself or herself in a noisy, boisterous, or other
disorderly manner by either words or acts which disturb the good order and
quiet of the community.
(Prior Code, § 9-321)
§ 9-322 SMOKING IS PROHIBITED.
   Smoking shall not be permitted, and smoking areas shall not be designated in
those areas where smoking is prohibited by the Fire Chief, state statute,
ordinances, or regulations of the city or other applicable law.
(Prior Code, § 9-322)

§ 9-400 OBTAINING OR ATTEMPTING TO OBTAIN GOODS, PROPERTY, OR SERVICE BY FALSE
OR FRAUDULENT USE OF CREDIT CARDS OR OTHER FALSE OR FRAUDULENT MEANS.
   (A)   It shall be unlawful for any person knowingly to obtain, or attempt to
obtain, any goods, property, or service of a value of less than $1,000 by use
of any false, fictitious, or counterfeit credit card, telephone number, credit
number, or other credit device; or by the use of any credit card, telephone
number, credit number, or other credit device of another beyond or without the
authority of the person to whom such card, number, or device was issued; or by
the use of any credit card, telephone number, credit number, or other credit
device in any case where such card, number, or device has been revoked, and
notice or revocation has been given to the person to whom issued.
   (B)   It shall be unlawful for any person knowingly to obtain, or attempt to
obtain, by the use of any fraudulent scheme, device, means, or method,
telephone or telegraph service or the transmission of a message, signed, or
other communication by telephone or telegraph, or over telephone or telegraph
facilities of a value of less than $200 with intent to avoid payment of charge
therefor.
   (C)   Any person who violates any provision of this section is guilty of a
misdemeanor.
(Prior Code, § 9-400)
§ 9-401 OBTAINING PROPERTY IN RETURN FOR WORTHLESS CHECK; MAKING, ISSUING
WORTHLESS CHECKS.
   (A)   It shall be unlawful for any person to obtain any money, service,
goods, or other property or thing of value by means of a check, draft, or order
for the payment of money, or its equivalent, upon any bank or other depository,
knowing at the time of the making, drawing, issuing, uttering, or delivering of
such check, draft, or order that there is not sufficient funds on deposit in,
or credit with, such bank or other depository with which to pay the same upon
presentation. Any person who shall violate the provisions of this division (A),
if the amount of the check, draft, or order is less than $200, shall be guilty
of a misdemeanor.
   (B)   (1)   It shall be unlawful for any person to make, draw, issue, utter,
or deliver any check, draft, or order for the payment of money, or its
equivalent, upon any bank or other depository, knowing, or having reason to
know, there is not sufficient funds on deposit in, or credit with, such bank or
other depository with which to pay the same upon presentation.
      (2)   Any person who shall violate the provision of this division (B)
shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
(Prior Code, § 9-401)
§ 9-402 FRAUDULENTLY OBTAINING FOOD OR LODGING.
   Every person who shall, at any hotel, motel, inn, eating, lodging, or
boarding house, or restaurant, receive, or cause to be furnished, any food or
accommodation, with intent to defraud the owner or keeper of such hotel, motel,
inn, eating, lodging, or boarding house, or restaurant, and any person who
shall obtain credit at any hotel, motel, inn, eating, lodging, or boarding
house, or restaurant, by use of any false pretense or device, or by depositing
in such hotel, motel, inn, eating, lodging, or boarding house, or restaurant,
any baggage or property of less value than the amount of such credit, or of the
bill by such person incurred, with such fraudulent intent, and any person who,
after obtaining credit or accommodation at any hotel, motel, inn, eating,
lodging, or boarding house, or restaurant, shall abscond from such hotel,
motel, inn, eating, lodging, or boarding house, or restaurant, or shall remove,
or attempt to remove, therefrom any baggage or personal property of any kind
subject to the lien provided in W. Va. Code § 38-2-5, with intent to defraud
the owner or keeper of such hotel, motel, inn, eating, lodging, or boarding
house, or restaurant, without first having paid, satisfied, or arranged all
claims or bills for lodging, entertainment, or accommodation, shall be guilty
of a misdemeanor.
(Prior Code, § 9-402)
§ 9-403 PROCURING GAS, WATER, OR ELECTRICITY BY DEVICE, WITH INTENT TO DEFRAUD.
   Every person who, with intent to injure or defraud, procures, makes, or
causes to be made, any pipe, tube, wire, or other conductor of gas, water, or
electric energy, and connects the same, or causes it to be connected with any
main, service pipe, or other pipe for conducting or supplying gas or water, or
any wires or other conductor of electric energy, in such manner as to supply
gas, water, or electric energy to any lamp, burner, orifice, or any other
device, by or at which gas, water, or electric energy is consumed, around or
without passing through the meter provided for measuring and registering the
quantity of gas, water, or electric energy consumed, or in any other manner so
as to evade payment therefor, and every person who, with like intent, injures
or alters any gas, water, or electric meter, or obstructs its action, shall be
guilty of a misdemeanor.
(Prior Code, § 9-403)

§ 9-500 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this article, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   ABANDONED. In addition to those definitions provided by state codes, local
ordinances, and case law, the term ABANDONED means and refers to any item which
has ceased to be used for its designated and intended purpose. The following
factors are among others, and will be considered in determining whether or not
an item has been ABANDONED:
      (1)   Present operability and functional utility;
      (2)   The date of last effective use;
      (3)   The condition of disrepair or damage;
      (4)   The last time an effort was made to repair or rehabilitate the
item;
      (5)   The status of registration or licensing of the item;
      (6)   The age and degree of obsolescence;
      (7)   The cost of rehabilitation or repair of the item versus its market
value; and
      (8)   The nature of the area and location of the item.
   ABATE. To repair, replace, remove, destroy, demolish, or otherwise remedy
the condition in question by such means and in such a manner and to such an
extent as the Enforcement Officer, in his or her judgment, shall determine is
necessary in the interest of the general health, safety, and welfare of the
community.
   ATTRACTIVE NUISANCE. Any condition, instrument, or machine which is unsafe,
unprotected, and may prove detrimental to children, whether in a building, on
the premises of a building, or on an unoccupied lot. This includes any
abandoned wells, shafts, basements, or excavations; abandoned refrigerators and
motor vehicles; any structurally unsound fences or structures; or any lumber,
trash, fences, debris, or vegetation which may prove hazarders or dangerous to
inquisitive minors.
   DEBRIS/REFUSE/BRUSH.
      (1)   BRUSH is yard clippings, leaves, branches, and other such matter.
      (2)   DEBRIS is the scattered remains of something broken or destroyed,
and ruins. It shall also include waste building materials, bricks, concrete
blocks, and other matter.
      (3)   REFUSE is all solid waste, including garbage, paper, cardboard, tin
cans, wood, glass, and liquid petroleum waste, such as motor oil and other such
similar items.
   DISMANTLED. That from which essential equipment, parts, or contents have
been removed or stripped, and the outward appearance verifies the removal.
   ENFORCEMENT OFFICER. The Chief of Police, Fire Chief, Building Inspector, or
City Engineer and if there is one, the City Health Officer, or their designated
representative, or as appointed by Council.
   GARBAGE/UNSANITARY MATTER. Decomposed animal and vegetable wastes resulting
from the handling, preparation, cooking, and consumption of food.
   INOPERATIVE. Incapable of functioning or producing activity for mechanical
or other reasons.
   LIEN-HOLDER. Any person, as defined in this article, who has a recorded
interest in real property, including mortgagee, beneficiary under deed of
trust, or other recorded liens or claims of interest in real property.
   NUISANCE.
      (1)   Any public nuisance known at common law or in equity jurisprudence.
      (2)   A thing or act, committed or permitted, failure to act, occupation,
or use of property which:
         (a)   Shall annoy, injure, or endanger the safety, health, comfort, or
repose of any number of persons;
         (b)   Shall offend the public decency;
         (c)   Shall unlawfully interfere with, obstruct, or tend to obstruct
or render dangerous for passage any public park, public playground, street,
alley, or highway; or
         (d)   Shall in any way render any number of persons insecure in life
or in the use and enjoyment of their property.
   OWNER. The registered owner of a vehicle, the person(s) to whom property tax
is assessed on real or personal property, as shown on the last equalized
assessment roll of the county, renter(s), lessee, and other occupants residing
permanently or temporarily on property.
   PERSON. Individual, partnership, joint venture, corporation, association,
social club, fraternal organization, trust, estate, receiver, or any other
entity.
   PREMISES. Any building, lot, parcel, real estate, or land, or portions of
land, whether improved or unimproved, occupied or unoccupied, including
adjacent streets, sidewalks, parkways, and parking strips.
   PROPERTY. Any real property including, but not limited to, land, lot, or
parcel of land, or any hereditament held by any owner, and shall include any
alley, sidewalk, parkway, or unimproved public easement abutting such real
property, lot, or parcel of land.
   STRUCTURE. Anything constructed, built, or planted upon, any edifice or
building of any kind, or any piece of work artificially built up or composed of
parts joined together in some definite manner, which structure requires
location on the ground or is attached to something having a location on the
ground, including fences, gates, garages, carports, swimming and wading pools,
patios, outdoor areas, paved areas, walks, tennis courts, and similar
recreation areas.
   WRECKED. That which has the outward manifestation or appearance of damage to
parts and contents which are essential to operation.
(Prior Code, § 9-500)
§ 9-501 DUTY OF POLICE OFFICERS.
   It shall be the duty of all police officers to observe the sanitary
condition of the city, and through the Chief of Police, to report to the Mayor
and City Council promptly any nuisance or accumulation of filth found to exist
in any portion of the city requiring their action.
(Prior Code, § 9-501)
§ 9-502 MAINTENANCE OF PREMISES.
   No person owning or in possession of any lot, house, building, or enclosure
shall allow or suffer to exist in or upon such premises any violation as
defined in this article. The lack of knowledge of the violation on the part of
the owner shall not exempt the owner from responsibility.
(Prior Code, § 9-502)
§ 9-503 INSPECTION, INVESTIGATIONS, AND COMPLAINTS; ENFORCEMENT OFFICER.
   The Enforcement Officer, or his or her designated representative(s), shall
cause inspections to be made from time to time within the municipality, and
when they deem it in the best interest of the municipality so to do, within the
extraterritorial jurisdiction of the municipality as provided, determine
whether any condition exists or activity is being practiced which constitutes a
nuisance; and each such officer shall cause an investigation to be made upon
written complaint made by any responsible person. In the absence of the City
Health Officer, any public Health Officer having jurisdiction within the
municipality is hereby vested with authority conferred by this article on a
City Health Officer, and he or she may exercise such authority when authorized
to do so by his or her superiors.
(Prior Code, § 9-503)
§ 9-504 RIGHT TO ENTER PRIVATE PREMISES; DUTY OF OCCUPANTS.
   Enforcement officers shall have the right to enter upon private premises for
the purposes specified in this article upon proper identification and in
compliance with all applicable provisions of law. Unless it appears probable
that advanced warning would defeat the purpose of such entry, occupants of
premises to be entered shall be given reasonable notice in advance, and in any
case, no owner or occupant shall prevent such entry which is sought to be made
in compliance with law. If advanced notice is not given, a search warrant from
applicable court having jurisdiction is necessary.
(Prior Code, § 9-504)
§ 9-505 NOTICE TO ABATE; APPEAL.
   (A)   If, at any time, an enforcement officer, Mayor, or City Recorder, upon
receiving and verifying a complaint, shall find that a condition which
constitutes a nuisance exists within the municipality or within the
extraterritorial jurisdiction of the municipality, as provided, he or she may,
for the first offense, give notice, in writing, to the owner, occupant, or
person in charge of the premises upon which such condition exists, stating
therein the condition which constitutes a nuisance; directing such addressee to
remedy the condition within the time stated in such notice, which shall not be
more than seven days; and no such owner, occupant, or person in charge shall
fail to comply with the terms of such notice. If, however, the owner, occupant,
or person in charge of such property, after receiving notice to abate, wishes
to challenge the notice, they must do so in writing to the Municipal Court not
less than ten days after receipt of such notice. Ordinarily, the Municipal
Judge will render a decision within ten calendar days from the date of a
hearing.
   (B)   If, after receiving the challenge, just cause is found to suspend the
notice to abate, an order will be issued to both the enforcement officer and
property owner, occupant, or person in charge stating the reason and what
action, if any, is necessary to comply. If, after reviewing the challenge of
notice to abate, there is no just cause to suspend the action, the original
date to abate shall stand without question, and notice will be given, in
writing, to the person challenging the notice and the enforcement officer,
Mayor, or City Clerk.
   (C)   If, during the course of inspection of a property, the enforcement
officer finds an imminent hazard to health or public safety, or the welfare of
the public, or any person within or near the premises upon which such nuisance
exists, the situation will be remedied without question, by means necessary,
without an appeal period.
   (D)   Failure to comply with a notice to abate by the date of remedy shall,
for each day, constitute a separate offense.
   (E)   For any second or subsequent offense for committing or maintaining a
nuisance, a citation or summons shall be issued.
   (F)   Nothing in this section shall be considered to prohibit any police
officer from arresting or issuing a citation to any person for committing or
maintaining a nuisance when such arrest is made pursuant to law.
(Prior Code, § 9-505)
§ 9-506 COMMITTING OR MAINTAINING A NUISANCE.
   Nothing in this chapter shall be considered to prohibit any police officer
from arresting or issuing a citation to any person for committing or
maintaining a nuisance when such arrest is made pursuant to law.
(Prior Code, § 9-506)
§ 9-507 RECOURSE OF MUNICIPALITY WHEN NOTICE TO ABATE NUISANCE IS IGNORED.
   (A)   Upon failure of any person to whom notice has been given pursuant to
this article to comply with the terms of such notice, the enforcement officer
or Mayor may forthwith direct the appropriate municipal officer or employee to
remedy the condition which is the subject of such notice if an emergency or
danger exists, and expense incurred by the municipality in so doing shall be
charged to the addressee of such notice, as well as to the owner of the
premises which is the subject of such notice, jointly and severally, to be
collected as municipal taxes, or in any other manner authorized by law for the
collection of money due to the municipality.
   (B)   If in the opinion of the court the nuisance is unsafe, unsanitary,
dangerous, unsightly, or detrimental to the public welfare, the court shall
enter an order permitting the Mayor to forthwith direct the appropriate
employee or other individual to remedy the condition which is the subject of
such complaint. Furthermore, any expense incurred by the municipality in so
doing shall be charged to the addressee of such notice, as well as to the owner
of the premises which is the subject of such notice, jointly and severally, to
be collected as municipal taxes or in any other manner authorized by law for
the collection of money due to the municipality.
   (C)   Abatement by the municipality of any condition which constitutes a
nuisance and reimbursement of the municipality of expenses incurred thereby
shall not prevent prosecution for maintenance of a nuisance.
   (D)   The municipality will prosecute the responsible party for failure to
comply with the notice to abate and for the violation itself.
(Prior Code, § 9-507)
§ 9-508 RESPONSIBILITY OF PROPERTY OWNERS, OCCUPANTS, AND OTHERS.
   Each owner, lessee, tenant, occupant, or person in charge of any real
property within the municipality, or at any place beyond the corporate limits
of municipality over which the municipality has right-of-way, and each agent or
representative of any such person, is hereby charged with responsibility for
the maintenance and use of such real property in such manner that no use of, or
activity or condition upon or within such real property shall constitute a
nuisance; and all such persons are hereby charged with the duty of observing
all of the provisions of this article, but such responsibility to commit or
maintain any nuisance upon or within any real property in the municipality or
property outside the corporate limits of the municipality over which the
municipality has a right-of-way.
(Prior Code, § 9-508)
§ 9-509 NOTICE TO PROPERTY OWNERS PRIOR TO REMOVAL BY MUNICIPALITY OF AN
ABANDONED OR JUNK VEHICLE.
   Prior to taking any abandoned or junked motor vehicle into custody and
possession from private property, the municipality shall give the private
property owner and the owner of said motor vehicle, if that person is
ascertainable, 30 days’ notice by registered or certified mail, or service of
process, that such action will be taken unless the said motor vehicle is
restored to a functional use.
(Prior Code, § 9-509)
§ 9-510 NUISANCES PROHIBITED.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to cause, harbor, commit, or maintain,
or to suffer to be caused, harbored, committed, or maintained any nuisance as
defined by the statute or common law of this state, or as defined by this code
or other ordinance of the city, at any place within the city, or at any place
within the area surrounding the city and within one mile of the city limits
when such nuisance constitutes a hazard to the health, safety, or good order of
the city or its inhabitants.
(Prior Code, § 9-510)
§ 9-511 CREATION OF NUISANCE PROHIBITED.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to create a nuisance on his or her lot
or a lot occupied by him or her, or to allow a nuisance to remain on his or her
lot or a lot occupied by him or her. Dead animals, stagnant water, decayed
vegetables and fruits, and filthy privies and stables causing an offensive
odor, or anything that causes injury or damage to the health or life of any
other person, is declared a nuisance.
(Prior Code, § 9-511)
§ 9-512 PUBLIC NUISANCES.
   The following are hereby defined as public nuisances affecting the health,
safety, and welfare of the citizens of the city and are hereby prohibited:
   (A)   Act done or committed. Prohibited any act done, or committed or aided
or assisted to be done or committed by any person, or any substance, being, or
thing kept, maintained, placed, or found in or upon public or private place,
which is injurious or dangerous to the public health or safety;
   (B)   Buildings, bridges, structures. Prohibited all buildings, bridges, or
other structures of whatever character kept or maintained, or which are
permitted by any person owning or having control thereof to be kept or
maintained, in a condition unsafe, dangerous, unhealthy, or injurious to the
public;
   (C)   Trees and appendages. Prohibited all trees and other appendages of, or
to realty kept or maintained, or which are permitted by any person owning or
having control thereof to be kept or maintained, in a condition unsafe,
dangerous, unhealthy, or injurious to the public;
   (D)   Stagnant water. Prohibited all ponds or pools of stagnant water, and
all foul or dirty water or liquid when discharged through any drain pipe or
spout, or thrown into or upon any street, public place, or lot;
   (E)   Obstructions. Prohibited all obstructions caused or permitted on any
street or sidewalk to the danger or annoyance of the public; all stones,
rubbish, dirt, filth slops, vegetable matter, or other article thrown or placed
by any person on or in any street, sidewalk, or other public place;
   (F)   Unsafe sidewalks. Prohibited all sidewalks, gutters, or curbstones
permitted to remain in an unsafe condition or out of repair;
   (G)   Places animals kept. Prohibited all stables, cattle yards, hog, sheep,
or cow pens, or other places where animals are kept, or yard for poultry,
permitted by the owner thereof or the person responsible therefor, and where
permitted by ordinance, to be in such condition as to become offensive,
annoying, or injurious to the public;
   (H)   Explosive storage. Prohibited all houses, buildings, structures, or
enclosures used for storage of power, dynamite, or other explosive or highly
flammable substance or gases, except those maintained pursuant to permit issued
by competent authority;
   (I)   Litter, trash, garbage. Prohibited any litter, trash, garbage, or
refuse, or any unlicensed motor vehicle, tractor, lawn mower, or any part
thereof in an inoperative condition;
   (J)   Grass, weeds, brush. Prohibited any offensive substance or growth of
grass, weeds, or brush upon any lot or parcel of ground;
   (K)   Pools or vessels of stagnant water. Prohibited all pools of stagnant
water or vessels holding stagnant water in which mosquitoes or other insects
can breed;
   (L)   Potential breeding places. Prohibited any carcasses of animals not
buried or otherwise disposed of in a sanitary manner within 24 hours after
death. Accumulation of manure, rubbish, litter, trash, rubble, refuse, debris,
paper, combustible materials, offal, or waste, or matter of any kind or form
which is uncared for, discarded, or abandoned, or improperly stacked building
materials, all of which are potential breeding placed for flies, mosquitoes, or
other vermin;
   (M)   Septic tanks or sewer lines. Prohibited any leaking septic tanks or
sewer lines, or other sewer existing in an unsanitary manner and which could
cause disease transmissions;
   (N)   Rank growth.
      (1)   Prohibited any grass, weeds, and rank growth of vegetation which:
         (a)   Every owner or occupier of any lot, tract, or parcel of land
within the municipal boundaries of the city, as the same may be adjusted from
time to time in the fashion provided by law, to cause the grass and weeds
growing thereon to be cut whenever said grass or weeds shall have grown to a
height in excess of eight inches from the ground, when measured as nearly
perpendicularly to the ground as is reasonably possible, and at all times to
keep and maintain all such grass and weeds at a height of less than eight
inches from the ground, when measured as nearly perpendicularly to the ground
as is reasonably possible;
         (b)   Regardless of height, harbors, conceals, or invites deposits or
accumulation of refuse or trash;
         (c)   Harbors rodents or vermin;
         (d)   Gives off unpleasant noxious odors; and/or
         (e)   Constitutes a fire hazard.
      (2)   Any person convicted of violating the provisions of this division
(N) shall be guilty of a nuisance, and shall be fined for a first offense not
less than $75 or more than $200. For a second offense, he, she, or they shall
be fined not less than $100 nor more than $500. For a third and subsequent
offense, he, she, or they shall be fined not less than $250 nor more than
$1,000. Each day any such violation continues shall constitute a separate
offense.
   (O)   Fire and decay damage. Prohibited all buildings, walls, and other
structures which have been damaged by fire, decay, or otherwise, and which
endanger the health, peace, and safety of the general public;
   (P)   Industrial waste. Prohibited any solid or industrial waste, including,
but not limited to, garbage, tin cans, bottles, rubbish, refuse, trash,
construction waste or demolition waste, tree trimmings, or manufacturing waste
or industrial waste dumped, thrown, burned, spilled, or abandoned, except such
waste disposed of lawfully in a landfill or permitted incinerator;
   (Q)   Unsanitary animal conditions. Prohibited any animal or animals kept or
maintained in an unsanitary condition or surroundings;
   (R)   Obnoxious odors. Prohibited any disagreeable or obnoxious odors and
stenches, as well as substances, causes, or conditions which give rise to the
emission or generation of such odors or stenches;
   (S)   Unlawful activity. Prohibited any building, structure, or other place
or location where any activity which is in violation of law is conducted,
performed, or maintained;
   (T)   Fire hazard. Prohibited the maintenance of any items or the overall
condition of the property which creates, or tends to create, a fire hazard or
fire menace;
   (U)   Obstructing clear view. Prohibited all trees, hedges, signs, or other
obstructions, or any portion of same, so located as to prevent persons driving
vehicles approaching an intersection of streets from having a clear, safe view
of traffic approaching such intersection;
   (V)   Growth over public road, sidewalk. Prohibited all limbs of trees or
other plants which project over a public road which are less than 13 feet and
six inches, and over a public sidewalk less than nine feet above the surface of
said road, or protrude upon the sidewalk and hinder travel;
   (W)   Blown trash. Prohibited any property that is in such condition that it
allows, permits, or creates rubbish, debris, or other personal property to be
blown on or across a public roadway;
   (X)   Loud noises. Prohibited all loud or unusual noises and annoying
vibrations which offend the peace and quiet of persons of ordinary
sensibilities;
   (Y)   Abandoned objects. Prohibited all abandoned, dismantled, wrecked,
inoperable, unlicensed, and discarded objects, equipment, or appliances such
as, but not limited to, vehicles, boats, water heaters, refrigerators,
furniture which is not designed for outdoor use, household fixtures, machinery,
equipment, cans, or containers standing or stored on property, or on sidewalks
or streets, which can be viewed from a public street or walkway, alley, or
other public property, and which items are readily accessible from such places,
or which are stored on private property in violation of any other law or
ordinance; and
   (Z)   Detrimental or fire hazard; other nuisances. Prohibited any
putrescibles, garbage, rubbish, refuse, or recyclable items which have not been
recycled within 30 days of being deposited on the property which are determined
by an Enforcement Officer to constitute a fire hazard or to be detrimental to
human life, health, or safety:
      (1)   Fire or environmental health. Prohibited any oil, grease, paint,
other petroleum products, hazardous materials, volatile chemicals, pesticides,
herbicides, fungicides, or waste (solid, liquid, or gaseous) which is
determined by an enforcement officer to constitute a fire or environmental
hazard, or to be determined to human life, health, or safety;
      (2)   Stored materials. Prohibited any lumber (excluding lumber for a
construction project on the property with a valid permit), salvage materials,
including, but not limited to, auto parts, scrap metal, tires, and other
materials stored on premises in excess of 72 hours and visible from a public
street, walkway, alley, or other public property;
      (3)   Receptacles. Prohibited any receptacles for discarded materials and
recyclables which are left in the front yard following the day of the regularly
scheduled refuse pick up for the property;
      (4)   Abandoned pool, pond, and spa. Prohibited any swimming pool, pond,
spa, other body of water, or excavation which is abandoned, unattended,
unsanitary, empty, which is not securely fenced, or which is determined by the
enforcement officer to be detrimental to life, health, or safety;
      (5)   Dilapidation, deterioration, decay. Prohibited any premises which
detrimentally impacts the surrounding neighborhood because of dilapidation,
deterioration, or decay, or is unsafe for the purpose for which it is being
used, or is not secured or is improperly secured;
      (6)   Injurious or annoyance. Prohibited any condition on a property
which meets the requirements of divisions (Z)(6)(a) and (Z)(6)(b) below:
         (a)   Is injurious to health, or is indecent or offensive to the
senses, or an obstruction to the free use of property, so as to interfere with
the comfortable enjoyment of life or property; and
         (b)   Affects at the same time an entire community or neighborhood, or
considerable number of persons, although the extent of the annoyance or damage
inflicted upon individuals may be unequal.
      (7)   Loudspeakers, or amplifiers on vehicles. The use of any mechanical
loudspeakers or amplifiers on trucks, airplanes, or other vehicles for
advertising or other purposes, except by special permission of the Mayor;
      (8)   Noises to attract attention. The use of any drum, loudspeaker, or
other instrument or device for the purpose of attracting attention to any
performance or event, show, sale, or display, or advertisement of merchandise,
by the creation of noise;
      (9)   Bells or gongs. The sounding of any bell or gong attached to any
building or premises which disturb the quiet or repose of any person in the
vicinity thereof; and/or
      (10)   Radios, phonographs, and the like. The playing of any radio,
phonograph, piccolo, or any musical instrument in such manner or with such
volume as to annoy or disturb the quiet, comfort, or repose of any person in
any dwelling, hotel, or other residence.
(Prior Code, § 9-512)
§ 9-513 SMOKE, SOOT, CINDERS, AND THE LIKE.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to permit or cause the escape of such
quantities of dense smoke, soot, cinders, noxious acids, fumes, or gases as to
be detrimental to or to endanger the health, comfort, and safety of the public,
or so as to cause, or have a tendency to cause injury or damage to property or
business.
(Prior Code, § 9-513)
§ 9-514 COLLECTION OF, OR BURNING OF, LEAVES OR OTHER MATTER IN PUBLIC STREETS.
   It shall be unlawful to collect and pile leaves and brush in the city
streets. It shall be unlawful to burn leaves or other matter in the city
streets.
(Prior Code, § 9-514)
§ 9-515 DEPOSITING GRASS CLIPPINGS AND OTHER SIMILAR DETRITUS INTO THE PUBLIC
STREETS.
   (A)   It shall be unlawful for the owner or any person in control of any
property within the corporate limits of the city to throw, deposit, or permit
to be thrown or deposited, into the right-of-way of any public street of the
city any grass clippings or other similar detritus for the purpose, or with the
effect, of clogging the storm sewers of the city and the intake outlets
thereof, and a violation hereof shall be punishable in accordance with the
general law.
   (B)   Upon conviction, there shall be taxed, as a part of the costs of any
proceeding to determine the violation of this provision of the city code, the
reasonable costs of cleaning out any storm sewer or intake outlet thereof
clogged or obstructed in any fashion by activity constituting a violation
hereof; provided, however, that in no event shall any sum less than $6 be taxed
as a part of the costs of such suit for such purpose.
(Prior Code, § 9-515)
§ 9-516 UNAUTHORIZED USE OF SIRENS AND OTHER EMERGENCY TYPE WHISTLES OF SIMILAR
IMPACT.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to sound, blow, or cause to be sounded
or blown any siren or other emergency type whistle of similar impact upon the
public from any place, either inside the corporate limits of the city or
without the corporate limits of the city, where the same may be heard within
such limits, unless such person shall be the authorized driver of an authorized
emergency vehicle as defined in the Code of West Virginia, as amended, or a
member of the Volunteer Fire Department engaged in the performance of his or
her duties as such.
(Prior Code, § 9-516)
§ 9-517 SHALL NOT BLOCK STREETS, SIDEWALKS, LANES, RIGHTS-OF-WAY.
   No person shall accumulate or store construction or building material, items
for sale, display, storage, parked, or any other item otherwise on any street,
sidewalk, lane, or right-of-way.
(Prior Code, § 9-517)
§ 9-517(A) YARD, GARAGE SALES, UNAUTHORIZED SALES PROHIBITED.
   (A)   Definitions. For the purpose of this section, the following
definitions shall apply unless the context clearly indicates or requires a
different meaning.
      PERSONAL PROPERTY. Property which is owned, utilized, and maintained by
an individual or members of his or her residence, and acquired in the normal
course of living in or maintaining a residence. It does not include merchandise
which was purchased for resale or obtained on consignment.
      YARD SALE. All general sales, open to the public, conducted from or on a
residential premises in any residential area, for the purpose of disposing of
personal property including, but not limited to, all sales entitled “garage,”
“lawn,” “yard,” “attic,” “porch,” “room,” “backyard,” “patio,” “flea market,”
or “rummage” sale.
   (B)   Number and hours of sales permitted.
      (1)   No more than two yard sales shall be held at any residence and/or
family household, or by any individual or entity during a calendar year. If
members of more than one residence join in such sale, then such sale shall be
considered as having occurred at all such residences.
      (2)   In addition to the above two such sales, in division (B)(1) above,
an individual residence or family household shall be permitted to participate
in one neighborhood yard sale per calendar year. A NEIGHBORHOOD YARD SALE shall
be defined as any yard sale held by and at multiple adjoining or nearby
residences, and promoted or advertised as a neighborhood, street, or community
sale.
      (3)   Such yard sales shall be limited in time to no more than the
daylight hours and three consecutive days. No such sale shall be conducted on
Sunday.
   (C)   Property permitted to be sold. It shall be unlawful for any individual
to sell or offer for sale, under authority granted by this article, property
other than personal property.
   (D)   Display of sale property. Personal property offered for sale may be
displayed within the residence in a yard, garage, carport, and/or in a private
driveway. No personal property offered for sale at such a sale shall be
displayed in any public right-of way.
   (E)   Advertising; signs.
      (1)   Two signs of not more than six square feet each shall be permitted
to be displayed on the property of the residence where the sale is being
conducted.
      (2)   Two signs of not more than four square feet each shall be
permitted, provided written permission to erect said signs is received from the
property owners upon whose property such signs are to be placed.
      (3)   No sign or other form of advertisement shall be exhibited for more
than two days prior to the day such sale is to commence.
      (4)   Signs shall be removed at the end of the sale.
      (5)   No signs shall be placed in any city right-of-way, or on or
attached to any utility poles, street signs, or traffic control signs.
   (F)   Public nuisance.
      (1)   The individual(s) conducting the sale, and the owner(s) or tenant
(s) of the premises on which such sale or activity is conducted, shall be
jointly and severally responsible for the maintenance of good order and decorum
on the premises during all hours of such sale or activity. No such individual
shall permit any loud or boisterous conduct on said premises, nor permit
vehicles to impede the passage of traffic on any roads or streets in the area
of such premises. All such individuals shall obey the reasonable orders of any
member of the Police or Fire Department of the city in order to maintain the
public health, safety, and welfare.
      (2)   The City Police Department or the City Mayor has the right to
enjoin immediately any yard sale operating in violation of this article or
causing a nuisance to the city.
   (G)   Parking. All parking of vehicles shall be conducted in compliance with
all applicable laws and ordinances. Further, the Police Department may enforce
such temporary controls to alleviate any special hazards and/or congestion
created by any such sale.
   (H)   Persons and sales exempted. The provisions of this section shall not
apply to or affect the following:
      (1)   Persons selling goods pursuant to an order or process of a court of
competent jurisdiction;
      (2)   Persons acting in accordance with their powers and duties as public
officials;
      (3)   Any sale conducted by any merchant or mercantile, or other business
establishment, from or at a place of business where such sale would be
permitted, or any other sale conducted by a manufacturer, dealer, or vendor;
and
      (4)   Any bona fide charitable, educational, cultural, or governmental
institution or organization when the proceeds from the sale are used directly
for the institution’s or the organization’s charitable purposes, and the goods
or articles are not sold on a consignment basis.
   (I)   Notification to city. Prior to any yard sale, person or persons
conducting said sale shall notify the City Police Department or the City
Recorder of the date and place of sale.
   (J)   Penalty.
      (1)   Whoever violates any provision of this section shall be fined not
less than $50 nor more than $250 for each offense.
      (2)   Anyone who violates this section by failing to remove any sale sign
(s) as required herein shall be fined $25 for each such sign.
      (3)   Each day a portion of this section is violated shall constitute a
separate offense.
(Prior Code, § 9-517(A))
§ 9-517(B) FLEA MARKETS.
   (A)   FLEA MARKET shall mean an open-air market for the sale of new and/or
secondhand articles and goods by one or more merchants, which is conducted on
an open, non-residential lot.
      (1)   Flea markets shall be permitted uses only in non-residential areas,
or as conditional uses in the business areas.
      (2)   The sale of animals is prohibited in any flea market, including,
but not limited to, reptiles, birds, felines, and canines.
      (3)   Flea market operators must have the appropriate business licenses
and permits. Flea markets shall comply at all times with all state and local
law and regulations, including, but not limited to, Health Department
regulations.
   (B)   (1)   Whoever violates any provision of this section shall be fined
not less than $100 nor more than $250 for each offense.
      (2)   Anyone who violates this section by failing to remove any sale sign
(s), as required herein, shall be fined $25 for each such sign.
      (3)   Each day a portion of this section is violated shall constitute a
separate offense.
      (4)   The City Police Department or the City Mayor has the right to
enjoin immediately any flea market operating in violation of this section or
causing a nuisance to the city.
   (C)   Prior to any flea market, person or persons conducting said sale shall
notify the City Police Department or City Recorder of the date and place of the
sale.
(Prior Code, § 9-517(B))
§ 9-518 REMOVAL OF ABANDONED, DUPLICATED POLES, WIRE, OR CABLE.
   (A)   Definitions. For the purpose of this section, the following
definitions shall apply unless the context clearly indicates or requires a
different meaning.
      DANGEROUS or DAMAGED POLE. Any utility pole that is structurally
compromised due to weather, a traffic incident, and/or age, and poses a
potential threat to public safety.
      DOUBLE POLE. Any utility pole which is attached or in close proximity to
a new utility pole.
      PLANT. The cables, terminals, conductors, and other fixtures necessary
for transmitting electrical, telephone, cable television, or other
telecommunications service.
      UTILITY POLE. A column or post used to support service lines for public
utility.
   (B)   Dangerous poles. Whenever a pole shall, on the judgment of the Mayor
or Maintenance Supervisor, become a menace to persons or property, or shall
interfere with any municipal work, or with the operation of any municipal
construction, it shall be removed, and a new pole may be substituted therefor.
Such pole shall be removed within five days after notice, unless it is an
imminent danger to persons or property which then shall be removed at once.
   (C)   Removal of abandoned poles. Every pole, when no longer used for
service, shall be taken down
and removed from the street immediately upon abandonment. Upon application,
time may be extended by Council for a period of up to one year.
   (D)   Double pole. A written notice shall be given to the public utility,
which has the top plant on the double pole, that the plant must be removed
within 30 days or be subject to a penalty. Upon removal of each plant on the
pole, notice shall be given to the subsequent plant on the pole that the plant
must be removed within 30 days. The last utility to remove its plant is
responsible for removing the double pole within an additional 30 days.
   (E)   Abandoned wires or cables. All abandoned wires or cables attached to a
pole which shall become disused or abandoned in, or over or upon, any street
shall be forthwith removed by the owner or proprietor of such pole, wire, or
cable immediately upon such abandonment.
   (F)   Penalties for offenses. Any person convicted of a violation of any
provisions of this section shall be punished by a fine of not less than $250
nor more than $1,000. Each day such violation continues shall be a counted a
separate offense.
(Prior Code, § 9-518)
