§ 9-700 COURTESY, AND THE LIKE, DUE TO AND FROM MUNICIPAL EMPLOYEES.
   (A)   Municipal officers and employees shall be courteous in their official
transactions with the public, and they shall conduct themselves in the
performance of official duties so as not to deprive any person, at the time and
under the circumstances existing then and there, of any lawful right or benefit
to which such person is entitled. Any person who feels aggrieved by the conduct
of any municipal officer or employee is hereby invited to bring the matter to
the attention of such officer’s or employee’s department head or to the Mayor,
without prejudice to any other recourse to which such aggrieved person may be
entitled.
   (B)   Members of the public, in turn, should be courteous in their
transactions with municipal officers and employees, and it shall be unlawful
for any person to knowingly taunt, deride, jeer, or otherwise insult or debase,
whether by act, word, or gesture, any municipal officer or employee at any time
or place while such officer or employee is lawfully engaged in the performance
of any official duty.
(Prior Code, § 9-700)
§ 9-701 PUBLIC OFFICERS AND EMPLOYEES; OBSTRUCTING OFFICER.
   Any person who, by threats, menacing acts, or otherwise, shall forcibly or
illegally hinder, obstruct, or oppose, or attempt to hinder, obstruct, or
oppose, or shall counsel, advise, or invite others to hinder, obstruct, or
oppose any officer of this city in the lawful exercise or discharge of such
officer’s official duty shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
(Prior Code, § 9-701)
§ 9-702 SAME; REFUSAL TO AID OFFICER.
   Any person who shall, on being required by an officer, refuse or neglect to
assist such officer in the execution of the office in a criminal case, or in
the preservation of the peace, or the apprehending or securing of any person
for a breach of the peace, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
(Prior Code, § 9-702)
§ 9-703 SAME; INTERFERENCE, AND THE LIKE, WITH POLICE OFFICERS.
   Any person who shall, at any time, intercept, molest, or interfere with any
police officer while on duty, or any person then under the charge and direction
of an officer while on duty, or who knowingly gives false or misleading
information to a member of the Police Department, shall be guilty of a
misdemeanor.
(Prior Code, § 9-703)
§ 9-704 SAME; IMPERSONATING.
   (A)   No person shall falsely represent such person’s self to be an officer
or employee of the city, or, without proper authority, wear or display any
uniform, insignia, or credential which identifies any city officer or employee.
   (B)   No person without proper authority shall assume to act as an officer
or employee of the city, whether to gain access to the premises, obtain
information, perpetrate fraud, or any other purpose.
   (C)   This section shall not be construed to prevent a private citizen from
making a lawful citizen’s arrest when a violation is committed in such
citizen’s presence.
(Prior Code, § 9-704)
§ 9-705 OBSTRUCTING OR GIVING FALSE INFORMATION TO AN OFFICER; FLEEING.
   (A)   No person shall, by threats, menaces, and acts, or otherwise forcibly
or illegally hinder or obstruct, or attempt to hinder or obstruct, any law
enforcement officer, probation officer, or parole officer acting in his or her
official capacity.
   (B)   (1)   (a)   No person shall, with intent to impede or obstruct a law
enforcement officer in the conduct of an investigation of a felony offense,
knowingly and willfully make a materially false statement.
         (b)   Provided, that the provisions of division (B)(1)(a) above shall
not apply to statements made by a spouse, parent, stepparent, grandparent,
sibling, half-sibling, child, stepchild, or grandchild, whether related by
blood or marriage, of the person under investigation.
      (2)   Statements made by the person under investigation may not be used
as the basis for prosecution under this division (B). For the purposes of this
division (B), LAW ENFORCEMENT OFFICER shall not include watchman, state police,
or college security personnel.
   (C)   No person shall intentionally flee, or attempt to flee, by any means
other than the use of a vehicle from any law enforcement officer, probation
officer, or parole officer acting in his or her official capacity who is
attempting to make a lawful arrest of the person, and who knows or reasonably
believes that the officer is attempting to arrest him or her.
   (D)   (1)   No person shall intentionally flee, or attempt to flee, in a
vehicle from any law enforcement officer, probation officer, or parole officer
acting in his or her official capacity, after the officer has given a clear
visual or audible signal directing the person to stop.
      (2)   For the purposes of this division (D), VEHICLE includes any motor
vehicle, motorcycle, motorboat, all-terrain vehicle, or snowmobile, as those
terms are defined in W. Va. Code § 17A-1-1, whether or not it is being operated
on a public highway at the time, and whether or not it is licensed by the
state.
      (3)   For the purposes of this division (D), FLEE and FLEEING do not
include any person’s reasonable attempt to travel to a safe place, allowing the
pursuing law enforcement officer, probation officer, or parole officer to
maintain appropriate surveillance, for the purpose of complying with the
officer’s direction to stop.
(W. Va. Code § 61-5-17)
   (E)   No person shall refuse or fail to comply with any lawful order,
direction, or signal of a police officer.
(Prior Code, § 9-705)
§ 9-706 FALSE FIRE ALARM.
   No person shall make, turn in, or telephone, or by use of any means or
methods of communication aid or abet in the making or turning in of, any alarm
of fire which he or she knows to be false at the time of making or turning in
the alarm.
(W. Va. Code § 15A-10-20) (Prior Code, § 9-706)
§ 9-707 FALSE REPORTS CONCERNING BOMBS OR OTHER EXPLOSIVE DEVICES.
   (A)   No person shall impart or convey, or cause to be imparted or conveyed,
any false information, knowing or having reasonable cause to believe such
information to be false, concerning the presence of any bomb or other explosive
device in, at, on, near, under, or against any dwelling house, structure,
improvement, building, bridge, motor vehicle, vessel, boat, railroad car,
airplane, or other place, or concerning an attempt or alleged attempt being
made, or to be made, to so place or explode any such bomb or other explosive
device.
   (B)   Notwithstanding any provision of this section to the contrary, any
person violating the provisions of division (A) above for a second offense, or
whose violation of division (A) above results in another suffering serious
bodily injury, shall be guilty of a felony and prosecuted under appropriate
state law.
(W. Va. Code § 61-6-17) (Prior Code, § 9-707)
§ 9-708 IMPERSONATING AN OFFICIAL OR LAW ENFORCEMENT OFFICER.
   (A)   (1)   No person shall falsely represent himself or herself to be a law
enforcement officer or law enforcement official, or be under the order or
direction of any such person. No person not a law enforcement officer or law
enforcement official shall wear the uniform prescribed for such persons, or the
badge or other insignia adopted for use by such persons with the intent to
deceive another person.
      (2)   For purposes of this section, LAW ENFORCEMENT OFFICER and LAW
ENFORCEMENT OFFICIAL shall have the meanings set forth in W. Va. Code § 30-29-
1, except that such terms shall not include members of the State Division of
Public Safety, and shall not include individuals hired by non-public entities
for the provision of security services.
(W. Va. Code § 61-1-9)
   (B)   No person shall falsely represent himself or herself to be an officer
or employee of the city, or exercise or attempt to exercise any of the duties,
functions, or powers of a municipal officer. No person not a member of the Fire
Department, for the purpose of such false representation, shall wear a uniform,
or part thereof similar to the uniform, worn by a member of the Fire
Department.
(Prior Code, § 9-708)
§ 9-709 ATTEMPTS.
   Every person who attempts to commit an offense, but fails to commit or is
prevented from committing it, shall be subject to the penalty provided in §
9-17 if the offense is punishable by confinement in jail.
(W. Va. Code § 61-11-8) (Prior Code, § 9-709)
§ 9-710 CITATION IN LIEU OF ARREST; FAILURE TO APPEAR.
   (A)   A police officer may issue a citation instead of making an arrest for
the following offenses, if there are reasonable grounds to believe that the
person being cited will appear to answer the charge:
      (1)   Any misdemeanor, not involving injury to the person, committed in a
police officer’s presence; provided, that the officer may arrest the person if
he or she has reasonable grounds to believe that the person is likely to cause
serious harm to himself or herself, or others; and
      (2)   When any person is being detained for the purpose of investigating
whether such person has committed or attempted to commit shoplifting, pursuant
to §
9-107.
   (B)   The citation shall provide that the defendant shall appear within a
designated time.
   (C)   If the defendant fails to appear in response to the citation, or if
there are reasonable grounds to believe that he or she will not appear, a
complaint may be made and a warrant shall issue. When a physical arrest is made
and a citation is issued in relation to the same offense, the officer shall
mark on the citation, in the place specified for court appearance date, the
word “arrested” in lieu of the date of court appearance.
(W. Va. Code § 62-1-5a) (Prior Code, § 9-710)
§ 9-711 FALSELY REPORTING AN EMERGENCY INCIDENT.
   A person is guilty of reporting a false emergency incident when, knowing the
information reported, conveyed, or circulated is false or baseless, he or she:
   (A)   Initiates or circulates a false report or warning of, or impending
occurrence of, a fire, explosion, crime, catastrophe, accident, illness, or
other emergency under circumstances in which it is likely that public alarm or
inconvenience will result, or that firefighting apparatus, ambulance apparatus,
one or more rescue vehicles, or other emergency apparatus might be summoned;
   (B)   Reports, by word or action, to any official or quasi-official agency
or organization having the function of dealing with emergencies involving
danger to life or property, an alleged occurrence or impending occurrence of a
fire, explosion, crime, catastrophe, accident, illness, or other emergency in
which it is likely that public alarm or inconvenience will result, or that
firefighting apparatus, ambulance apparatus, one or more rescue vehicles, or
other emergency apparatus might be summoned, which did not occur, does not in
fact exist;
   (C)   Reports to a law enforcement officer or agency the alleged occurrence
of any offense or incident which did not in fact occur, or an allegedly
impending occurrence of an offense or incident which is not in fact about to
occur, or false information relating to an actual offense or incident, or to
the alleged implication of some person therein; or
   (D)   Without just cause, calls or summons by telephone, fire alarm system,
or otherwise, any firefighting apparatus, ambulance apparatus, rescue vehicles,
or other emergency vehicles.
(W. Va. Code § 61-6-20) (Prior Code, § 9-711)
§ 9-712 FALSE REPORT.
   No person shall make or give a false report or false information to any
police or fire officer of the city.
(Prior Code, § 9-712)
§ 9-713 FALSE SWEARING.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to willfully swear falsely, under an
oath or affirmation lawfully administered, on any occasion concerning any
municipal matter or thing, material or not material, or to procure another
person to do so.
(Prior Code, § 9-713)

§ 10-1 PLANNING COMMISSION AUTHORIZED; STATEMENT OF OBJECTIVES.
   The City Council, in order to promote the orderly development of the
community, hereby establishes a municipal planning commission, hereafter known
as the City Planning Commission. It’s objective shall be that highway systems
be carefully planned; that the new community center grow only with adequate
highway, utility, health, educational, and recreational facilities; that the
needs of agriculture, industry, and business be recognized in future growth;
that residential areas provide healthy surroundings for family life; and that
the growth of the community is commensurate with, and promotive of, the
efficient and economic use of public funds.
(Prior Code, § 10-1)
§ 10-2 CONTINUATION OF EXISTING PLANNING COMMISSION.
   Any existing planning commission shall continue to operate as though it was
established under this article. All actions lawfully taken under prior acts are
hereby validated and continued in effect until amended or repealed by action
taken under the authority of this article. The membership of any existing
commission shall continue unchanged until the first regular meeting of the City
Council in January of the year following enactment of this article. At that
time, any appointments or changes necessary shall be made to bring the
membership of the Commission into conformity with the provisions of this
article.
(Prior Code, § 10-2)
§ 10-3 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this article, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   COMPREHENSIVE PLAN. A complete comprehensive plan or any of its parts, such
as a comprehensive plan of land use and zoning, of thoroughfares , of
sanitation, of recreation, and of other related matters. It shall include such
ordinance or ordinances as may be deemed necessary to implement such complete
COMPREHENSIVE PLAN.
   PLANNING COMMISSION or COMMISSION. The Municipal Planning Commission.
   PUBLIC PLACE. Any tracts owned by the city.
   STREETS. Includes streets, avenues, boulevards, highways, roads, lanes,
alleys, and all public ways.
   UNIT OF GOVERNMENT. Any federal, state, regional, county, or municipal
government.
   UTILITY. Any facility used in rendering service which the public has a right
to demand.
(Prior Code, § 10-3)
§ 10-4 MUNICIPAL PLANNING COMMISSION; GENERALLY.
   The Municipal Planning Commission shall consist of not less than five, nor
more than 15, individuals, all of whom shall be freeholders and residents of
the city. They shall be qualified by knowledge and experience in matters
pertaining to the development of the city. They shall include representatives
of business, industry, and labor, and shall be nominated by the Mayor, subject
to the confirmation of the governing body. At least three-fifths of the
Commission’s members shall be residents of the city for a period of ten years
prior to nomination and confirmation. One member of the Commission shall also
be a member of the governing body of the city, and one member shall also be a
member of the administrative department of the city, the term of these two
members to be coextensive with the term of office to which they have been
elected or appointed. The governing body and the Mayor, however, may designate
others to serve as the city’s representatives on the Commission, so long as
such designation occurs at the first regular meeting of the Commission each
year. The remaining members of the Commission first selected shall serve terms
of one year, two years, and three years, respectively. Thereafter, members
shall be selected for terms of three years each. Vacancies shall be filled for
the unexpired term only, in the same manner as original selections are made.
Members of the Commission shall serve without compensation, but shall be
reimbursed for all necessary expenses incurred in the performance of their
official duties.
(Prior Code, § 10-4)
§ 10-5 ADVISORY MEMBERS.
   (A)   A designated representative of the County Planning Commission may
serve as an advisory member of the Municipal Planning Commission.
   (B)   A designated representative of the Municipal Planning Commission may
serve as an advisory member of the County Planning Commission.
   (C)   All such advisory members shall have all the privileges of membership,
except the right to vote.
(Prior Code, § 10-5)
§ 10-6 REGULAR AND SPECIAL MEETINGS.
   (A)   The Commission shall fix the time and place for holding regular
meetings, but it shall meet at least once in the months of January, April,
July, and October.
   (B)   Special meetings of the Commission may be called by the President or
by at least two members, upon submission of a written request to the Secretary.
The Secretary shall send to all members at least two days in advance of a
special meeting, a written notice fixing the date, time, and place of the
meeting, but written notice of a special meeting is not required if the date,
time, and place of the special meeting have been fixed in a regular meeting.
(Prior Code, § 10-6)
§ 10-7 QUORUM.
   A majority of the members of the Commission shall constitute a quorum. No
action of the Planning Commission shall be official unless authorized by a
majority of all of the members of the Commission at a regular or properly
called special meeting.
(Prior Code, § 10-7)
§ 10-8 OFFICES; APPROPRIATION FOR EXPENSES.
   The City Council shall provide the Commission with suitable offices for the
holding of meetings and the preservation of plans, maps, documents, and
accounts, and shall provide by appropriation a sum sufficient to defray the
necessary expenses of the Commission.
(Prior Code, § 10-8)
§ 10-9 ELECTION OF OFFICERS.
   At its first regular meeting in each year, the Commission shall elect from
its members a President and Vice-President. The Vice-President shall assume the
powers and responsibilities of the President during his or her absence or
disability.
(Prior Code, § 10-9)
§ 10-10 APPOINTMENT, DUTIES, AND COMPENSATION FOR SECRETARY AND EMPLOYEES;
SPECIAL AND TEMPORARY SERVICES; LEGAL ASSISTANCE.
   (A)   The Commission shall appoint and prescribe the duties and fix the
compensation of a Secretary and such employees as are necessary for the
discharge of duties and responsibilities of the Commission. All such
compensation, however, be in conformity to, and in compliance with the salaries
and compensation fixed by the governing body.
   (B)   The Commission may make contracts for special or temporary services
and any professional counsel. The City Solicitor, upon request and without
additional compensation, shall render legal assistance and service to the
Commission.
(Prior Code, § 10-10)
§ 10-11 ADMINISTRATIVE POWERS AND AUTHORITY.
   To effectuate the purposes of this article, the Commission shall have the
power, authority, and duty to:
   (A)   Exercise general supervision of, and make rules and regulations for,
the administration of the affairs of the Commission;
   (B)   Prescribe uniform rules and regulations pertaining to its
investigations and hearings;
   (C)   Supervise the fiscal affairs and responsibilities of the Commission;
   (D)   (1)   Prescribe the qualifications of, appoint, remove, and fix the
compensation of the employees, of the Commission; and
      (2)   Such compensation is to be in conformity to, and in compliance
with, the salaries and compensation fixed by the governing body.
   (E)   Delegate to employees authority to perform ministerial acts in all
cases, except where the final action of the Commission is necessary;
   (F)   Keep an accurate and complete record of all departmental proceedings,
and record and file all bonds and contracts, and assume responsibility for the
custody and preservation of all papers and documents of the Commission;
   (G)   Make recommendations and an annual report to the governing body
concerning the operation of the Commission and the status of planning within
its jurisdiction;
   (H)   Prepare, publish, and distribute reports, ordinances, and other
materials relating to the activities authorized under this article;
   (I)   Adopt a seal and certify all official acts;
   (J)   Pursue any legal, equitable, or special remedy for the enforcement of
the provisions of this article or any ordinance, rule, and regulation, or any
action taken thereunder;
   (K)   Prepare and submit an annual budget in the same manner as other
municipal departments, and the Commission shall be limited in all expenditures
to the provisions made therefor by the governing body;
   (L)   If deemed necessary, establish an advisory committee or committees;
and
   (M)   (1)   Delegate to a committee, composed of one or more members of the
Commission, the power to hold any public hearings or conferences required or
permitted under this article to be held by the Commission.
      (2)   If the hearing or conference is held by a committee, a written
record of the substance of the hearing or conference shall be made and
preserved with the records of the Commission for not less than five years.
      (3)   The committee shall [Missing Text] authority only to conduct the
hearing and report to the Commission.
(Prior Code, § 10-11)
§ 10-12 EXPENDITURES; DISPOSITION OF GIFTS; PARTICIPATION IN FEDERAL PLANNING
ASSISTANCE PROGRAMS.
   (A)   The Planning Commission shall have the power and authority to expend,
under regular municipal procedure, all sums appropriated to it for the purposes
and activities authorized under this article.
   (B)   Any monies accepted shall be deposited with the city in a special non-
reverting [Missing Text] Planning Commission Fund to be available for
expenditures for the purpose designated by the donor. The Municipal Recorder
shall draw warrants against such funds only on vouchers signed by the President
and Secretary of the Commission.
   (C)   The Planning Commission is empowered and authorized to accept, spend,
and use funds provided for the purposes of this article by the government of
the United States, and any other agency or group. Those interests are in
harmony with such purposes, in accordance with federal requirements and subject
to such conditions or limitations the Constitution or law of this state may
provide.
(Prior Code, § 10-12)

§ 10-13 COMPREHENSIVE PLAN FOR PHYSICAL DEVELOPMENT OF TERRITORY.
   The Planning Commission shall make, and recommend for adoption to the
governing body, a Comprehensive Plan for the physical development of the
territory within the corporate limits of the city. In preparing a Comprehensive
Plan, the Planning Commission shall make careful and comprehensive surveys and
studies of the existing conditions and probable future changes of such
conditions within the corporate limits of the city.
(Prior Code, § 10-13)
§ 10-14 SAME; CONTENTS.
   The Comprehensive Plan may include the following, or a study of the
following:
   (A)   Careful and comprehensive surveys and studies of existing conditions
and the probable future growth of the municipality;
   (B)   Maps , plats, charts, and descriptive material presenting basic
information, locations, extent, and character of any of the following:
      (1)   History, population, and physical site conditions;
      (2)   Land use, including the height, area, bulk, and location, and use
of private and public structures and premises;
      (3)   Population densities;
      (4)   Community centers and neighborhood units;
      (5)   Blighted and slum areas;
      (6)   Streets, including bridges, viaducts, subways, parkways, and other
public ways and places;
      (7)   Sewers, sanitation, and drainage, including handling treatment and
disposal of excess drainage waters, sewage, garbage, refuse, wastes, ashes,
trash, and other similar matters;
      (8)   Stream pollution;
      (9)   Flood control and prevention;
      (10)   Public and private utilities, including water, light, heat,
communication, and other services;
      (11)   Transportation, including rail, bus, truck, air and water
transport, and their terminal facilities;
      (12)   Local mass transportation, including motor and trolley busses; or
street, elevated or underground railways, and taxicabs;
      (13)   Parks and recreation, including parks, playgrounds, reservations,
forests, public grounds, and spaces and facilities of a recreational nature;
      (14)   Public buildings and institutions, including governmental
administration and service buildings, hospitals, infirmaries, clinics, penal
and correctional institutions, and other civic and social service buildings;
      (15)   Education, including location and extent of schools, colleges, and
universities;
      (16)   Land utilization, including residence, industry, agriculture,
forests, and other uses;
      (17)   Conservation of water, soil, agricultural, and mineral resources;
and
      (18)   Any other factors which are a part of the physical, economic, or
social situation within the city.
   (C)   Reports, maps, charts, and recommendations setting forth plans for the
development, redevelopment, improvement, extension, and revision of the
subjects set out in division (B) above so as to substantially accomplish the
objective set forth in §
10-1;
   (D)   A long-range development program of public works projects, based on
the recommended plans of the Commission, for the purpose of eliminating
unplanned, unsightly, untimely, and extravagant projects, and with a view to
stabilizing industry and employment, and the keeping of such program up to date
by yearly revisions; and
   (E)   A long-range financial program of governmental expenditures in order
that such development program may be carried out, and the keeping of such
program up to date, for all separate taxing units within the city for the
purpose of assuring efficient and economic use of public funds.
(Prior Code, § 10-14)
§ 10-15 SAME; NOTICE AND PUBLIC HEARING.
   (A)   Prior to the adoption of the Comprehensive Plan, the Planning
Commission shall hold two public hearings and give at least 30 days’ notice
prior to the dates set for the hearings. The notices shall contain the date,
time, and place of the hearings, and they shall be published as Class I legal
advertisements, and advertised via any other available media (that is, radio or
television). The advertising area for such notices shall be the municipality.
   (B)   (a)   The first hearing shall be used to introduce the Comprehensive
Plan and the second hearing shall be used to gather citizen input. The second
hearing shall be held no less than five, nor more that 14, days after the first
hearing.
      (b)   After the notices for the public meeting have been advertised, the
Planning Commission shall make copies of the Comprehensive Plan available for
public inspection at the office of the Planning Commission and the Municipal
Recorder’s office.
(Prior Code, § 10-15)
§ 10-16 SAME; ADOPTION BY COMMISSION.
   After a public hearing has been held, the Commission may, by resolution,
adopt the Comprehensive Plan and recommend the ordinance to the governing body
of the city.
(Prior Code, § 10-16)
§ 10-17 SAME; CERTIFICATION AND PRESENTMENT TO GOVERNING BODY.
   (A)   Upon adoption of the Comprehensive Plan, and recommendation of the
ordinance by the Planning Commission, the Secretary shall certify a copy of the
Plan to the governing body.
   (B)   At the first meeting of the governing body, after adoption of the
plan, the Secretary or a member of the Commission shall present the Plan to the
governing body.
(Prior Code, § 10-17)
§ 10-18 SAME; CONSIDERATION OF PLAN AND ORDINANCE BY GOVERNING BODY;
PUBLICATION.
   After presentation of the Plan to the governing body, the governing body
shall proceed to a consideration of the Plan and ordinance, and shall either
adopt, reject, or amend the plan. If the ordinance adopting the Comprehensive
Plan is published, the Plan may be incorporated by reference in the ordinance
and the full text of said Plan not published.
(Prior Code, § 10-18)
§ 10-19 SAME; REJECTION OR AMENDMENT BY GOVERNING BODY; CONSIDERATION AND
REPORT BY COMMISSION.
   (A)   If the governing body rejects the Plan and ordinance or amends it,
then it shall be returned to the Planning Commission, along with a written
explanation of the reasons for its rejection or amendment.
   (B)   (1)   The Planning Commission shall have 45 days in which to consider
the rejection or amendment and report back to the governing body.
      (2)   If the Commission approves the amendment, the ordinance shall stand
as adopted by the governing body as of the date of the filing of the
Commission’s report with the governing body.
      (3)   If the Commission disapproves of the rejection or amendment, it
shall state its reasons for such disapproval in the report, and the governing
body shall again consider the Plan and ordinance, and its action in rejecting
or amending said Plan and ordinance, after such consideration, shall be final.
   (C)   In case the Commission does not file a report with the governing body
within 45 days, the action in rejecting or amending the Plan and ordinance
shall be final.
(Prior Code, § 10-19)
§ 10-20 SAME; AMENDMENT OF PLAN AND ORDINANCE AFTER ADOPTION.
   After the adoption of a Comprehensive Plan and ordinance, all amendments to
it shall be adopted according to the procedures set forth in §§
10-15 through
10-19, except that publication of the notices of the date, time , and place of
the hearings upon such amendment need only be 15 or more days prior to the date
of the hearing. If the governing body desires an amendment, it may direct the
Planning Commission to prepare an amendment and submit it to public hearings
within 60 days after formal written request by the governing body.
(Prior Code, § 10-20)
§ 10-21 SAME; VALIDATION OF PRIOR ACTION.
   The adoption of a Comprehensive Plan, or any general development plans, by a
Planning Commission under the authority of prior acts is hereby validated and
shall continue in effect until amended under authority of this chapter.
(Prior Code, § 10-21)
§ 10-22 SAME; INTERDEPARTMENTAL COOPERATION.
   Whenever the Planning Commission undertakes the preparation of a
Comprehensive Plan, the various municipal officials and departments shall make
available, upon the request of the Commission, such information as it relates
to the Commission’s activity.
(Prior Code, § 10-22)
§ 10-23 JURISDICTION OF MUNICIPAL PLANNING COMMISSION.
   The authority of the Planning Commission shall not extend beyond the
corporate limits of the city.
(Prior Code, § 10-23)
ARTICLE 3: SUBDIVISION CONTROL
Section
   
10-24   Subdivision plats; approval required prior to recordation

10-27   Same; effect of approval or disapproval

10-31   Improvement location permits; authority to issue and control

§ 10-24 SUBDIVISION PLATS; APPROVAL REQUIRED PRIOR TO RECORDATION.
   After a Comprehensive Plan and an ordinance, containing provisions for
subdivision control and the approval of plats and replats, has been adopted by
the governing body and a certified copy of the ordinance has been filed with
the Clerk of the County Commission, a plat of a subdivision must be approved by
the Planning Commission before it can be recorded.
(Prior Code, § 10-24)
§ 10-25 SAME; APPLICATION FOR APPROVAL; NOTICE AND HEARING.
   (A)   A person desiring the approval of a plat shall submit a written
application for approval, together with a copy of the proposed plat, to the
Planning Commission.
   (B)   Upon receipt of the application, the Planning Commission, if it
tentatively approves the application, shall set a date, time, and place for a
hearing, notify the applicant in writing, and notify by publication in the
manner specified in §
10-15.
(Prior Code, § 10-25)
§ 10-26 SAME; BASIS FOR COMMISSION’S ACTION UPON APPLICATION FOR APPROVAL.
   (A)   In determining whether an application for approval shall be granted,
the Commission shall determine if the plat provides for:
      (1)   Coordination of subdivision streets with existing and planned
streets;
      (2)   Coordination with and extension of facilities included in the
Comprehensive Plan;
      (3)   Establishment of minimum width, depth, and area of lots within the
projected subdivision;
      (4)   Distribution of population and traffic in a manner tending to
create conditions favorable to health, safety, convenience, and the harmonious
development of the city; and
      (5)   Fair allocations of areas for streets, parks, schools, public and
semi-public buildings, homes, utilities, business, and industry.
   (B)   As a condition of approval of a plat, the Commission may specify:
      (1)   The manner in which streets and sidewalks shall be laid out,
graded, and improved;
      (2)   Provisions for water, sewage, and other utility services;
      (3)   Provisions for schools;
      (4)   Provisions for essential municipal services; and
      (5)   Provisions for recreational facilities.
(Prior Code, § 10-26)
§ 10-27 SAME; EFFECT OF APPROVAL OR DISAPPROVAL.
   (A)   Following the hearing, the Commission shall either approve or
disapprove the application for approval of the plat.
   (B)   If the Commission approves the application, it shall affix the
Commission’s seal upon the plat. If it disapproves the application, it shall
set forth its own records and provide the applicant with a copy thereof.
   (C)   The applicant may re-submit his or her plat for approval, provided he
or she alleviates the reasons given for its original disapproval.
(Prior Code, § 10-27)
§ 10-28 SAME; APPLICATION FEES.
   The Planning Commission shall charge a fee of ________ for all applications
for approval of plates.
(Prior Code, § 10-28)
§ 10-29 SAME; PLATS FILED WITHOUT APPROVAL.
   (A)   The filing and recording of a plat involving the subdivision of lands
covered by the Comprehensive Plan and ordinance shall be without legal effect
unless approved by the Planning Commission.
   (B)   Provided, that failure to comply with this section shall not
invalidate or affect the title to any land within the area of such plat.
(Prior Code, § 10-29)
§ 10-30 SAME; CONDITIONAL APPROVAL; BONDS.
   (A)   The Planning Commission may approve a plat for a subdivision in which
the improvements and installations have not been completed, as required by the
ordinance, for the approval of plats if the applicant provides a bond which
shall:
      (1)   Run to the city;
      (2)   Be in an amount determined by the Commission to be sufficient to
complete the improvements and installations;
      (3)   Be with surety satisfactory to the Planning Commission; and
      (4)   Specify the time for the completion of the improvements and
installations.
   (B)   If the applicant fails to complete the improvements and installations,
the city may carry out such improvements and installations.
(Prior Code, § 10-30)
§ 10-31 IMPROVEMENT LOCATION PERMITS; AUTHORITY TO ISSUE AND CONTROL.
   (A)   An improvement location permit for a structure of platted or unplatted
lands shall not be issued unless the structure and its location conform to this
city’s Comprehensive Plan and ordinance.
   (B)   The Municipal Building Inspector shall have the authority to issue and
control improvement location permits within this city.
(Prior Code, § 10-31)
§ 10-32 REVIEW OF DECISIONS OF COMMISSION BY CERTIORARI.
   A decision of the Planning Commission may be reviewed by a writ of
certiorari in a court of competent jurisdiction. A petition for certiorari
shall specify the grounds upon which it is alleged that the Commission’s action
is illegal or improper. Such petition must be filed within 60 days following
the Commission’s decision.
(Prior Code, § 10-32)
ARTICLE 4: ZONING
Section
   
10-33   Zoning Authority; generally
   
10-34   Zoning District; generally
   
10-35   Same; preliminary study
   
10-36   Procedures; tentative report; notice and hearings
   
10-37   Same; action by governing body on tentative report

10-39   Supplemental and amending ordinances
   
10-40   Changes of zoning rules and regulations; petition for change

10-42   Election on zoning ordinance; form of ballots or ballot labels;

10-43   Existing uses safeguarded
§ 10-33 ZONING AUTHORITY; GENERALLY.
   In order to obtain the objectives stated in §
10-1, the governing body shall have and exercise the following powers:
   (A)   To classify, regulate, and limit the height, area, bulk, and use of
buildings hereafter to be erected;
   (B)   To regulate and determine the area of front, rear and side yards,
courts, and other open spaces about such buildings;
   (C)   To regulate and determine the use and intensity of use of land and lot
areas;
   (D)   To classify, regulate, and restrict the location of trades, callings,
industries, commercial enterprises, and the location of buildings designed for
specified uses;
   (E)   To regulate and control, or prohibit in certain areas, junk yards,
dumps, or automobile or appliance grave yards, or the maintenance and operation
of second hand stores or outlets in residential areas;
   (F)   To classify and designate the rural lands among agricultural,
industrial, commercial, residential,
and other uses and purposes; and
   (G)   To divide the municipality into districts of such kind, character,
number, shape, and area as may be necessary to carry out the purposes of this
section.
(Prior Code, § 10-33)
§ 10-34 ZONING DISTRICT; GENERALLY.
   The various kinds of districts created in order to carry out the purposes of
§
10-33, need not necessarily cover or include the same territory, and may
overlap or coincide. The districts created shall also be subject to the
following:
   (A)   Rules and regulations as to height, area, bulk, and use of buildings
and as to the area of all yards, courts, and open spaces shall be uniform for
each class of buildings throughout each district;
   (B)   For each district designated for the location of trades, callings,
industries, commercial enterprises, or buildings, or designated for specified
uses, rules and regulations may be enforced specifying uses that shall be
excluded or subjected to reasonable requirements of a special nature, and
designating the use for which buildings may not be erected, altered, or used;
   (C)   The rules and regulations in one or more districts of the same kind or
character may differ from those in other like districts, but shall be uniform
for each district; and
   (D)   Several parts of the municipality may be classified within a single
district, although not contiguous.
(Prior Code, § 10-34)
§ 10-35 SAME; PRELIMINARY STUDY.
   In establishing such districts and rules and regulations, the governing body
shall give reasonable regard to existing conditions, the character of buildings
erected in each district, the most desirable use for which the land in each
district may be adapted, and the conservation of property values throughout the
city.
(Prior Code, § 10-35)
§ 10-36 PROCEDURES; TENTATIVE REPORT; NOTICE AND HEARINGS.
   (A)   (1)   Recommendations as to the boundaries of district and rules and
regulations, and restrictions, to be enforced shall be prepared by the Planning
Commission.
      (2)   The Commission may prepare the tentative report on its own
initiative, or the governing body may require its preparation.
   (B)   The Commission shall hold preliminary hearings and conferences on such
dates at such times and places, and upon such notice as it may determine to be
necessary to inform and aid itself in the preparation of the tentative report.
   (C)   The tentative report, which shall include the proposed zoning
ordinance with explanatory maps, shall be made to the governing body by the
Secretary of the Commission.
(Prior Code, § 10-36)
§ 10-37 SAME; ACTION BY GOVERNING BODY ON TENTATIVE REPORT.
   (A)   The governing body shall consider the tentative report and shall
return it, with any suggestions and recommendations, to the Planning Commission
for its final report.
   (B)   Until the final report of the Commission is received by the governing
body, no zoning ordinance shall be adopted.
(Prior Code, § 10-37)
§ 10-38 SAME; FINAL REPORT; NOTICE AND HEARING; ACTION.
   After the Planning Commission submits the final report, the governing body
shall give all interested persons an opportunity to be heard, with reference to
the final report, at public hearings convenient for all persons affected.
Notices of the dates, times, and places of such hearings shall be published as
Class II legal advertisements within 14 consecutive days preceding the date set
for the hearings. The notices shall state that the report contains a
comprehensive zoning ordinance for the city, that written objections to the
final report, filed with the Municipal Recorder at or before the hearings, will
be heard, and that the hearings will be continued from time to time as may be
found necessary. During the time between the date of the first publication of
the notice and the date of the hearing, the final report shall be on file in
the office of the Planning Commission, available for public inspection. Upon
completion of the public hearings, the governing body shall proceed to the
consideration of the ordinance.
(Prior Code, § 10-38)
§ 10-39 SUPPLEMENTAL AND AMENDING ORDINANCES.
   The governing body may, from time to time, amend, supplement, or change the
rules and regulations, and districts, fixed by ordinance hereunder.
(Prior Code, § 10-39)
§ 10-40 CHANGES OF ZONING RULES AND REGULATIONS; PETITION FOR CHANGE.
   Petitions, duly signed, may be presented to the Municipal Recorder
requesting an amendment, supplement of, or instead of changing of rules and
regulations of the zoning ordinance by:
   (A)   The Planning Commission; or
   (B)   The owners of 50% or more of the real property area to which the
petition relates.
(Prior Code, § 10-40)
§ 10-41 SAME; CONSIDERED AS AMENDMENTS TO COMPREHENSIVE PLAN; NOTICE AND
HEARING.
   (A)   Amendments, supplements, or changes of the rules and regulations of
the zoning ordinance shall be considered as amendments to the Comprehensive
Plan. Any proposed ordinance for the amendment, supplement, change, or repeal
of the zoning ordinance, not originating upon petition of the Planning
Commission, shall be referred to the Commission for consideration and report
before any final action is taken by the governing body.
   (B)   Prior to submission to the governing body of a Planning Commission
petition or a report on a proposed ordinance referred to it for amendment,
supplement, change, or repeal of the zoning ordinance, the Commission shall
give notices and hold public hearings in the manner prescribed under § 10-15,
except that publication need be made only 15 or more days prior to the date set
for such hearings.
(Prior Code, § 10-41)
§ 10-42 ELECTION ON ZONING ORDINANCE; FORM OF BALLOTS OR BALLOT LABELS;
PROCEDURE.
   (A)   If, within 60 days following adoption of the zoning ordinance by the
governing body, a petition is filed with the Municipal Recorder asking for
submission of the zoning ordinance to the qualified voters of the city, such
ordinance shall not take effect until the ordinance has been approved by a
majority of the legal votes cast at any regular primary, or general or special,
election called for that purpose. The petition must be signed by a number of
qualified voters, in their own handwriting, residing in the area affected by
the proposed zoning equal to not less than 15% of the total legal votes cast in
the affected area for all candidates for Governor at the last preceding general
election at which a Governor was elected. Only qualified voters residing in the
area affected by the proposed ordinance shall be eligible to vote with respect
thereto.
   (B)   Upon the ballots, or ballot labels where voting machines are used,
there shall be written or printed the following:
 
    For Zoning
 
    Against Zoning
 
   (C)   If a majority of the legal votes cast upon the question be for zoning,
the provisions of the zoning ordinance shall, upon the date the results of such
an election are declared, be effective. If a majority of the legal votes cast
upon the question be against zoning, said zoning ordinance shall not take
effect, but the question may again be submitted to a vote at any regular,
primary, or general election in the manner herein provided.
   (D)   The governing body shall designate whether such election shall be held
as a primary, general, or special election. The election at which the question
of zoning is voted upon shall be held at the voting precincts established for
holding primary or general elections. All of the provisions of the general
election laws of this state concerning primary, general, or special elections,
when not in conflict with the provisions of this article, shall apply to voting
and elections hereunder, insofar as practicable.
   (E)   Notice of all elections at which the question of zoning is voted upon
shall be given by publication of the order calling for a vote on such question
as a Class II legal advertisement. The publication area for such publication
shall be the area in which voting on the question of zoning is to be conducted.
(Prior Code, § 10-42)
§ 10-43 EXISTING USES SAFEGUARDED.
   The zoning ordinance or ordinances shall not prohibit the continuance of the
use of any land, building, or structure for the purpose for which such land,
building, or structure is used at the time the zoning ordinance or ordinances
take effect, but any alteration or addition to any land, building, or structure
for the purpose of carrying on any use prohibited under the zoning rules and
regulations applicable to the district may be prohibited; provided, that no
such prohibition shall apply to alterations or additions to, or replacement of,
buildings or structures by any farmer, industry, or manufacturer, or to the use
of land presently owned by any farmer, industry, or manufacturer but not used
for agricultural, industrial, or manufacturing purposes, or to the use or
acquisition of additional land which may be required for the protection,
continuing development, or expansion of any agricultural, industrial, or
manufacturing operation, or any present or future satellite agricultural,
industrial, or manufacturing use.
(Prior Code, § 10-43)
ARTICLE 5: BOARD OF ZONING APPEALS
Section

§ 10-44 CREATION; MEMBERSHIP; TERMS; VACANCIES.
   (A)   As part of the zoning ordinance, the governing body hereby establishes
the Board of Zoning Appeals, consisting of five members to be appointed by the
Mayor, subject to the confirmation of the governing body.
   (B)   The members of the Board of Zoning Appeals shall be individuals who
are freeholders and residents of the city, and at least three-fifths of such
members shall have been residents of the city for at least ten years preceding
the time of their appointment. No member of the Board of Zoning Appeals shall
be a member of the Planning Commission, nor shall any member hold other
elective or appointive offices in the municipal government, nor shall more than
one particular interest or profession be represented.
   (C)   Members of the Board shall serve without compensation, but shall be
reimbursed for all reasonable and necessary expenses incurred in the
performance of their duties.
   (D)   Upon initial creation of the Board of Zoning Appeals, the members
shall be appointed for the following terms: One for a term of one year; two for
a term of two years; and two for a term of three years. The terms shall expire
on January 1 of the first, second, and third year, respectively, following
their appointment. Thereafter, as their terms expire, each new appointment
shall be for a term of three years.
   (E)   If a vacancy occurs on the Board of Zoning Appeals, the Mayor shall
appoint a new member, subject to the confirmation of the governing body, for
the length of the unexpired term.
(Prior Code, § 10-44)
§ 10-45 OFFICERS; QUORUM; COMPENSATION OF SECRETARY AND EMPLOYEES.
   (A)   (1)   At its first meeting of each year, the Board of Zoning Appeals
shall elect a Chairperson and Vice-Chairperson from its membership.
      (2)   The Vice-Chairperson shall have the power and authority to act as
Chairperson whenever the Chairperson is unable to discharge the duties of his
or her office.
   (B)   A majority of the members of the Board of Zoning Appeals shall
constitute a quorum. No action of the Board shall be official, unless
authorized by a majority of its members.
   (C)   The Board of Zoning Appeals may appoint and fix the compensation of a
Secretary and such employees as are necessary for the discharge of its duties,
all in conformity to, and in compliance with, the rates of compensation set by
the governing body.
(Prior Code, § 10-45)
§ 10-46 OFFICES; APPROPRIATION FOR EXPENSES.
   The governing body shall provide the Board of Zoning Appeals with suitable
offices and shall appropriate enough money to sufficiently defray the
reasonable expense of the Board.
(Prior Code, § 10-46)
§ 10-47 RULES AND REGULATIONS AND PROCEDURES; MINUTES AND RECORDS.
   (A)   The Board of Zoning appeals shall adopt such rules and regulations
concerning the filing of appeals, applications for vacancies and exceptions,
the giving of notice, and the conduct of hearing as may be necessary to carry
out its duties under and the terms of this article.
   (B)   The Board shall keep minutes of its proceedings, keep records of all
official actions and shall record the vote on all actions taken. All minutes
and records shall be filed in the office of the Board and shall be public
records.
(Prior Code, § 10-47)
§ 10-48 POWERS; AUTHORITY AND DUTIES.
   The Board of Zoning Appeals shall:
   (A)   Hear and determine appeals from and review any orders, requirements,
decisions, or determinations made by an administrative official or board
charged with the enforcement of any ordinance or rule and regulation adopted
pursuant to §§
10-34 to
10-44 of this chapter;
   (B)   Permit and authorize exceptions to the district rules and regulations
only in the classes of cases or in a particular situation, as specified in the
Zoning Ordinance;
   (C)   Hear and decide special exceptions to the terms required to act under
the ordinance; and
   (D)   Authorize upon appeal in specific cases such variance from the terms
of the zoning ordinance as will not be contrary to the public interest, where,
owing to special conditions, a literal enforcement of the provisions of the
zoning ordinance will result in undue hardship, and so that the spirit of the
zoning ordinance shall be observed and substantial justice done.
(Prior Code, § 10-48)
§ 10-49 HEARING OF APPEAL.
   The Board of Zoning Appeals shall fix a reasonable time for the hearing of
an appeal. Public notice of the hearing shall be given in the manner specified
in § 10-15 of this chapter. Notice shall also be given, by registered mail, to
all persons who own property within a three block radius of the affected area
and a sign shall be posted on the affected premises, indicating the date, time,
and place of the hearing.
(Prior Code, § 10-49)
§ 10-50 STAYING OF WORK ON PREMISES WHEN APPEAL TAKEN; EXCEPTION.
   When an appeal has been taken and filed with the Board of Zoning Appeals,
all proceedings and work on the premises in question shall be stayed unless the
administrative official or board from whom or which the appeal is taken shall
certify that, by reason of facts stated in the certificate, a stay would cause
imminent peril to life or property. If such certificate be filed, proceedings
or work on the premises shall not be stayed, except by a restraining order
granted by a court of competent jurisdiction.
(Prior Code, § 10-50)
§ 10-51 PETITION FOR WRIT OF CERTIORARI FROM DECISION OR ORDER.
   (A)   Every decision or order of the Board of Zoning Appeals shall be
subject to review by certiorari in a court of competent jurisdiction. The
provisions of §
10-32 shall also apply in this section.
   (B)   Upon review by certiorari, all proceedings and work on the premises in
question shall be stayed unless the administrative official or board from whom
or which the appeal is taken shall certify that a stay would cause imminent
peril to life or property.
(Prior Code, § 10-51)
ARTICLE 6: ENFORCEMENT PROVISIONS
Section
   
10-52   Enforcement
   
10-53   Injunction
   
10-54   Penalty
   
10-55   Conflicts of law
§ 10-52 ENFORCEMENT.
   The governing body shall provide penalties, as set out in §
10-54 of this chapter, for failure to comply with the provisions of any
ordinance or rule and regulation adopted pursuant to the provisions of this
chapter. Any buildings erected, raised, or converted on land or premises used
in violation of any provision of any ordinance or rule and regulation adopted
under the authority of this chapter shall be considered a common nuisance. The
owner of such building, land, or premises shall be liable for maintaining a
common nuisance.
(Prior Code, § 10-52)
§ 10-53 INJUNCTION.
   The Planning Commission, the Board of Zoning Appeals, or any designated
official may seek an injunction in a court of competent jurisdiction to
restrain a person or unit of government form violating the provisions of this
article or of any ordinance or rule and regulation adopted pursuant hereto. The
Planning Commission, the Board of Zoning Appeals, or any designated enforcement
official (building inspector) may also seek a mandatory injunction in a court
of competent jurisdiction directing a person or unit of government to remove a
structure erected in violation of the provisions of this article or of any
ordinance or rule and regulation adopted pursuant hereto. If the Planning
Commission, the Board of Zoning Appeals, or the designated enforcement official
is successful in any such suit, the respondent shall bear the costs of the
action.
(Prior Code, § 10-53)
§ 10-54 PENALTY.
   Any person who violates any provision of this article shall be guilty of a
misdemeanor and, upon conviction, shall be fined not less than $10 nor more
than $200 dollars.
(Prior Code, § 10-54)
§ 10-55 CONFLICTS OF LAW.
   Whenever any provision of this article conflicts with the provisions of any
ordinance, or statute, the provisions which establish a higher standard shall
prevail.
(Prior Code, § 10-55)
