§ 11-1 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this chapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   MUNICIPAL PUBLIC WORKS, WORKS, or PROJECTS.
      (1)   The construction or repair of public buildings, utilities, or
property.
      (2)   The construction, reconstruction, establishment, acquisition,
improvement, renovation, extension, enlargement, increase, equipment,
maintenance, repair (including replacements), and operation of jails, jail
facilities, municipal buildings, police stations, fire stations, libraries,
museums, other public buildings, incinerator plants, land fill or other garbage
disposal systems, hospitals, piers, docks, terminals, airports, drainage
systems, flood control systems, stormwater systems and associated stormwater
management program, flood walls, culverts, bridges (including approaches,
causeways, viaducts, underpasses, and connecting roadways), public markets,
cemeteries, motor vehicle parking facilities (including parking lots,
buildings, ramps, curb-line parking, meters, and other facilities considered
necessary, appropriate, useful, convenient, or incidental to the regulation,
control, and parking of motor vehicles), farms, dormitories, apartments, and
other housing facilities for the students and faculties of institutions of
higher education; facilities providing housing for the elderly, including, but
not limited to, life care facilities, congregate living facilities and adult
residential facilities, stadiums, gymnasiums, sports arenas, auditoriums,
public recreation centers, public recreation parks, swimming pools, roller
skating rinks, ice skating rinks, tennis courts, golf courses, polo grounds, or
the grading, regrading, paving, repaving, surfacing, resurfacing, curbing,
recurbing, widening, or otherwise improving of any street, avenue, road, alley,
or way, or the building or renewing of sidewalks, where works or projects will
be made self-supporting, and the cost thereof, together with the interest
thereon, will be returned within a reasonable period, not exceeding 40 years,
by means of tolls, fees, rents, special assessments, or charges other than
taxation; and the terms shall also mean any works or project as a whole, and
all integral parts thereof, including all necessary, appropriate, useful,
convenient, or incidental appurtenances and equipment in connection with any
one or more of the above.
(W. Va. Code § 8-16-1)
   STORMWATER MANAGEMENT PROGRAM.
      (1)   The activities associated with the management, operation,
maintenance, and control of stormwater and stormwater systems, and shall
include, but not be limited to, public education, stormwater and surface runoff
water quality improvement, mapping, planning, flood control, inspection,
enforcement, and any other activities required by state and federal law.
      (2)   The term STORMWATER MANAGEMENT PROGRAM shall not include those
activities associated with the management, operation, maintenance, and control
of highways, road, and drainage easements, and/or stormwater facilities
constructed, owned, and/or operated by the State Division of Highways without
the express agreement of the Commissioner of Highways.
(W. Va. Code § 8-16-1)
   STORMWATER SYSTEMS.
      (1)   A STORMWATER SYSTEM in its entirety or any integral part thereof
used to collect and dispose of stormwater and an associated stormwater
management program. It includes all facilities, structures, and natural
watercourses used for collecting and conducting stormwater to, through and from
drainage areas to the points of final outlet including, but not limited to, any
and all of the following: Inlets, conduits, outlets, channels, ponds, drainage
easements, water quality facilities, catch basins, ditches, streams, gulches,
flumes, culverts, siphons, retention or detention basins, dams, floodwalls,
pipes, flood control systems, levies, and pumping stations.
      (2)   The term STORMWATER SYSTEMS shall not include highways, roads, and
drainage easements, and/or stormwater facilities constructed, owned, and/or
operated by the State Division of Highways.
(W. Va. Code § 8-16-1)
(Prior Code, § 11-1)
§ 11-2 PUBLIC USES FOR WHICH PRIVATE PROPERTY CAN BE TAKEN OR DAMAGED.
   The public uses for which private property can be taken or damaged are as
follows:
   (A)   For the construction of railways, waterways, roadways, sidewalks,
storm sewers, or other works for internal improvement used by public works;
   (B)   For the construction of telephone and power plants used by the public;
   (C)   For construction, maintaining, and operating the works of natural
resources;
   (D)   For constructing, maintaining, and operating water plants;
   (E)   For the purpose of constructing, maintaining, and operating sewer
systems and sewage plants;
   (F)   For the reasonable use of, and incorporated company engaged in, public
enterprises of which the municipality is sole or part owner;
   (G)   For buildings, parks, recreation areas, monuments, and the like, of
the municipality;
   (H)   For cemeteries or enlarging existing ones;
   (I)   For public schools, libraries, and hospitals; and
   (J)   For constructing, maintaining, and operating pipelines, plants,
systems, and storage facilities; for the transportation by common carrier as a
public utility of coal and its derivatives, and all mixtures and combinations.
(W. Va. Code § 8-16-1) (Prior Code, § 11-2)
§ 11-3 MUNICIPALITIES AUTHORIZED TO CONSTRUCT, AND THE LIKE, PUBLIC WORKS, AND
TO ACQUIRE PROPERTY; PAYMENT OF COSTS.
   The municipality is, and any two or more municipalities acting jointly,
whether situate in the same county or different counties, are, hereby empowered
and authorized to construct, reconstruct, establish, acquire, improve,
renovate, extend, enlarge, increase, own, equip, repair (including
replacements), maintain and operate any municipal public works, together with
all appurtenances necessary, appropriate, useful, convenient, or incidental for
or to the maintenance and operation of such works, and shall have plenary power
and authority to acquire by gift, grant, purchase, condemnation, or otherwise,
and thereafter hold, all necessary lands, rights, easements, rights-of-way,
franchises, and other property therefor within or without, or partly within and
partly without, the corporate limits of any such municipality or
municipalities, and to issue revenue bonds to pay the costs of such public
works and properties; provided, that this section shall not be construed to
authorize any municipality to construct, reconstruct, establish, acquire,
improve, renovate, extend, enlarge, increase, own, equip, repair (including
replacements), maintain, or operate any works which would render a service
already being adequately rendered within such municipality. No obligation shall
be incurred by any municipality in such construction, reconstruction,
establishment, acquisition, improvement, renovation, extension, enlargement, or
increase, except such as is payable solely from the funds provided under the
authority of this article.
(W. Va. Code § 8-16-2) (Prior Code, § 11-3)
§ 11-4 OBLIGATION PAID BY GENERAL OBLIGATION BONDS.
   The municipality may issue general obligation bonds for public works
projects, the price of which shall not be below the par value of the bond. The
sale of general obligation bonds shall be governed by the restrictions and
limitations of the United States Government, plus the indebtness of the two
shall not be more than 5% of the value of the taxable property within; nor
shall any bond be issued unless the debt will be serviced within the regular
tax levy limits prescribed in the tax limitation amendment. No general
obligation bonds shall be issued until their quest of issuing has been
submitted to the voters during an annual or special election, and three-fifths
of the people voting approve the bond.
(Prior Code, § 11-4)
§ 11-5 OBLIGATION PAID BY REVENUE BONDS.
   (A)   The municipality may issue revenue bonds for public works projects.
The revenue bonds shall not in any way be a corporate indebtness of this
municipality within the meaning of any statutory or constitutional limits
therein.
   (B)   Such revenue bonds shall bear interest at not more than 8% annum
payable semi-annually and shall mature at a time set by the resolution. Such
bond may be made redeemable before mature at not more than par value below
thereto and a premium of 5%. Said ordinance shall fix the form and denomination
of the bonds, plus the place where the principal and interest are to be paid
which may be at any bank or trust company. The bonds shall include on the front
that the municipality is not responsible for paying for the bonds, but that
payment will come from the net revenues of the works. All bonds shall be under
the Uniform Commercial Code of the state. Said bonds shall be exempt from all
taxation. All bonds shall contain the municipal seal, and all the signatures on
the bond shall remain good even if these people leave office. If the proceeds
of the bonds are not enough more may be issued. If the proceeds are too great,
the profit shall be used to pay back the bonds.
(Prior Code, § 11-5)
§ 11-6 OBLIGATION PAID BY SPECIAL ASSESSMENT.
   (A)   The cost of the public works project may be apportioned upon the
landowners whose land abuts upon the project’s rights-of-way. If the project’s
rights-of-way should be different on one street than another than the cost may
be equitably apportioned, and the cost shall only be against those whose
abutting land benefitted from the project’s rights-of-way. All situations not
covered in this section, the cost shall be apportioned equally as determined by
the governing body.
   (B)   (1)   The property abutting any project’s right-of-way may be held in
lien until such assessment, which is charged to such property, is paid. A
notice of the liens shall be certified by the Recorder and sent to the County
Clerk.
      (2)   The owner shall pay when the installments come due. If he or she
defaults his or her payments for 60 days, this municipality can demand the
entire sum owed and take legal action to obtain it based on the records as held
by the Clerk of the county.
(Prior Code, § 11-6)
§ 11-7 ISSUANCE OF GENERAL OBLIGATION BONDS TO BE REPAID BY SPECIAL
ASSESSMENTS.
   (A)   This municipality may issue general obligation bonds for improvements,
acquisition, or constriction in anticipation of special assessments, the price
of which shall not be below the par value of the bond.
   (B)   The bonds shall be payable not to exceed ten years from the date of
the issuance, and shall bear interest not to exceed 8% annum, payable annually;
and the sale of municipal bonds shall be governed by the restrictions and
limitations of the United States Government, plus the indebtness of the city
shall not be more than 5% of the value of the taxable property within; nor
shall any bond be issued unless an annual tax is imposed to pay off the
interest of all bonds and the balance in ten years.
   (C)   All money collected from the abutting landowners shall go to the
paying of the bonds. No general obligation bonds shall be issued until their
question of issuing has been submitted to the voters during an annual or
special election, in which three-fifths of the people voting approve the bond.
(Prior Code, § 11-7)
§ 11-8 ACCEPTANCE OF GRANTS; PROCUREMENT OF LOANS.
   (A)   The municipality can secure loans to build or improve its works from
federal sources, private agencies, individuals, or corporations which loan or
temporary advance money which can be repaid out of the proceeds of the bonds
issued under this article.
   (B)   In no event shall any loan or temporary advance be a general
obligation of the municipality, but shall be paid for solely from the proceeds
of the bond or the revenue of the works.
(Prior Code, § 11-8)
§ 11-9 LIMITATIONS OF ADDITIONAL ASSESSMENT.
   When the cost of constructing public works projects has been assessed
against abutting property owners, no part of the cost of a similar improvement
of the same portion of the street shall be assessed for ten years after
completion of the preceding similar assessment.
(Prior Code, § 11-9)
§ 11-10 SPECIAL PROVISIONS AS TO CERTAIN MUNICIPAL PUBLIC WORKS.
   (A)   If the works is a city parking lot, the city may use revenue from
other parking meters and lots unless they have already been committed
elsewhere.
   (B)   If the work is for a jail, the city may pledge, not to exceed 20
years, all fines and fees. This municipality may pay off early all bonds issued
for repairs of abutting property.
(Prior Code, § 11-10)
§ 11-11 CONSTRUCTION, AND THE LIKE, TO BE UNDER CONTROL OF GOVERNING BODY OR
APPOINTED BOARD, AND THE LIKE.
   (A)   The construction and repair of all works may be made up of a committee
or board containing either all or a part of the governing body (for example,
the Sanitary Board and the Parks and Recreation Board).
   (B)   The governing body shall set the powers and compensation of such Board
members, the number of members, and the way in which they are to be appointed
or selected. The Board shall be non-partisan and shall establish its own
bylaws.
(Prior Code, § 11-11)
§ 11-12 POWERS OF BOARD.
   The Board shall take all steps necessary and have the power to make
contracts and agreements in order to carry out the provisions in this article;
provided, that any contract relating to financial matters shall be approved by
the governing body. The Board shall employ and fix the rate of compensation for
those necessary, and it shall do such work as the Board directs. All expenses
incurred shall be paid by visions provided for in this article, and at no time
shall the Board spend beyond extent to which money shall have, or may have,
been provided under the authority of this article. No contract or agreement
with any contractor of over $1,000 shall be made without first having open
public bids and the award made to the best bidder. The Board shall establish
rules and regulations for the use of the works.
(Prior Code, § 11-12)
§ 11-13 RATES FOR SERVICES RENDERED BY WORKS.
   This municipality has the power to establish rates and maintain these rates
for all public works, and to charge these rates to people for services
rendered. The rates shall be used for the maintenance, improvement, and to pay
off the bonded indebtedness. All rate changes shall be subject to public
hearing.
(Prior Code, § 11-13)
§ 11-14 ACCOUNTING SYSTEM, YEARLY AUDITING, CUSTODIAN OF FUNDS.
   This municipality/Board shall maintain a proper system of accounting,
showing the amount received. All accounts shall be audited every year by a
competent auditor, and all audits shall be open to the public. The Treasurer,
or other appointed official, shall be the custodian of funds derived from the
income received from the works, and all such funds shall be kept separate from
municipal funds.
(Prior Code, § 11-14)
§ 11-15 PUBLICATION OF FINANCIAL STATEMENT.
   (A)   The Board/municipality shall publish a financial statement every year
as a Class I legal advertisement.
   (B)   It shall include all expenditures for the year and who such
expenditures went to. It shall also include the money taken in from the bonds
and how it was used, plus a report on the debts that had occurred during the
year and a final balance.
   (C)   If the Board fails these duties, every member concurring in the
failure shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and fined not less than $100 or more
than $200.
(Prior Code, § 11-15)
§ 11-16 PENALTY.
   Any person convicted of violating the provisions of this chapter shall be
guilty of a misdemeanor, and if no specific penalty is provided for, the
violation thereof shall be no less than $50 or more than a fine not exceeding
$1,000. Each day any such violation continues shall constitute a separate
offense.
(Prior Code, § 11-16)
ARTICLE 1: WATERWORKS SYSTEM
Section
   
11-100   Authorization of waterworks
   
11-101   Rates or charges for services; discontinuance of services
   
11-102   System of accounts; audits
   
11-103   Preparation and publication of financial statement
   
11-104   Declaration and injury to waterworks system
   
11-105   Filling of swimming pools, large impoundments
§ 11-100 AUTHORIZATION OF WATERWORKS.
   (A)   (1)   The municipality shall have the responsibility for the planning
and implementation of a waterworks system for the citizens of the municipality
and those other area residents whom the Council deems it feasible to serve.
      (2)   This to be accomplished in keeping with existing state statutes
with regard to health and environmental considerations, and to be enacted with
regard to the health, safety, and public interest of the citizens.
   (B)   The Council, in keeping with the statutes of the state, may engage in
contracts for the provision of planning, engineering, and construction services
with the purpose of providing water service for the residents of this
municipality and those other populations to be considered.
(Prior Code, § 11-100)
§ 11-101 RATES OR CHARGES FOR SERVICES; DISCONTINUANCE OF SERVICES.
   (A)   This municipality has the power to charge and maintain just equitable
rates to every person using the system, and to change these rates from time to
time. The revenue gained from such charges shall be used to upkeep the works
and pay off debt service requirements. All rates, if not paid when charged, may
constitute a lien, and if not paid in 30 days after the same is due, the amount
thereof, plus 10% and the attorneys fee, can be gained by the municipality in a
civil suit, and such suit may be foreclosed against such lot, parcel of land,
or building. If this course of action does not work, then the municipality may
make application to the Public Services Commission for relief.
   (B)   Whenever a rate hike is to be put into effect, a public hearing shall
be held not less that ten days after the proposal after which the hearing shall
be held and the rates shall be decided on. A copy of the rates shall be kept
with the Recorder and open to the public at all times. The aggregate of the
rates must be sufficient to maintain the care of the works and must be approved
by the Public Service Commission before being implemented.
   (C)   The municipality shall not discontinue service to any customer for
violation of rules and regulations, or for non-payment of the bill, without
first having tried diligently to induce the customer to comply with its rules
and regulations, or to pay his or her bills.
   (D)   Service shall actually be discontinued only after at least 24 hours’
written notice shall have been given to the customer by the city that bills are
five or more days delinquent, or that the violation of rules must cease;
provided, however, that where fraudulent use of water is detected, or where the
city’s regulations re-measuring equipment have been tampered with, or where a
dangerous condition is found to exist on the customer’s premises, the water may
be shut off without advance notice. In no case shall the city discontinue
service on Friday, Saturday, Sunday, or a day prior to a holiday or if an
emergency exists. All disconnections shall be performed between the hours of 8:
00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m.
   (E)   There shall be charged to, and collected form, each and every person
seeking a connection to the waterworks system of the city, prior to and as a
condition to such connection, a one-time charge of $25, which shall be non-
refundable, to reimburse the city for the estimated costs of such connection.
   (F)   If a customer of the waterworks system of the city who is moving from
one location on said system to another location on said system, the Clerk is
authorized to waive such connection or startup fee if such customer has, at the
former location to which the city has provided for his or her account water
services, promptly paid a charge therefor.
   (G)   The decision of the Clerk with respect to the waiver or non-waver of
such fee shall be final unless the customer affected shall, at the time such
waiver is refused by the Clerk, demand a hearing on such question with the
Council, and the Council shall thereupon take cognizance of such request, and
hear and determine finally such matter at the next session of Council.
(Prior Code, § 11-101)
§ 11-102 SYSTEM OF ACCOUNTS; AUDITS.
   This municipality shall establish an accounting system based on the system
of accounts as provided by the State Public Service Commission for the
waterworks system. These accounts shall be audited annually and the audit
should be made open to the public.
(Prior Code, § 11-102)
§ 11-103 PREPARATION AND PUBLICATION OF FINANCIAL STATEMENT.
   (A)   The Clerk of the municipality in charge of the accounting for the
waterworks system shall prepare a monthly income statement to be presented to
the Mayor and Council showing the cash collected and disbursed for the period.
   (B)   The municipality shall prepare an annual report including a balance
sheet, income statement, and list of assets of the waterworks system. Such a
report shall be prepared in accordance with the format and system of accounts
provided by the State Public Services Commission.
   (C)   The municipality shall publish a financial statement of the waterworks
system every year as a Class I legal advertisement.
(Prior Code, § 11-103)
§ 11-104 DECLARATION AND INJURY TO WATERWORKS SYSTEM.
   (A)   Declaration of necessity; water connection required where available.
The use of the water system of the city is determined and declared to be
essential for the protection and preservation of the public health, comfort,
safety, economy, and general welfare of the inhabitants of the city, and of the
area served by the system.
   (B)   Tapping water pipes. It shall be unlawful for any person to tap, or
cause to be tapped, any pipe belonging to the city or any water company
supplying water to any of the inhabitants of the city, or to any private pipe
connected with such water pipe, unless consent first be had from the city.
   (C)   Injury to water fixtures. It shall be unlawful for any person
willfully to break, injure, deface, or destroy any water main, meter, bend,
branch, sleeve, cap, valve, hydrant, jet, fireplug, service pipe, stopcock,
box, plate, or covering, or any other fixture or thing used or connected with
the distribution of water throughout the streets of the city, or for its
introduction into any building of the city.
   (D)   Unlawful waste, flooding, or diversion of water. It shall be unlawful
for any occupant of the premises into which water has been introduced to permit
the water to run or waste unnecessarily from any water pipe, hydrant, jet,
cock, or other fixture; or to overflow or flood the sidewalk or pavement, or to
flow out upon any lot or street, or to flow from his or her fountain into
adjacent premises and there be used; or to be taken from or used by any person
other than such occupant or a member or a visitor of his or her family, except
in case of fire.
(Prior Code, § 11-104)
§ 11-105 FILLING OF SWIMMING POOLS, LARGE IMPOUNDMENTS.
   (A)   Henceforth, all swimming pools, or any other amounts of water to be
consumed by the filling of large impoundments rapidly, must be metered and
billed as such by the City Clerk.
   (B)   Preceding the filling of such large impoundments, a contact should be
made with the City Clerk or other city officials so that the Water Department
can compensate for a sudden drop in the water level of the storage tanks.
   (C)   In addition, any city employee used by the individual as an aid in
filling an impoundment must be reimbursed for the time consumed at his or her
going rate of pay. This reimbursement is payable to the city.
(Prior Code, § 11-105)
ARTICLE 2: SEWAGE WORKS SYSTEM
Section
   
11-201   Authorization of sewage works
   
11-202   Declaration of necessity; sanitary sewer connection required where
available
   
11-203   Rates or charges for sanitary sewer services; collection of said rates
or charges
   
11-204   System of accounting; audits
   
11-205   Preparation and publication of financial statement
   
11-206   Sewage works system
§ 11-201 AUTHORIZATION OF SEWAGE WORKS.
   (A)   This municipality shall have the responsibility for the planning and
implantation of a sewage system for the citizens of the municipality and those
other area residents whom the city deems it feasible to serve. This is to be
accomplished in keeping with existing state statutes with regard to health and
environmental considerations, and to be enacted with regard to the health,
safety, and public interest of the citizens.
   (B)   The city, in keeping with the statutes of the state, may engage in
contracts for provision of planning, engineering, and construction services
with the purpose of providing sewage service for the residents of the
municipality and those other populations to be considered.
(Prior Code, § 11-201)
§ 11-202 DECLARATION OF NECESSITY; SANITARY SEWER CONNECTION REQUIRED WHERE
AVAILABLE.
   Any person owning abutting land to the sanitary sewer or where such sewer
might be placed shall be compelled to hook up to the public sewer, and a notice
to do so will be given to the owner. The use of the sanitary sewer system of
the city is determined and declared to be essential for the protection and
preservation of the public health, comfort, safety, economy, and general
welfare of the inhabitants of the city and of the area served by the system.
Falling to comply with this order after ten days have gone by shall be a
misdemeanor beginning on the eleventh day, and every day afterwards, shall be a
separate offense. The fine shall not be less than $5 or more than $25 per day.
(Prior Code, § 11-202)
§ 11-203 RATES OR CHARGES FOR SANITARY SEWER SERVICES; COLLECTION OF SAID RATES
OR CHARGES.
   (A)   This municipality shall issue, from time to time, a schedule of rates
or charges for persons using the sanitary sewer system. Implementation of new
rates or charges shall be subject to a public hearing, to be held not less that
ten days after the proposal to change said rates or charges is made. A copy of
the rates shall be kept with the Recorder and open to the public at all times.
The aggregate of the rates must be sufficient to maintain the care of the
sewage works. All rate changes must be approved by the Public Service
Commission before being implemented.
   (B)   All charges in connection with the city sanitary sewer system, within
and/or without the corporate limits, if not paid when due, shall constitute a
lien upon the premises served by the system. If any service charge or fee shall
not be paid within 30 days after the same is due, the amount thereof, together
with a penalty of 10% and a reasonable attorney’s fee, may be recovered by the
city in a civil action. In connection with such action, the lien described by
this section may be foreclosed against such lot, parcel of land, or building,
in accordance with the laws relating thereto.
   (C)   The municipality shall not discontinue sanitary sewer service to any
customer because of non-payment of service charges unless they have first
acquired the approval of the Public Service Commission. The municipality shall
make use of such remedies as may be available for the collection of delinquent
accounts prior to application to the Public Service Commission for other
relief.
(Prior Code, § 11-203)
§ 11-204 SYSTEM OF ACCOUNTING; AUDITS.
   This municipality shall establish an accounting system based on the system
of accounts as provided by the State Public Service Commission for the sewer
works system. These accounts shall be audited annually, and the audit should be
made open to the public.
(Prior Code, § 11-204)
§ 11-205 PREPARATION AND PUBLICATION OF FINANCIAL STATEMENT.
   (A)   The Clerk of the municipality in charge of the accounting for the
sewage works system shall prepare a monthly income statement to be presented to
the Mayor and Council showing the cash collected and disbursed for the period.
   (B)   The municipality shall prepare an annual report including a balance
sheet, income statement, and list of assets of the sewage works system. Such a
report shall be prepared in accordance with the format and system of accounts
provided by the State Public Services Commission.
   (C)   The municipality shall publish a financial statement of the sewage
works system every year as a Class I legal advertisement.
(Prior Code, § 11-205)
§ 11-206 SEWAGE WORKS SYSTEM.
   (A)   Certain buildings required to have sanitary water closets, connected
to sanitary sewer or sanitary septic tanks.
      (1)   Each inhabitable building or structure in the city, or beyond the
city limits for a distance of one mile, used or intended for use for
residential, commercial, industrial, or institutional purposes, or wherein
persons are employed or congregate, or are intended to be employed or
congregate, shall be provided by the owner, occupant, or person in charge, at
his or her own expense, with one or more sanitary flush toilets, in such number
as to be reasonably sufficient to accommodate the number of persons usually
resident, employed, or congregating; and where persons of both sexes are
employed or congregate, there shall be not less than one such sanitary water
closet, enclosed so as to ensure privacy, for each sex; and such toilets shall,
at the expense of the owner, occupant, or person in charge of the premises, be
connected to a sanitary sewer.
      (2)   It shall be unlawful for any owner or agent to put any person in
possession of any building, or any part, not provided with water closet
accommodations, except a watchman for the purpose of guarding such building or
part.
   (B)   Application for sewer service required. It shall be unlawful for any
person, including public bodies as well as natural persons, to make an initial
cut-in or connection with the city sewer system and use that system without
first making written application for such connection and paying all incident
costs, charges, fees, and deposits. Such application shall be made on forms
prescribed and furnished by the city, and shall constitute an agreement by the
applicant with the city to abide by all provisions of this article and such
applicable rules and regulations of the City Council in regard to the use of
the sewer system. Such application for service by firms, partnerships,
associations, and corporations shall be submitted only by their duly authorized
agent; and the official title of such agent shall be signed to the application.
   (C)   Rendering service.
      (1)   The application shall grant, or cause to be granted, to the city,
without cost, all rights, easements, permits, and privileges which are
necessary for the rendering of sewer service.
      (2)   Duly authorized employees of the city shall have access at all
reasonable hours to the premises of the applicant for the purpose of installing
or removing any of its property, examining pipes or fixtures, or for any
purpose incidental to the rendering of sewer service.
   (D)   Unauthorized connections prohibited.
      (1)   No person shall connect to or turn on any sewer service, or cut-in,
interconnect, tap, or make any alteration to any main distribution or
collection pipe of the city’s sewer system, or permit any connection or tapping
to be made to the sewer system on his or her premises or the premises occupied
by him or her, or knowingly use the sewer service from connections in violation
of any of the provisions of this article, or any rules or regulations adopted
by the city with respect to this article.
      (2)   Roof drains, yard and area drains, footer drains, or any line
carrying flow other than exclusively sanitary wastewater are prohibited from
connection to the sanitary sewer system. However, where, in the opinion of the
city, property damage will occur if the stipulations and this section are
followed, a variance, in writing, can be granted by the city to protect
property and lives.
   (E)   Matter not to be thrown into sewer. No person shall throw or deposit
in or upon any public sewer or any trap, basin, inlet, grating, manhole, or
other appurtenance of any public sewer in the city any sticks, stones, brick,
earth, gravel, dirt, mud, hay, straw, manure, rubbish, litter, sweepings,
offal, vegetables, garbage, other than properly shredded garbage from an
approved disposal device, trees, shrubs, branches, twigs, leaves, papers, rags,
oils, grease, gasoline, benzene, cinders, or refuse matter of any kind.
   (F)   Introducing into sewer hot, corrosive or explosive substances. No
person shall make or maintain any connection with any public sewer or
appurtenance whereby there may be conveyed into the sewer any hot, suffocating,
corrosive, flammable, or explosive liquid, gas, vapor, substance, or material
of any kind; and no person shall cause to enter or flow into any public sewer
or appurtenance any hot, corrosive, suffocating, flammable, or explosive
liquid, gas, vapor, substance, or material of any kind; however, the provisions
of this section shall not apply to water from ordinary hot-water broilers of
residences.
   (G)   City not liable for damage. The city shall be liable for any damage
resulting from bursting of any sewer main, service pipe, or valve, or from
discontinuing the operation of its sewer collection, treatment, and disposal
facilities, for repairs, extensions, or connections, or from the accidental
failure of the sewage collection, treatment, and disposal facilities from any
cause whatsoever. In cases of emergency, the Sanitary Board shall have the
right to restrict the use of its sewage collection, treatment, and disposal
facilities in any reasonable manner for the protection of the city and its
sewer system.
   (H)   Tampering with sewer appurtenances. No person shall break or damage,
turn, lift, remove, raise, or tamper with any cover or any manhole, basin,
inlet, or other appurtenance of any public storm sewer without a written permit
from the city, or of any combined sewer or sanitary sewer without a written
permit from the.
   (I)   Obstruction. No person shall obstruct, impede, or cause to be impeded
or obstructed the flow of any public sewer, nor interfere with its free
discharge or ventilation, nor clog up such sewer or any appurtenance.
   (J)   Sewer taps only by authorized persons. No person, except those persons
duly employed or authorized by the city, shall tap the city’s sewer mains.
(Prior Code, § 11-206)
ARTICLE 3: SOLID WASTE
Section

11-322   Littering and deposit of garbage, refuse, rubbish, junk, and the like

§ 11-300 AUTHORIZATION OF SOLID WASTE MANAGEMENT.
   (A)   In order to protect the public health and general welfare of the
residences of this municipality, the governing body may enact and enforce
ordinances for the provision of service to collect and dispose of domestic,
commercial, or industrial solid wastes from units located within the corporate
boundaries of this municipality.
   (B)   This section is not to be interpreted in a manner so as to present the
governing body of this municipality from entering into a contractual agreement
with a private supplier of solid waste collection and/or disposal services. Nor
is the above intended to prevent this municipality from entering into an
agreement with other governmental jurisdiction at some time in the future. Any
agreement flowing out of the authorization of this section will be achieved in
a manner consistent with state requirements with regard to the establishment of
rate structures and penalties to the abuse of service.
(Prior Code, § 11-300)
§ 11-301 PRIVATE SCAVENGERS, AND THE LIKE, NOT TO DO BUSINESS IN THE CITY.
   It shall be unlawful for any person, except the city, or its designee, to
engage in or conduct the business of collection, removal, or disposal of
refuse, raw garbage, or prepared garbage within the city, and private
scavengers, pushcart operators, and private garbage collectors are hereby
prohibited from engaging in the business of transport or disposing of raw or
prepared garbage and refuse containing organic wastes, putrid matter, and
wastes or excreta subject to purification from the city.
(Prior Code, § 11-301)
§ 11-302 DISPOSAL.
   The disposal of refuse in any quantity by any person in any place, public or
private, other that at the site or sites designated for refuse disposal by the
governing body, is expressly prohibited.
(Prior Code, § 11-302)
§ 11-303 OPERATION OF SOLID WASTE DISPOSAL SITE.
   Any operator, whether of a public or private nature, of a solid waste
disposal site which is located within the corporate boundaries of this
municipality must operate and maintain such site in such a manner as to qualify
the disposal site as a sanitary landfill as defined by the State Health
Department and Public Law of the United States Code, and any rules or
regulations adopted pursuant to such legislated authority.
(Prior Code, § 911-303)
§ 11-304 PREMISES TO BE KEPT CLEAN.
   All persons within the municipality are hereby required to keep their
premises in a clean and sanitary condition, free from accumulation of refuse,
except when stored as provided in this article.
(Prior Code, § 11-304)
§ 11-305 MANDATORY DISPOSAL; PROOF REQUIRED; PENALTY IMPOSED.
   (A)   Each person occupying a residence or operating a business
establishment in this municipality shall either:
      (1)   Subscribe to and use a solid waste service and pay the fees
established therefor; or
      (2)   Provide proper proof that said person properly disposes of solid
waste at least once within every 30-day period at approved solid waste
facilities, or in any other lawful manner.
   (B)   Each person that disposes of solid waste, other than subscribing to a
solid waste service, must show proof, each 30-day period, of disposal by lawful
manner to the City Recorder.
   (C)   Any person who violates the provisions of this section by not lawfully
disposing of his or her solid waste, or failing to provide proper proof that he
or she lawfully disposes of his or her solid waste at least once a month, is
guilty of a misdemeanor. Upon conviction, he or she is subject to a fine of not
less than $50 nor more than $1,000.
(W. Va. Code§ 22C-4-10) (Prior Code, § 11-305)
Statutory reference:
   Similar provisions, see W. Va. Code § 8-12-5
§ 11-306 PREPARATION OF GARBAGE FOR COLLECTION.
   Preparation of garbage for collection to be prescribed by the supplier of
collection and those standards complied with.
(Prior Code, § 11-306)
§ 11-307 STORAGE.
   It shall be unlawful for any person within the city to store, or permit the
storage of, bury, throw out, deposit, or place any garbage or refuse upon any
street, sidewalk, gutter, or private property, or any other such place, whether
owned by such person or not, or to deposit garbage anywhere within the city, or
the premises occupied by him or her, except as provided by in this article. All
garbage and refuse shall be stored in a vessel, can, or tank which shall be
leak proof and watertight, and kept in such condition and which is fitted with
covers so closely fitted that no odor can escape there from, such tops not to
be removed except long enough to put such garbage into such vessel, can, or
tank and replaced immediately thereafter. All containers are to be made of a
durable plastic or metal designed to be used for the storage of garbage.
(Prior Code, § 11-307)
§ 11-308 WHERE RECEPTACLES TO BE KEPT; DUTY TO EMPTY AND CLEAN RECEPTACLES.
   (A)   All garbage receptacles shall be kept in the rear of any building, or
in the basement or other area, or in an enclosure where they will not
constitute a nuisance or be offensive to the public, neighboring occupants, or
occupants of the property on which they are located, and where they will not
permit the gathering of flies.
   (B)   All garbage receptacles shall be emptied and their contents removed to
an approved dumping area not less frequently than as required by § 11-305.
Whenever any such garbage receptacles become foul, they shall be replaced or
treated with some disinfecting solution.
(Prior Code, § 11-308)
§ 11-309 CONTAINERS USED FOR COLLECTION.
   Containers used for collection shall conform to a size and weight
established by the supplier of collection and standards complied with.
(Prior Code, § 11-309)
§ 11-310 STORAGE ON PUBLIC WAY; EXCEPTIONS.
   No person shall accumulate or store garbage, rubbish, refuse, trash, brush,
leaves, tree, and shrubbery trimmings, refuse receptacle, bulk container,
construction waste, or building material, or any other item of waste or
recyclable material for collection or otherwise, on any street, sidewalk, lane,
or right-of-way, except during the day for scheduled collection.
(Prior Code, § 11-310)
§ 11-311 LOCATION OF CONTAINERS FOR COLLECTION.
   All accumulations of refuse and trash shall be placed for collection in
accordance with the following.
   (A)   Public streets. No refuse, trash, brush, leaves, or tree and shrubbery
trimmings refuse receptacle or bulk container shall be placed within the
vehicular travel-way, in the gutter of any street, or in the vehicular travel-
way in areas not having curbs and gutters.
   (B)   Public sidewalks. Refuse, trash, brush, leaves, or tree and shrubbery
trimmings refuse receptacle or bulk container may be placed on the sidewalk on
the day of collection so long as it does not unreasonably interfere with
pedestrian traffic.
   (C)   Public alleys. Refuse, trash, brush, leaves, or tree and shrubbery
trimmings refuse receptacle or bulk container may be placed in a public alley
on the day of collection so long as it does not unreasonably interfere with
vehicular or pedestrian traffic.
(Prior Code, § 11-311)
§ 11-312 COLLECTION AND DISPOSAL SUPERVISION.
   All refuse accumulated within the corporate limits shall be collected,
conveyed and disposed of under the supervision of such officer as the governing
body shall designate. Collections shall be made regularly in accordance with an
announced schedule.
(Prior Code, § 11-312)
§ 11-313 DELIVERY OF REFUSE UPON PRIVATE PROPERTY.
   It shall be unlawful to deliver refuse to or upon private property.
(Prior Code, § 11-313)
§ 11-314 POST COLLECTION PROCEDURES.
   Refuse receptacles returned to the curbside after collection shall be
removed to the approved storage location by the end of day of collection, and
any spilled or left over material removed. The property owner or occupant shall
be responsible for such removal.
(Prior Code, § 11-314)
§ 11-315 DISTURBING CONTAINERS.
   No unauthorized person shall uncover, ruffle, rifle, pilfer, dig into, turn
over, or in any other manner disturb or use any refuse container belonging to
another. This section shall not be construed to prohibit the use of public
containers for their intended purpose.
(Prior Code, § 11-315)
§ 11-316 THROWING, SCATTERING, OR DELIVERING REFUSE UPON ANY PREMISES, STREET,
OR PLACE.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to throw, place, or scatter any garbage,
rubbish, or other refuse over or upon any premises or street, either public or
private, or adjacent to such place, either with or without the intention to
later remove or burn the material; or to permit, from the accumulation of
refuse, any premises owned, occupied, or controlled by such person to become or
remain offensive, unsanitary, or unsightly, or unsafe, to public health or
hazardous from fire; or to burn such garbage, rubbish, trash, or other refuse
within the corporate limits.
(Prior Code, § 11-316)
§ 11-317 DISPLAY OF DECALS.
   Decals shall be displayed as prescribed by the service provided and visible
by city officers.
(Prior Code, § 11-317)
§ 11-318 CUSTOMER LIST TO BE PROVIDED TO CITY.
   It shall be the responsibility of service providers to furnish a list of
customers to the City Recorder.
(Prior Code, § 11-318)
§ 11-319 DUTY OF CONTRACTORS TO REMOVE DEBRIS; COLLECTION OF REFUSE FROM LOTS.
   Building contractors, excavators, and other persons who, in the course of
their respective businesses, cause debris or refuse of any kind to accumulate
upon any street or at any other place within the city shall remove and dispose
of such debris or refuse within 48 hours of notification by the city or, as
directed by a city officer, before it becomes a hazard to the public health,
safety, or welfare, and at the completion of each project shall remove and
dispose of all such debris and refuse in a sanitary and lawful manner. When
debris or refuse accumulates on any lot so as to become a nuisance and is not
subject to removal by any contractor or other person, as provided in this
section, the city, after notice to the property owner to do so and his or her
failure to comply within a reasonable time, may collect and dispose of such
debris and refuse; and the cost of such collection and disposal shall become a
charge against the owner of such lot, and shall be collected in any manner
provided by law.
(Prior Code, § 11-319)
§ 11-320 FALLEN TREES, STUMPS, AND DEBRIS WHICH ARE ON PUBLIC RIGHT-OF-WAY.
   Fallen trees, stumps, and debris which are on the public right-of-way shall
be collected and disposed of by the city, and the cost of such collection and
disposition may be charged to the owner of the property upon which such trees,
stumps, and debris originated. Fallen trees, stumps, and debris not on a public
right-of-way shall be removed promptly and disposed of in a sanitary and lawful
manner by the owner or occupants of the properties upon which they are
situated.
(Prior Code, § 11-320)
§ 11-321 UNAUTHORIZED USE OF DUMPSTERS.
   No person without authorization shall dump garbage or trash, or assist in
the unauthorized dumping of garbage or trash, in a dumpster or other solid
waste container which is located on the property of another person and leased,
or otherwise owned or maintained, by another person. The act of throwing
isolated objects into a dumpster or other solid waste container in the
prevention or elimination of litter is specifically exempted from any penalties
under this section.
(W. Va. Code § 61-3-53) (Prior Code, § 11-321)
§ 11-322 LITTERING AND DEPOSIT OF GARBAGE, REFUSE, RUBBISH, JUNK, AND THE LIKE.
   (A)   The Commissioner of Highways, Director of Department of Natural
Resources, and the City Street Superintendent, and the court for the city,
shall be the responsible agencies for administration and enforcement of
regulations relating to maintenance of cleanliness and improvement of
appearances on and along streets, roads, alleys, and other public areas or ways
in the city.
   (B)   No person shall place, deposit, dump, or throw, or cause to be placed,
deposited, dumped, or thrown, any litter, garbage, refuse, trash, can, bottle,
paper, ashes, cigarette or cigar butt, carcass of any dead animal or any part
thereof, offal, or any other offensive or unsightly matter in or upon any
public or private highway, road, street, or alley, or upon the surface of any
land within 100 yards thereof, without the consent of the owner, or in or upon
any private property into or upon which the public is admitted by easement or
license, or upon any private property without the consent of the owner, or in
or upon any public park or other public property other than in such place as
may be set aside for such purpose by the governing body having charge thereof.
   (C)   If any such materials are thrown, cast, dumped, or discharged from a
motor vehicle in violation of the provisions hereof, such action shall be
deemed prima facie evidence that the owner and driver of such motor vehicle
intended to violate the provisions of this section.
   (D)   No portion of this section shall be construed to restrict a private
owner in the use of his or her own private property, or to prohibit the
disposal of materials designated in this section in any manner authorized by
law.
   (E)   Any law enforcement officer who shall observe a person violating the
provisions of this section shall have a mandatory duty to make an arrest, or
otherwise prosecute the violator to the limits provided herein.
(Prior Code, § 11-322)
§ 11-323 PENALTIES.
   Any person, for any violation of §§
11-304 through
11-311, and §
11-314, for a first offense shall be notified with a written notice of warning
and given a copy of this article, from the City Recorder, Mayor, or Chief of
Police. A second offense shall be a misdemeanor and a fine of $200 shall be
imposed. A third offense and other subsequent offenses, shall be fined $500.
Each day any such violation continues shall constitute a separate offense. All
other sections of this article shall be governed by §
11-16.
(Prior Code, § 11-323)
ARTICLE 4: PUBLIC RECREATION
Section
   
11-400   Board of Park Commissioners; creation; qualifications; term;
vacancies; powers and duties
   
11-401   Municipality, Board of Park Commissioners; authority to adopt rules
and regulations, other Commission rules; hours of operation, penalties
   
11-402   Rules and regulations for the city parks and recreation facilities
§ 11-400 BOARD OF PARK COMMISSIONERS; CREATION; QUALIFICATIONS; TERM;
VACANCIES; POWERS AND DUTIES.
   (A)   There is hereby established and continued the City Board of Park and
Recreation Commissioners, which shall be a public corporate body as provided by
W. Va. Code § 8-21, as amended.
   (B)   The management, control, and operation of Tracy Lake Park of said city
shall be vested in the Pennsboro Board of Park and Recreation Commissions.
   (C)   The Park Board shall consist of six persons, each of whom shall be
citizens, residents, and owners of real property within the city, and shall be
persons of outstanding reputation, ability, and integrity in said city, and
membership shall consist of five residents at large within the city limits and
one member of the governing body of the city, and shall be appointed by the
governing body of said city. Membership on the city governing body may not
disqualify any member for selection to the Park Board. The Mayor of said city
shall notify all appointees of their selection. The term of the Park Board
membership of any member of the city governing body so appointed shall continue
during his or her term as a member of the city governing body, and until his or
her successor is appointed or elected and qualified. The terms of other
appointed Park Board members shall be for six years, and until their successors
have been duly appointed and qualified; provided, that the terms of the members
of the Park Board first appointed shall be for one, two, three, four, and five
years respectively, from the first day of the month in which appointed. In the
event of a vacancy, and also within 30 days after the expiration of the term of
office of any member of the Park Board, a successor shall be appointed by the
governing body of the city. All vacancies shall be filled for the unexpired
term only and all other appointments shall be for a term of six years, and all
members of the Park Board shall continue in office until their successors shall
have been appointed. All members of the present Park Board shall continue in
office until replaced as herein provided. The said Park Board shall adopt
rules, regulations, and by-laws regulating the time and place of its meetings
and the conduct thereof. Any member of the Park Board shall be eligible for re-
appointment upon the expiration of his or her term. The members of the Park
Board shall serve without compensation, but may be reimbursed for any expenses
incurred in the performance of their duties under order, in writing, of the
said Park Board. Each member of the Park Board shall be removed for just cause
by the governing body of the city by recorded vote of a majority of said
Council after a public hearing thereon. When any member of the Park Board,
during his or her term of office, shall cease to be a resident and freeholder
of the city, he or she shall thereby be disqualified as a member of the Park
Board, and his or her office shall, thereupon, become vacant.
(W. Va. Code § 8-21-3)
   (D)   (1)   After appointment, the members of the Board shall qualify by
taking and filing with the Recorder of the city the oath prescribed by law for
public officials, and they shall not be permitted to serve upon said Park Board
until they have so qualified. If any member of said Park Board shall fail to so
qualify on or before the date upon which he or she should assume the duties of
his or her office, a vacancy shall exist which shall be filled as provided in
division (C) above.
(W. Va. Code § 8-21-5)
      (2)   At the first meeting held after the first Park Board has been
appointed, and annually thereafter, it shall organize by electing one of their
number a President, and another Vice President, and by electing a secretary who
need not be a member of the Park Board. The Secretary shall take the oath as
prescribed by law and shall furnish such bond as may be required by said Park
Board. The Secretary shall keep an accurate record of all the fiscal affairs of
the Park Board, and shall keep a minute book in which he or she shall record
the proceedings and transactions of each meeting of the Park Board, and a copy
of those minutes shall be provided from each meeting to the City Recorder,
which shall be available for inspection as other municipal records. The
President shall preside at all meetings when present and shall call special
meetings on his or her own motion, or when requested so to do by any two
members of the Park Board. In the absence of the President, the Vice President
shall exercise all the duties and functions of the President.
(W. Va. Code § 8-21)
      (3)   The City Treasurer shall be ex officio Treasurer of said Park
Board, and he or she shall take the oath prescribed by law and shall furnish
such bond as may be required by said Park Board.
(W. Va. Code § 8-21-5)
   (E)   The Board of Park and Recreation Commissioners shall have full and
complete supervision, management, operation, and control of Tracy Lake Park of
said city, including the maintenance, operations, improvements, and extension
thereof, and shall have power and authority to make all contracts and
agreements necessary and proper for the full and complete performance of its
duties as herein set forth and as provided and regulated by law.
   (F)   The Board of Park and Recreation Commissioners shall have power to
employ, fix the compensation of and discharge all employees of said park
system, and may require any such employee, before entering upon his or her
employment, to furnish and file with the City Recorder his or her bond in such
penalty and with such surety as the Park Board may Direct, each bond to be
payable to the said Board of Park and Recreation Commissioners and conditioned
as to the faithful performance of their respective duties as fixed by the Park
Board, this section, the Charter of said city, and according to law.
   (G)   The Board of Park and Recreation Commissioners shall have the right to
use such facilities, equipment, and materials of the city under such contracts,
conditions, and agreements with the Council of said city as are authorized by
the Charter and ordinances of the said city.
   (H)   In the event that all or any part of the real and personal property
comprising Tracy Lake Park be sold, the proceeds from such sale shall be used
by said Park Board in the maintenance and operation of the remaining Tracy Lake
Park, or to purchase, improve, or operate some other recreational facility
dedicated to the use of the general public of the said city.
   (I)   The Board of Park and Recreation Commissioners shall have all other
powers and duties provided by W. Va. Code § 8-21, 1931, as amended.
(W. Va. Code § 8-21-14)
   (J)   The Commission or Commissioners of the Board of Park and Recreation
Commission, appointed by the City Council, shall have no authority to sell,
trade, giveaway, transfer, or deed to another, or in any way dispose of any
real property, or shall incur any form of indebtedness without first obtaining
consent of the governing body of the city.
(W. Va. Code § 8-21-14)
(Prior Code, § 11-400)
§ 11-401 MUNICIPALITY, BOARD OF PARK COMMISSIONERS; AUTHORITY TO ADOPT RULES
AND REGULATIONS, OTHER COMMISSION RULES; HOURS OF OPERATION, PENALTIES.
   (A)   Authority to adopt rules and regulations.
      (1)   The City Council and the City Board of Park Commissioners shall
designate rules and regulations pertaining to the park and recreational
facility’s use. Upon Council approval of such rules and regulations by
ordinance, the city and Board of Park Commissioners is authorized and empowered
to enforce such rules and regulations. Violation shall be subject to the
penalties provided in Municipal Ordinance 9-30(D).
      (2)   No person in any park, recreation facility, or property of the city
shall cause any breach of the peace, disturbance, or create any nuisance; post
any private notice or advertisement therein or on any fence, post, or tree
thereof; violate any notice or card, or rules or regulations posted in or
adopted by the city, about any park, recreational facility, or property under
authority of the city; injure, mutilate, or deface any tree, shrub, flower,
building, structure, fence, property, or other thing in or about any park or
city recreation facility or property; throw at, shoot at, kill, or injure any
bird, animal, or pet of any kind in, or belonging to, any park or city
property; or violate any of the rules or regulations made for the government of
any park or city property, or violate any lawful order of the city or Board of
Park Commissioners.
   (B)   Hours of operation.
      (1)   No person may be in or on municipal property during the hours of
closure as posted without the express permission of the Mayor, City Recorder,
municipal police, or a Board of Park Commissioner member.
      (2)   All city property shall be closed from 10:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m.
throughout the year, unless other otherwise posted.
      (3)   Hours may be adjusted or established by resolution of City Council.
      (4)   Hours of operating shall be posted conspicuously at all entrances
to property.
      (5)   A violation of any rule, or destruction of signs or property, or
vandalism, shall be a misdemeanor and punishable under division (C) below.
   (C)   Rules, hours of operation of parks. The Board of Park Commissioners
shall establish rules and hours of operation for public parks and recreational
facilities under their authority. The hours may prohibit use of certain
facilities at certain times. No person shall make use of public parks and
recreations facilities during prohibited hours.
      (1)   The Board of Park Commissioners shall have the right to promulgate
rules and regulations for the operation of public park and recreation
facilities under its authority and the activities therein. A violation of any
park rule, or destruction of signs or property, or vandalism, shall be a
misdemeanor and punishable under division (E) below. Such rules and regulations
shall be posted at such park and recreation facilities and available for review
in the office of the City Recorder.
      (2)   Hours of operation shall be posted conspicuously at all entrances
or recreation facilities.
      (3)   Copies of all park regulations shall be furnished to the City
Council, City Recorder, Police Department, and Municipal Court.
   (D)   Vehicle regulations on Board, Park, Commission, and city property.
      (1)   The speed limit for motor vehicles is 25 mph in/on city property,
city park and recreation areas, streets unless otherwise posted. MOTOR VEHICLE
means any automobile, motorcycle, bicycle, or any other form of mechanical
transportation. All traffic laws, signs, and directions shall be strictly
observed. Driving of motor vehicles in any manner that creates a nuisance to
any guest by repetitive or continuous cruising or operation is prohibited.
      (2)   As used in this section, BOARD means the city or any of the city’s
boards, authorities, or commissions, the City Park (Tracy Lake) and Recreation
Board(s), and VEHICLE means any automobile, motorcycle, bicycle, or any other
form of mechanical transportation.
      (3)   No person shall drive or propel, or cause to be driven or
propelled, along or over any roadway or other property under the supervision of
the Board at a greater rate of speed than as posted by the Board or the city.
      (4)   No vehicle shall be parked or stopped on any roadway or on any
other property within park areas under the supervision of the Board, except as
designated parking areas. No vehicle shall be parked or stopped on unpaved
areas within the park areas or on areas of the roadway designated for travel of
vehicles, or on paved areas not designated for parking, except on occasion when
such area is specifically designated as a parking or driving area, whichever
applies, by the Board or the city.
   (E)   Violations. Any person violating any provision of this article or any
ordinance, rule, or regulation duly adopted by the city, City Board of Park
Commissioners, or other commissions of the city shall be guilty of a
misdemeanor, and shall be fined no less than $50 or no more than $1,000.
      (1)   In addition, such person may be ejected from the park, building, or
other facility wherein the violation occurred.
      (2)   The replacement cost of any sign or property vandalized or
destroyed shall be included in any fine.
      (3)   Any drug related violation pertaining to the above shall carry a
minimum fine of $200 and a maximum of $1,000.
(Prior Code, § 11-401) (Ord. 13-1120, passed - -)
§ 11-402 RULES AND REGULATIONS FOR THE CITY PARKS AND RECREATION FACILITIES.
   (A)   Hours of operation for the city parks and recreation facilities are as
follows.
      (1)   The city park picnic and general use area shall be closed from the
hours of 10:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m.
      (2)   The Tracy Lake area shall be closed from 10:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m.
Night fishing is permitted. The city park shooting range shall be closed from
dusk until dawn.
      (3)   These hours shall not apply to law enforcement, city maintenance
workers during the performance of their official duties, and those with a
special permit.
   (B)   Fires may be lighted only in a fireplace or other facility constructed
for a fire; or use a charcoal grill or a gasoline or gas stove, or fire rings
or grills, provided by the city park. Those persons responsible for a fire
shall extinguish it completely before leaving it. Ashes, charcoal briquettes,
and other materials used for a fire shall be left in the fire ring or grill,
and shall not be strewn over the ground.
   (C)   Loud or excessive noise, demonstrations, disturbances, disorderly
conduct, profanity, public drunkenness, and the possession or use of controlled
substances is prohibited.
   (D)   Garbage, waste, bottles, cans, paper, junk, or any other trash or
refuse shall be deposited in trash containers. It shall not be dumped,
deposited, or strewn within the boundary of the city park.
   (E)   Dogs and cats are the only pets permitted in the city park. They shall
be restrained at all times on a sturdy leash not to exceed ten feet in length.
The owner or master shall clean up the pet’s excreta, keep it quiet and from
disturbing other guests, and is responsible for all damages it causes.
   (F)   Horseback riding is permitted only on roads normally open to public
travel, and designated routes and areas as posted on the area.
      (1)   No person shall bring or allow horses in designated camping areas.
      (2)   The owner shall be responsible for the removal and disposal of any
waste produced by the animals.
      (3)   Feed shall be restricted to locally obtained or pelletized horse
feed.
   (G)   Fireworks, explosives, incendiaries, flammables, and other dangerous
substances are prohibited in the city park.
   (H)   Uncased firearms, uncased bows, and uncased arrows are prohibited in
the city park, except in the shooting range.
   (I)   The city park assumes no responsibility for any personal property. If
personal property is abandoned or left unattended by park guests for more than
48 hours, it will be removed from the public use area and disposed of according
to law.
   (J)   Hawking, peddling, soliciting, begging, advertising, or carrying on
any business or commercial enterprise is prohibited in the city park without
the written permission of from the Park Board.
   (K)   Fishing and boating are permitted in the park lake only in accordance
with state law. Only trolling motors are permitted in Tracy Lake, no gasoline
motors are permitted. Night fishing is permitted.
   (L)   The speed limit for motor vehicles is 25 mph in the city park, except
where a lower speed limit is posted. All traffic laws, signs, and directions
shall be strictly observed. Driving of motor vehicles in any manner that
creates a nuisance to any guest by repetitive or continuous cruising or
operation is prohibited.
   (M)   Motor vehicles must stay on designated roads and parking lots. It is
unlawful for any unauthorized motor vehicle to go beyond a gate, cable, or
other obstruction, or to proceed beyond any sign prohibiting such travel. All
persons operating motor vehicles in the city park shall obey and comply with
all applicable state laws and rules.
   (N)   Camping shall not be permitted except in a designated area.
(Prior Code, § 11-402)

§ 12-1 ESTABLISHMENT OF POLICE DEPARTMENT.
   The City Council, in order to protect persons and property within the city,
to preserve law and order therein, and to enforce therein the criminal laws of
this state and ordinances of the municipality, does hereby establish a
Municipal Police Department; hereafter known as the City Police Department.
(Prior Code, § 12-1)
§ 12-2 SUBJECT TO AUTHORITY OF; CHAIN OF COMMAND; OBEDIENCE TO ORDERS.
   It is also established that the City Police Department is subject to the
control and authority of the Mayor for the city. The chain of command shall be
the Mayor, Chief of Police, and other members of the Police Department
according to rank and seniority within rank. All members of the Police
Department shall faithfully obey all lawful orders of their superiors in the
chain of command.
(Prior Code, § 12-2)
§ 12-3 MAINTAINING.
   The governing body shall provide all necessary equipment needed to maintain
such a Police Department.
(Prior Code, § 12-3)
§ 12-4 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this article, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   APPROVED LAW ENFORCEMENT TRAINING ACADEMY. Any training facility which is
approved and authorized to conduct law enforcement training, as provided in
this article.
   CHIEF EXECUTIVE. The Superintendent of the State Police; the Chief Natural
Resources Police Officer of the Division of Natural Resources; the Sheriff of
any state county; any administrative deputy appointed by the Chief Natural
Resources Police Officer of the Division of Natural Resources; or the Chief of
any state municipal law enforcement agency.
   COUNTY. The 55 major political subdivisions of the state.
   EXEMPT RANK. Any non-commissioned or commissioned rank of sergeant or above.
   GOVERNOR’S COMMITTEE ON CRIME, DELINQUENCY, AND CORRECTION or GOVERNOR’S
COMMITTEE. The Governor’s Committee on Crime, Delinquency, and Correction
established as a state planning agency pursuant to W. Va. Code § 15-9-1.
   LAW ENFORCEMENT OFFICER. Any duly authorized member of a law-enforcement
agency who is authorized to maintain public peace and order, prevent and detect
crime, make arrests, and enforce the laws of the state or any county or
municipality thereof, other than parking ordinances, and includes those persons
employed as campus police officers at state institutions of higher education in
accordance with the provisions of W. Va. Code § 18B-4-5, persons employed as
hospital police officers in accordance with the provisions of W. Va. Code § 16-
5B-19, and persons employed by the Public Service Commission as motor carrier
inspectors and weight-enforcement officers charged with enforcing commercial
motor vehicle safety and weight restriction laws, although those institutions
and agencies may not be considered law-enforcement agencies. The term also
includes those persons employed as county litter control officers charged with
enforcing litter laws who have been trained and certified as law-enforcement
officers and whose certification is currently active. The term also includes
those persons employed as rangers by resort area districts in accordance with
the provisions of W. Va. Code § 7-25-23, although no resort area district may
be considered a law-enforcement agency; provided, that the subject rangers
shall pay the tuition and costs of training. As used in this article, the term
LAW-ENFORCEMENT OFFICER does not apply to the chief executive of any West
Virginia law-enforcement agency, or to any watchman or special natural
resources police officer, or to any litter control officer who is authorized
and trained under the provisions of W. Va. Code § 7-1-3ff(d), but is not
trained and currently certified as a LAW-ENFORCEMENT OFFICER.
   LAW ENFORCEMENT OFFICIAL. The duly appointed chief administrator of a
designated law enforcement agency, or a duly authorized designee.
   MUNICIPALITY. Any incorporated town or city whose boundaries lie within the
geographic boundaries of the state.
   SUBCOMMITTEE or LAW ENFORCEMENT PROFESSIONAL STANDARDS SUBCOMMITTEE. The
subcommittee of the Governor’s Committee on Crime, Delinquency, and Correction
created by the state code.
   STATE LAW ENFORCEMENT AGENCY. Any duly authorized state, county, or
municipal organization employing one or more persons whose responsibility is
the enforcement of laws of the state or any county or municipality thereof;
provided, neither the Public Service Commission, nor any state institution of
higher education, nor any hospital, nor any resort area district, is a LAW
ENFORCEMENT AGENCY.
(W. Va. Code § 30-29-1) (Prior Code, § 12-4)
§ 12-5 CERTIFICATION.
   A person may not be employed as a law enforcement officer unless the person
is certified, or is certifiable, in one of the manners specified in W. Va. Code
§ 30-29-5, “Certification requirements and power to decertify or reinstate.”
(W. Va. Code § 30-29-5) (Prior Code, § 12-5)
§ 12-6 REIMBURSEMENT AGREEMENT.
   Pursuant to the provisions of W. Va. Code § 30-29-8, all law enforcement
officers shall, before attendance at a law enforcement officers’ training
academy, be required to enter into a written agreement with the city, which
agreement shall require and specify that if such employee should voluntarily
discontinue employment with the city within one year immediately following
completion of such training curriculum, such employee shall be obligated to pay
to the city the pro rata portion of the sum of such compensation, which is
equal to the part of such year which the employee has chosen not to remain in
the employ of the city.
(W. Va. Code § 30-29-8) (Prior Code, § 12-6)
§ 12-7 EDUCATION/TRAINING.
   In the event that the city and the officer determine that the officer shall
receive additional training for his or her services as an officer of police,
with the advance approval of the Mayor, the officer may acquire such
educational materials and enroll in such training as the parties may deem
appropriate, with the city to pay the costs thereof.
(Prior Code, § 12-7)
§ 12-8 VACATION.
   Vacation will be taken with a request in advance having been made by the
officer, except in the case of an emergency, to his or her proper supervisor.
The officer will make such arrangements as may be necessary to inform others of
their pending vacation to ensure coverage.
(Prior Code, § 12-8)
§ 12-9 BOND.
   The city will arrange for a bond for the carrying by the officer of a
firearm, and will arrange for general police liability insurance for the
benefit of the parties, in such amounts as the city, in its sole discretion,
deems appropriate at the expense of the city. No cause of action shall lie,
however, in favor of the officer and against the city in the event that the
city does not procure such bond or insurance, or in the event that the
insurance procured is subsequently determined to be insufficient to cover the
risks for which it was purchased.
(Prior Code, § 12-9)
