§ 15-300 SESSIONS OF COURT.
   The Municipal Court shall meet at times set by the Municipal Court Judge,
and at least monthly if necessary.
(Prior Code, § 15-300)
§ 15-301 ARREST WARRANTS.
   The Municipal Judge is invested with the authority to issue arrest warrants
for violations of this code.
(Prior Code, § 15-301)
§ 15-302 ISSUANCE OF SUMMONS.
   The Municipal Judge shall have, at his or her discretion, the choice of
either issuing an arrest warrant or a summons whenever an alleged violation of
the city ordinances occurs. The summons will order the defendant to appear
before the Municipal Court at a specified time in order to answer the charges
against himself or herself. The summons shall contain a brief description of
the offense charged against him or her, but need not be a verbatim account of
the supposed violated ordinance.
(Prior Code, § 15-302)
§ 15-303 ISSUANCE OF SUBPOENAS.
   The Municipal Judge shall have invested in his or her the authority to
subpoena witnesses whose testimony is relevant to any judicial proceeding. It
shall be unlawful for any citizen to ignore such subpoena and shall be a
contempt of court.
(Prior Code, § 15-303)
§ 15-304 POLICE OFFICER TO ATTEND SESSIONS OF COURT.
   The Chief of Police, or a police officer designated by him or her, shall
attend all sessions of the Municipal Court. He or she shall preserve order in
the courtroom and its immediate vicinity, and obey all orders of the Municipal
Judge.
(Prior Code, § 15-304)
§ 15-305 DEFAULT JUDGMENT IN CASES OF ORDINANCE VIOLATIONS.
   Whenever a defendant, in any case prosecuted by the city, having been duly
summoned fails to appear at the time the case is set for trial, the Municipal
Judge shall proceed to hear and examine the testimony offered on the part of
the city, and shall, if he or she finds the defendant guilty, render judgment
by default against the defendant for such amount under the ordinance violated
as he or she may deem justice requires, and it shall be binding, subject to the
defendant’s right of appeal.
(Prior Code, § 15-305)
§ 15-306 FAILURE TO APPEAR FOR SUMMONS, WARRANT, OR CITATION.
   (A)   It shall be unlawful for any person, duly summoned, to fail to appear
in response to a notice given for his or her appearance to Municipal Court.
   (B)   Failure for any person to answer a violation of any of the provisions
of the Municipal Ordinance shall be guilty of an offense against this section
regardless of the disposition of the original violation he or she was so
summoned to or gave bond to appear and answer and he or she may be subject to a
fine up to $500, and such punishment may be addition to the punishment given
for such original violation.
      (1)   If, having been notified at the time of issuance of a citation by
any officer of the municipal Police Department a defendant fails to appear with
a given time period, he or she shall be guilty of failure to appeal for court
and subject to a fine of up to $250.
      (2)   If a defendant fails to respond or appear for a summons or warrant
issued by the municipal court judge, he or she shall be guilty of failure to
appear for court and subject to a fine of up to $500.
(Prior Code, § 15-306)
§ 15-307 TRIALS CONDUCTED.
   Trials may be conducted agreeably to law and established usage. New trials
may be granted.
(Prior Code, § 15-307)
§ 15-308 DISPOSITION OF CASES.
   (A)   Every individual charged with a violation of a municipal ordinance
shall have the right to an immediate trial and disposition of his or her case
in conformity to due process requirements.
   (B)   However, this provision does not apply if the Municipal Court is not
is session, if the Municipal Judge is unavailable or if the defendant is not in
clear possession of his or her faculties.
(Prior Code, § 15-308)
§ 15-309 APPEALS.
   (A)   It shall be the right of any defendant to appeal any verdict of the
Municipal Court to the next term of the Circuit Court.
   (B)   Such an appeal must occur within 20 days following the judgment of the
Municipal Court. All appeals must be accompanied with the posting of an appeal
bond as set forth in §
15-405.
(Prior Code, § 15-309)
§ 15-310 CONTEMPT.
   (A)   It shall be unlawful for any individual to disrupt or hinder the
proceedings of the Municipal Court. When punishment is authorized, the
Municipal Judge may issue attachments for contempt and punish summarily, but
not limited to, the following cases:
      (1)   Misbehavior in the presence of his or her court, or so near thereto
as to obstruct the administration of justice;
      (2)   Violence, or threats of violence, to the Municipal Judge or any
officer, witness, or party going thereto, attending or returning from court,
for or in respect of any act or proceeding had or to be had in such court;
      (3)   Misbehavior of any officer in his or her official capacity, in
respect to any act or judicial proceeding had or pending before the Municipal
Judge, or any process, order, or notice therein;
      (4)   Disobedience or resistance of an officer, witness, party, or other
person to any lawful process, judgment, order, or notice of the Municipal
Judge;
      (5)   The disobedience or resistance to an order of the court; and/or
      (6)   The utterance of indecorous and profane language.
   (B)   An order to arrest may be issued by the Municipal Judge on whom the
person charged with the contempt may be taken and brought before him or her, or
such person may be taken in custody by any officer or any person upon the oral
order of the Municipal Judge and held to answer for the contempt. An
opportunity must be given the person charged to be heard in defense or
explanation of his or her conduct, and the Municipal Judge may thereupon
discharge him or her, or adjudge him or her guilty of the contempt and punish
him or her therefor by fine or imprisonment, or both. The fine shall not exceed
$100, nor the imprisonment ten days. The Municipal Judge shall not impose a
fine for contempt unless the defendant be present in court, or shall have been
served with a rule of the court to show cause, on some certain day, and shall
have failed to appear and show cause.
   (C)   The conviction for contempt, specifying the particular circumstances
of the offense and judgment thereon, must be entered by the Municipal Judge in
his or her docket. A warrant of commitment for the term of imprisonment
adjudged may be issued by the Municipal Judge commanding an officer to take the
offender to jail, and the keeper thereof to imprison him or her therein for
such term. The judgment may include, in addition to fines, all costs in the
case, including costs of arresting and keeping in prison the offender.
(Prior Code, § 15-310)
§ 15-311 JAIL SENTENCE.
   The Municipal Court Judge, in his or her discretion, may signify in advance
of trial that under no condition will a jail sentence be imposed, and the
defendant shall not be entitled to a trial by jury, and no such time may be
imposed for that offense.
(Prior Code, § 15-311)
§ 15-312 JURY TRIAL.
   (A)   Any defendant, in jeopardy of incarceration in any misdemeanor
proceeding before the Municipal Court, shall be entitled to a trial by jury
unless such defendant shall affirmatively waive, in writing, such right;
provided, however, the Municipal Court Judge, in his or her discretion, may
signify in advance of trial that under no condition will a jail sentence be
imposed, and the foregoing shall not be required and the defendant shall not be
entitled to a trial by jury.
   (B)   The Municipal Court Judge shall conduct a trial by jury consistent
with the procedures set forth in the “Rules of Criminal Procedure for West
Virginia Magistrate Courts and Municipal Court Hearings.”
(Prior Code, § 15-312)
§ 15-313 CITY PROSECUTOR.
   (A)   When, in the opinion of the Mayor of the city, it is necessary or
advisable to do so, the Mayor may nominate a City Prosecutor, subject to the
approval of the Council, who shall hold office during the will and pleasure of
the Council. The salary of such Prosecutor shall be fixed by the Council. The
City Prosecutor shall have the same qualifications as those set forth as for
the City Solicitor.
   (B)   His or her duties shall be to represent the city in all criminal
matters originating in the Municipal Court for the violation of any city
ordinance, and on appeal from said court to any other court from proceedings so
originating. He or she also shall, upon request, advise members of the Police
Department and other officials of the city on any criminal matters arising out
of the violation of any city ordinance.
(Prior Code, § 15-313)
§ 15-314 SEPARATION OF WITNESSES; EXCLUSION OF MINORS FROM COURTROOM.
   The Municipal Judge is authorized to examine witnesses separate and apart
from each other. He or she may also exclude all minors from the courtroom who
may be present as mere auditors.
(Prior Code, § 15-314)
§ 15-315 TRIAL PROCEDURE; GRANTING OF NEW TRIALS.
   Trials in the Municipal Court shall be conducted agreeably to law and
established usage. New trials may be granted.
(Prior Code, § 15-315)
§ 15-316 INTIMIDATION OF JUDICIAL OFFICERS, JURORS, AND WITNESSES; OBSTRUCTING
ADMINISTRATION OF JUSTICE.
   If any person, by threats, force, or otherwise intimidate or impede, or
attempt to intimidate or impede, the Municipal Judge, the Municipal Court Clerk
or Deputy Clerk, or any other officer of the Municipal Court, or any juror or
witness in the Municipal Court in the discharge of his or her duties as such,
or by any means impede or obstruct, or attempt to impede or obstruct, the
administration of justice in the Municipal Court, they shall be guilty of a
misdemeanor.
(Prior Code, § 15-316)
§ 15-317 FALSE SWEARING AND SUBORNATION OF FALSE SWEARING.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to knowingly swear falsely under oath or
affirmation lawfully administered in any trial or proceeding held in the
Municipal Court, or before the Municipal Judge, concerning any matter or thing,
material or not material, or to procure another person to do so.
(Prior Code, § 15-317)
§ 15-318 DISTURBANCE OF COURT PROCEEDINGS.
   (A)   It shall be unlawful for any person to create any disturbance in the
court or of any trial before the municipal court by making loud or unusual
noises, by using indecorous, profane, or blasphemous language, or by any
distracting conduct whatsoever.
   (B)   Any person so doing may be removed from court by order of the judge
and fined no less than $50 or no more than $500.
(Ord. passed 9-15-2015)
ARTICLE 4: BONDS
Section
   
15-400   Bail bonds and cash deposits in lieu thereof
   
15-401   Requisites and disposition of cash deposits posted in lieu of bail
bond
   
15-402   Unauthorized acceptance or approval of cash bond
   
15-403   Persons prohibited to be surety on bail bonds
   
15-404   Bond for witness
   
15-405   Appeal and appeal bonds
§ 15-400 BAIL BONDS AND CASH DEPOSITS IN LIEU THEREOF.
   (A)   Except as may be provided otherwise in any case by the provisions of
W. Va. Code § 62-1C, whenever any person is arrested for any violation of an
ordinance of the city or for any offense of which the Municipal Judge has
jurisdiction, it shall be lawful for the Municipal Judge, Recorder, Municipal
Court Clerk, Mayor, Chief of Police, or person in charge of police headquarters
to admit such person to bail upon the execution of a bond to the city in such
an amount as in the discretion of the officer will secure the prisoner’s
presence, conditioned that the accused will appear upon a day named, before the
Municipal Judge of the city, to await trial; and every such bond taken shall be
filed as soon as practicable with the Municipal Court Clerk by the officer
approving and taking such bond; and the Municipal Judge, Recorder, Municipal
Court Clerk, Mayor, Chief of Police, or person in charge of police headquarters
shall each have the power to approve any bond taken under the provisions of
this section, precedence being given to the ranking officer present at police
headquarters when such bond is presented.
   (B)   (1)   No person shall be accepted as surety upon any penal bond unless
he or she shall acknowledge the bond before some official duly authorized by
this code or by state law to administer an oath, and shall make oath that he or
she is the owner in fee of real estate situate in the city and worth the amount
of the bond over and above his or her debts and liabilities; but the officers
hereinbefore named in this section are hereby authorized and empowered to
accept a deposit in cash of an amount which, in the judgment of the officer
accepting the deposit, will be sufficient to cause the prisoner’s appearance
upon the day required of him or her before the Municipal Judge to await trial
upon the charge against him or her.
      (2)   The amount of such deposit shall not be less than a sum sufficient
in the judgment of the officer accepting the same to satisfy any reasonable
fine and costs which may be imposed by the Municipal Judge.
   (C)   In the event any person so released upon bond or such deposit shall
fail to appear before the Municipal Judge for trial at the appointed time, or,
having appeared, shall leave the court without awaiting trial, his or her bond
shall be forfeited thereby to the city, and if a cash deposit has been made to
secure his or her release, the sum so deposited shall be delivered to the
Municipal Judge, and by him or her promptly turned into the City Treasury to
the credit of the General Fund and accounted for by him or her in the same
manner that fines collected by him or her are accounted for; and in the event
of the forfeiture of a penal bond, the Treasurer shall forthwith take the steps
necessary at law for the collection thereof. However, this provision does not
apply if an individual is intoxicated or in need of protective custody.
(Prior Code, § 15-400)
§ 15-401 REQUISITES AND DISPOSITION OF CASH DEPOSITS POSTED IN LIEU OF BAIL
BOND.
   (A)   No cash bond shall be accepted by any officer authorized to accept
such bond unless the prisoner and the officer authorized to accept it are
present at police headquarters.
   (B)   The money deposited as security for any person’s appearance shall be
deposited at police headquarters, to be by him or her safely kept until the
next regular business day, when it shall be turned over by the person who
received it to the Judge or Clerk of the Municipal Court, and by the Judge or
Clerk disposed of as required by the bond and this section and § 15-400.
(Prior Code, § 15-401)
§ 15-402 UNAUTHORIZED ACCEPTANCE OR APPROVAL OF CASH BOND.
   If any officer shall accept or approve any cash bond at any place or in any
other manner than is herein provided for and authorized, such unauthorized
acceptance or approval shall constitute good cause for his or her suspension or
removal, or the reprimand or fining of such officer after a hearing on the
charge by the City Council.
(Prior Code, § 15-402)
§ 15-403 PERSONS PROHIBITED TO BE SURETY ON BAIL BONDS.
   No practicing attorney, officer of the Municipal Court, or member of the
police force shall be accepted as surety on any bond provided for in this code.
(Prior Code, § 15-403)
§ 15-404 BOND FOR WITNESS.
   The court may also require a recognizance or bond of a witness in a case,
with or without surety, but in no event in an amount in excess of $100, for his
or her appearance at such time as the court may fix and to give evidence in the
case, the procedure whereon may be the same as is prescribed for bonds for
persons under arrest.
(Prior Code, § 15-404)
§ 15-405 APPEAL AND APPEAL BONDS.
   From any judgment of imprisonment or for a fine of more than $10 under this
code, or any other ordinance of the city, the person against whom it is
rendered may, within 20 days after the date thereof, appeal to a court of
competent jurisdiction in the county wherein the offense was committed upon
entering into a recognizance with surety deemed sufficient in a penalty double
the amount of the fine and costs with the condition that the party appealing
will appear before such court on the first day of the next term thereof to
answer for the offense against the city with which he or she stands charged,
and not thence depart without leave of such court and will perform and satisfy
any judgment which may be rendered against him or her by the court on appeal.
And in case a fine not exceeding $10 is assessed, the person against whom it is
assessed may object thereto, and insist upon the increase thereof to a certain
sum exceeding $10, and judgment shall be given for such increased sum, and an
appeal allowed, if one is desired, from such judgment.
(Prior Code, § 15-405)
ARTICLE 5: FINES, COURT COST, SENTENCING
Section
   
15-500   Costs and fees
   
15-501   Payment of fines and costs
   
15-502   Payment of fine may be made condition of probation or suspension of
sentence
   
15-503   Court may require defendant to be on good behavior until fine and
costs are paid
   
15-504   Procedure upon default in payment under agreement; confinement in case
of willful default
   
15-505   Community service work may be substituted in lieu of incarceration or
a fine in Municipal Court
   
15-506   Home incarceration for Municipal Court offenders
§ 15-500 COSTS AND FEES.
   (A)   Costs and fees in all cases, including violations of city ordinances,
shall be as prescribed by state law for the courts of magistrates, together
with all lawful jail fees, if any, attributable to the defendant.
   (B)   All charges brought before the Municipal Court will reflect, upon
conviction, all applicable costs, fines, fees, administrative costs,
prosecution fees, and incarnation fees due the state and municipality as
authorized by state law, Municipal Charter, or ordinance, and distributed to
the appropriate state or county agency, or general or appropriate fund of the
municipality.
   (C)   Any changes in the court costs mandated to be charged by Circuit,
Magistrate, and Municipal Courts by the legislature of the state are hereby
automatically adopted as they occur.
   (D)   All cases appearing in the Municipal Court of the city shall have an
administrative court cost payable to the city in the amount of $30. This shall
be in addition to and added to fines imposed upon criminal defendants.
   (E)   In the event that the driver’s license of any resident of this state,
or the driver’s privilege of a non-resident of the state to drive a motor
vehicle in this state, has been suspended pursuant to notification from the
Clerk of Municipal Court to the State Division of Motor Vehicles of default in
the payment of fines and/or costs, and such resident or non-resident seeks to
pay those delinquent fines and/or costs in order that a notice of satisfaction
may be given, an additional administrative court cost of $25 shall be added to
the previously due fine and/or costs which shall be paid at the time of payment
of the delinquent fines and/or cost, prior to any notification of satisfaction
being given. In addition, any fees due the Division of Motor Vehicles shall be
collected by the Division.
   (F)   In each criminal case before or in the Municipal Court of a
municipality in which the defendant is convicted, whether by plea or at trial,
under the provisions of a municipal ordinance which has the same elements as an
offense described in W. Va. Code §§ 17C-5-2 or 20-7-18b, there shall be
imposed, in addition to other costs, fines, forfeitures, or penalties as may be
allowed by law, costs in the amount of $55. The Clerk of each Municipal Court,
or other person designated to receive fines and costs, shall, for purposes of
further defraying the cost to the municipality of enforcing the provisions of
the ordinance or ordinances described in this section and related provisions,
deposit these monies in the General Revenue Fund of the municipality.
   (G)   If any jail sentence is imposed, all jail fees shall be added as part
of the fine.
   (H)   The Municipal Judge shall assess costs in the amount of $2.50 for
issuing a sheep warrant, appointment, and swearing appraisers and docketing the
same.
   (I)   In each criminal case which must be tried by the Circuit Court, but in
which the Municipal Judge renders some service, costs in the amount of $10
shall be imposed by Municipal Court and shall be certified to the Clerk of the
Circuit Court.
(Prior Code, § 15-500)
§ 15-501 PAYMENT OF FINES AND COSTS.
   (A)   The Municipal Court may accept credit cards in payment of all costs,
fines, forfeitures, or penalties. The Municipal Court may collect a substantial
portion of all costs, fines, forfeitures, or penalties at the time such amount
is imposed by the court so long as the court requires the balance to be paid
within 180 days, and in accordance with a payment plan which specifies:
      (1)   The number of additional payments to be made;
      (2)   The dates on which such payments and amounts shall be made; and
      (3)   Amounts due on such dates.
   (B)   If costs, fines, forfeitures, or penalties imposed by the Municipal
Court for violations are not paid within 180 days, or a person who committed
any such violation defaults on a payment plan as described in division (A)
above, or if a person fails to appear or otherwise respond in court when
charged, the Municipal Court shall notify the Commissioner of the Division of
Motor Vehicles of such failure to pay or failure to appear.
   (C)   The Municipal Court may issue execution or employ any means of
enforcing judgment to collect fines and costs imposed before the court
authorized by law to collect.
(Prior Code, § 15-501)
§ 15-502 PAYMENT OF FINE MAY BE MADE CONDITION OF PROBATION OR SUSPENSION OF
SENTENCE.
   If a defendant is sentenced to pay a fine and payment of the fine, or fine
and costs, is ordered to be made on an installment basis, or on other
conditions under the provisions of this section; and if the defendant is also
placed on probation or imposition of the execution of sentence is suspended,
the court may make payment of the fine a condition of probation or suspension
of sentence.
(Prior Code, § 15-502)
§ 15-503 COURT MAY REQUIRE DEFENDANT TO BE ON GOOD BEHAVIOR UNTIL FINE AND
COSTS ARE PAID.
   If a defendant is permitted to pay a fine, or fine and costs, on an
installment basis, or under such other conditions as the court shall fix under
the provisions of §
15-502, the court may require as a condition that the defendant be of peace and
good behavior until the fine and costs are paid.
(Prior Code, § 15-503)
§ 15-504 PROCEDURE UPON DEFAULT IN PAYMENT UNDER AGREEMENT; CONFINEMENT IN CASE
OF WILLFUL DEFAULT.
   (A)   The Division of Motor Vehicles shall suspend the license of any
resident of this state, or the privilege of a non-resident, to drive a motor
vehicle in this state upon receiving notice from the Municipal Court that such
person has defaulted on payment of costs, fines, forfeitures, or penalties,
which were imposed on the person by the Municipal Court upon conviction, after
180 days following such conviction, or that such person has failed to appear in
court when charged.
   (B)   When any person sentenced to pay a fine defaults in the payment of any
such fine or of any installment of the fine, the court may issue a summons for
such person to appear before the court for a hearing on the question of whether
such person’s failure to pay the fine or any installment was attributable to
intentional refusal to comply with the prior order of the court, or a lack of a
good-faith effort to comply with the order. The court may, after hearing, order
that the person in default be allowed additional time for payment, may reduce
or remit the amount of the fine or the unpaid portion in whole or in part, or
upon a finding that the default was intentional or due to the lack of a good-
faith effort to comply with the prior order of the court, may order such person
confined for such period up to 30 days as the court, in its discretion, shall
determine.
(Prior Code, § 15-504)
§ 15-505 COMMUNITY SERVICE WORK MAY BE SUBSTITUTED IN LIEU OF INCARCERATION OR
A FINE IN MUNICIPAL COURT.
   (A)   Notwithstanding any provision of this code to the contrary, the
Municipal Judge may substitute, in lieu of the imposition of a sentence of
incarceration or imposition of a fine, community service work for such
incarceration or fine. Where community service work is ordered as a substitute
for a sentence of incarceration, an eight-hour work day shall extinguish one
day of any sentence of incarceration. Where community service work is ordered
as a substitute for a fine, the prevailing federal minimum wage in effect at
the time of sentencing shall be used to compute the hours of community service
work necessary to extinguish the fine. In the discretion of the court, the
sentence credits may run concurrently or consecutively.
   (B)   If approved by the court, any community service ordered pursuant to
the provisions of this section shall be performed for the city.
   (C)   Persons sentenced under the provisions of this section remain under
the jurisdiction of the Municipal Court. The court may withdraw the community
service sentence at any time, with or without notice, and order a person
previously sentenced to community service to serve the term of incarceration or
to pay the fine available to the court upon the person’s conviction; provided,
that any community service work performed before the community service sentence
is withdrawn shall be credited against any term of incarceration or fine
imposed.
(Prior Code, § 15-505)
§ 15-506 HOME INCARCERATION FOR MUNICIPAL COURT OFFENDERS.
   Notwithstanding any provision of this article to the contrary, when a person
is convicted under a municipal ordinance for which a period of incarceration
may be imposed, the Municipal Court may enter an order for home incarceration
as an alternative sentence to incarceration in a county or regional jail;
provided, that home incarceration shall be available at the expense of the
person convicted, and only if accepted by the County Sheriff’s Department Home
Confinement Office. Any person accepted by the County Sheriff’s Department Home
Confinement Office the home is required to enter into an agreement for payment
of any related fees to the County Sheriff’s Department Home Confinement Office.
(Prior Code, § 15-506)
ARTICLE 6: JURIES
Section
   
15-600   Demand for jury trial
   
15-601   Persons eligible to jury service
   
15-602   Number of jurors
   
15-603   Master jury list
   
15-604   Preparation of jury list for trial
   
15-605   Penalty for failure of jurors to attend
   
15-606   Discharge of jurors; excuse from attendance
   
15-607   When juror not entitled to compensation
   
15-608   Payment of compensation
   
15-609   Trial procedure
   
15-610   Defendant responsible
§ 15-600 DEMAND FOR JURY TRIAL.
   Upon timely request by a defendant, the Municipal Court may hold a jury
trial. A demand by the defendant for a jury trial must be made, in writing, not
later than 20 days after the defendant’s initial appearance before the
Municipal Judge; provided, that in the case of an indigent for who counsel is
to be appointed, the 20-day period shall not commence to run until counsel is
appointed. Failure to demand within such time constitutes a waiver of the right
to a trial by jury; however, §
15-312 shall apply.
(Prior Code, § 15-600)
§ 15-601 PERSONS ELIGIBLE TO JURY SERVICE.
   (A)   All persons who are at least 18 years of age and who are residents of
the city shall be liable to serve as jurors, except as provided in this
article. Such jurors shall be of good character and free from felony crime
convictions. No juror shall be deemed incompetent because the city is a party
to the matter to be tried and the juror is a resident of such city.
   (B)   The Municipal Judge may, in his or her discretion, exempt or excuse
any person from jury service when it appears that such service would be
improper or work an undue hardship. A prospective juror 70 years of age or
older is not disqualified from serving, but shall be excused from service by
the court upon the juror’s request.
   (C)   Any prospective juror who has, within the preceding two years, been
summoned to serve as a petit juror, grand juror, magistrate juror, or municipal
juror, and has actually attended sessions of a Circuit, Magistrate, or
Municipal Court shall be disqualified to serve on a municipal jury.
(Prior Code, § 15-601)
§ 15-602 NUMBER OF JURORS.
   The jury shall be comprised of 12 jurors.
(Prior Code, § 15-602)
§ 15-603 MASTER JURY LIST.
   Jurors shall be selected from a list of registered city voters provided by
the City Recorder.
(Prior Code, § 15-603)
§ 15-604 PREPARATION OF JURY LIST FOR TRIAL.
   When a trial is scheduled in the Municipal Court, the Court Clerk shall, no
later than 15 days before the scheduled trial date: obtain a copy of the master
jury list from the City Recorder’s office; randomly select the number of jurors
required for the Municipal Court from the panel or pool of jurors available for
service; and contact or otherwise arrange for the jurors so selected to appear
at the specified date, time, and place of the Municipal Court trial. If, before
the trial date, it becomes known that the jury panel will not be needed, the
Municipal Court Clerk shall notify the scheduled jurors.
(Prior Code, § 15-604)
§ 15-605 PENALTY FOR FAILURE OF JURORS TO ATTEND.
   If any person duly summoned to attend as a juror shall neglect to attend,
without any sufficient excuse, he or she shall pay a fine not exceeding $50,
which shall be imposed by the Municipal Judge.
(Prior Code, § 15-605)
§ 15-606 DISCHARGE OF JURORS; EXCUSE FROM ATTENDANCE.
   The court, when not incompatible with the proper dispatch of its business,
shall have power to discharge persons summoned as jurors or dispense with their
attendance on any day of its sitting.
(Prior Code, § 15-606)
§ 15-607 WHEN JUROR NOT ENTITLED TO COMPENSATION.
   No juror who shall depart without leave of the Municipal Judge shall be
entitled to receive any compensation for his or her services as a juror.
(Prior Code, § 15-607)
§ 15-608 PAYMENT OF COMPENSATION.
   Such jurors shall be paid, inclusive of meal or travel cost within the city,
related to jury duty. It shall be the duty of the Municipal Court Clerk, as
soon as practicable after the adjournment of the court, or before the
adjournment of the court at such time as the court may direct, to deliver to
each juror a certified copy of any order making an allowance to him or her,
payable out of the City Treasury; and the Treasurer shall, upon demand, pay to
such juror the amount allowed to him or her.
(Prior Code, § 15-608)
§ 15-609 TRIAL PROCEDURE.
   Upon selection of a jury, as set forth in this chapter, the Municipal Court
Judge shall conduct a trial by jury consistent with the procedures set forth in
the “Rules of Criminal Procedure for West Virginia Magistrate Courts.”
(Prior Code, § 15-609)
§ 15-610 DEFENDANT RESPONSIBLE.
   Any time a trial by jury is granted by the Municipal Court Judge, the
defendant shall be responsible for the payment of the juror’s fees and cost of
service for each juror to the Clerk of the court for disbursement to each
juror. Also, the defendant shall pay the Clerk a sum of $200 for administrative
fees (mailings, notices, and costs associated) for the trial. These fees and
costs are passed to the defendant, only if the defendant is found guilty.
(Prior Code, § 15-610)
